bmps: Banca Monte dei Paschi di Siena (MPS) is an Italian bank based in Siena, founded in 1472 and considered the world's oldest bank still in operation. It offers retail, business and wealth-management banking across Italy; after a state rescue in 2017 it returned to strength and in 2025 took control of the investment bank Mediobanca.
bmri: Bank Mandiri is one of Indonesia's largest banks, state-owned and based in Jakarta. It was formed in 1998 by merging four state banks after the Asian financial crisis and serves large corporations, small businesses and retail customers, including through its Livin' app.
bmt: Bubblemaps is a blockchain data visualization tool that shows the links between wallets as 'bubbles'. It is used to spot token concentration and possible manipulation; BMT is the platform's token.
bmw: BMW is a German carmaker based in Munich, founded in 1916 as a maker of aircraft engines. It builds premium BMW cars and motorcycles and also owns the MINI and Rolls-Royce Motor Cars brands.
bmy: Bristol Myers Squibb is a US pharmaceutical company headquartered in Princeton, New Jersey. It develops medicines for cancer, blood disorders, immunology and cardiovascular disease, including Opdivo and Eliquis.
bn: Danone is a French food company from Paris whose roots go back to a yogurt factory opened in Barcelona in 1919. It makes dairy and plant-based products (Activia, Alpro), Evian and Volvic water, and baby and medical nutrition (Aptamil, Nutricia).
bn-ca: Brookfield Corporation is a Canadian investment company based in Toronto with roots going back to 1899. It owns and manages real estate, renewable power, infrastructure, private equity and insurance businesses worldwide, largely through its asset manager Brookfield Asset Management.
bnb: BNB is the coin of the BNB Chain ecosystem, launched in 2017 by the Binance exchange founded by Changpeng Zhao. It pays fees on BNB Smart Chain, gives trading-fee discounts on Binance and is used in DeFi and staking.
bnc4: Cea Industries (BNC4) is a tokenized version of shares in Cea Industries, a US company listed on Nasdaq that holds BNB as its treasury reserve. The token trades on BNB Chain and tracks the stock price; it is not the share itself.
bnd: Vanguard Total Bond Market (BND) covers the whole US investment-grade bond market in one fund: Treasuries, corporate bonds and mortgage-backed securities.
bnkr: BankrCoin (BNKR) is the official token of Bankr, an AI agent that buys and sells crypto through ordinary chat messages. Bankr is known for helping users of the Farcaster social network buy coins right in their feed.
bnp: BNP Paribas is France's largest bank and one of the biggest in the eurozone, formed in 2000 by the merger of BNP and Paribas. It runs retail networks in France, Belgium, Italy and Luxembourg, a large investment bank, insurance and asset management; in Ukraine it owns a stake in UkrSibbank.
bns: Scotiabank (Bank of Nova Scotia) is a Canadian bank based in Toronto, founded in 1832 in Halifax. Beyond Canada it has a strong presence in Latin America, including Mexico, Chile and Peru, and in the Caribbean.
bnt: Bancor is an ecosystem of decentralized protocols for on-chain trading and liquidity, launched in 2017. Bancor was one of the pioneers of automated market makers (AMMs), and its Carbon protocol lets users set up automatic trading strategies; BNT is used for governance.
bny: BNY (Bank of New York Mellon) is the oldest bank in the US, founded in 1784 by Alexander Hamilton and based in New York. It is the world's largest custodian bank, holding and servicing securities for institutional investors and managing client assets.
bob: BOB (Build on Bitcoin) is a hybrid layer-2 network that combines Bitcoin's security with Ethereum compatibility. It lets people use bitcoin in DeFi apps; BOB is the network token.
boba: Boba Network is a layer-2 network for Ethereum that makes transactions faster and cheaper using optimistic rollup technology. Its HybridCompute feature lets smart contracts call off-chain services and APIs, and BOBA is used for fees, staking and governance.
bobo: Bobo (BOBO) is an Ethereum memecoin launched in 2023 featuring Bobo, the bear character crypto traders use as a symbol of falling markets. It is a community token with no utility beyond trading.
bold: BOLD is the dollar stablecoin of Liquity V2, a decentralized lending protocol on Ethereum. Users mint BOLD by depositing ETH or liquid staking tokens as collateral and choose their own interest rate on the loan.
bome: BOOK OF MEME (BOME) is a meme token on Solana created in 2024 by the artist Darkfarms. It was conceived as a decentralized digital archive of memes stored on Arweave and IPFS, and became known for its rapid surge right after launch.
bone: BONE (Bone ShibaSwap) is the governance token of ShibaSwap, the decentralized exchange of the Shiba Inu ecosystem. It is also used to pay transaction fees on Shibarium, Shiba Inu's layer-2 network, and to vote on proposals.
bonk: Bonk is a dog-themed meme coin on Solana, launched on Christmas 2022 to cheer up the community after the FTX collapse. A large share of the tokens was given away free to Solana users and developers, and BONK is integrated into many apps on the network.
booe: Book of Ethereum (BOOE) is a meme coin on Ethereum inspired by the Solana meme coin Book of Meme (BOME). It has no product of its own: its value rests on community interest and trading.
bora: BORA is a blockchain platform for games and digital entertainment created by a South Korean company that belongs to the Kakao group. It distributes games and digital content and rewards participants with BORA tokens.
borg: SwissBorg is a crypto investment app from Lausanne, Switzerland, founded in 2017, where users buy, sell and exchange crypto, earn yield and use automated strategies. BORG is the app's token, giving holders better rewards and lower fees.
boson: Boson Protocol is a UK-founded decentralized commerce protocol that lets brands sell physical products on-chain as redeemable NFTs: the buyer holds a token that can be traded or exchanged for the real item, with funds held in escrow until delivery. BOSON is used for staking, fees and governance.
bounty: ChainBounty (BOUNTY), formerly Sentinel Protocol, is a blockchain-based security project that pools collective cybersecurity intelligence to protect crypto users from hackers, scams and fraud, for example through shared threat databases.
box: DeBox is a decentralized social app for crypto communities: users sign in with a wallet, chat in groups and join clubs that can be limited to holders of certain tokens or NFTs. BOX is the token at the center of the DeBox ecosystem.
bp: Backpack is a crypto exchange and wallet in one app, founded by Armani Ferrante's team, which previously built developer tools for Solana. The exchange offers spot and futures trading, and the wallet supports several blockchains; BP is the ecosystem token.
bpac11: BTG Pactual is Latin America's largest investment bank, headquartered in São Paulo and Rio de Janeiro. It offers investment banking, trading, asset and wealth management, and a digital bank for individual clients.
br: Broadridge Financial Solutions is a New York fintech company spun off from ADP in 2007. It sends shareholder reports and proxy voting materials on behalf of companies and funds, and provides brokers and banks with trade-processing software.
br-token: Bedrock (BR) is a liquid restaking protocol that issues liquid tokens such as uniBTC and uniETH for staked BTC, ETH and other assets. BR is the governance token: holders lock it as veBR to vote on protocol settings and on how rewards are split between liquidity pools.
brainon: Ondo AI Leaders Portfolio (BRAINon) is a tokenized portfolio from Ondo Finance that gives on-chain exposure to companies across the artificial intelligence value chain: chip and compute makers, AI infrastructure and energy. Weights follow a modified market-cap method.
brent: Brent is the world's main benchmark for crude oil, named after a North Sea field. Most of the oil traded globally is priced off Brent.
brett: Brett (BRETT) is a meme token on Coinbase's Base network, named after a character from Matt Furie's Boy's Club comic, a friend of Pepe the Frog. The community promotes it as «the Pepe of Base».
brev: Brevis is a ZK coprocessor that lets smart contracts read historical blockchain data and run complex computations off-chain, verified with zero-knowledge proofs. BREV is the network's token.
bridgestone: Bridgestone is a Japanese tire maker from Tokyo, founded in 1931 and one of the largest in the world. It makes tires for cars, trucks, aircraft and heavy machinery under the Bridgestone and Firestone brands, plus other rubber products.
brise: Bitgert (BRISE) began in 2021 as a token on BNB Chain and later launched its own blockchain, Bitgert Chain, which promotes near-zero gas fees and fast transactions. BRISE is the chain's native coin.
brk-b: Berkshire Hathaway is an American conglomerate from Omaha, Nebraska, led for decades by Warren Buffett. It owns the insurer GEICO, the BNSF railroad, energy companies and Duracell, and holds large stakes in Apple, Coca-Cola and American Express.
brl1: BRL1 is a stablecoin pegged to the Brazilian real, launched by a group of Brazilian crypto companies, including exchanges Mercado Bitcoin and Foxbit. Each token aims to equal one real and is backed by reserves.
brla: BRLA is a stablecoin pegged to the Brazilian real, issued by the Brazilian company BRLA Digital. Each token aims to equal one real and is backed by reserves, letting users make fast payments and conversions between reais and crypto on blockchains.
bro: Brown & Brown is one of the largest insurance brokers in the US, founded in 1939 in Florida. It finds property, liability, health and employee insurance for businesses and individuals and earns commissions from insurers.
broccoli: CZ's Dog (BROCCOLI) is a memecoin on BNB Chain named after Broccoli, the dog of Binance founder Changpeng Zhao. The token appeared in early 2025 after CZ talked about his dog on social media.
brz: Brazilian Digital Token (BRZ) is a stablecoin pegged to the Brazilian real, issued by Transfero. Each BRZ aims to equal one real and is backed by reserves; it circulates on several blockchains and is used for payments, trading and remittances in reais.
bsb: Block Street (BSB) is a decentralized finance infrastructure project whose BSB token is issued on several networks, including Ethereum, BNB Chain and Base. It builds on-chain tools for trading and lending.
bsv: Bitcoin SV (Satoshi Vision) is a cryptocurrency that split off from Bitcoin Cash in a 2018 hard fork. Its backers, including Craig Wright, pushed for very large blocks to scale, and the network positions itself as a platform for micropayments and enterprise data.
bsx: Boston Scientific is a US medical device maker based in Marlborough, Massachusetts, founded in 1979. It makes stents, catheters, pacemakers, cardiac ablation systems and devices for minimally invasive surgery.
btc: Bitcoin is the first cryptocurrency, launched in 2009 by the pseudonymous Satoshi Nakamoto. Its supply is capped at 21 million coins, which is why it is often called 'digital gold'.
btcmt: Minto is a Bitcoin-mining project whose BTCMT token is tied to the hashrate of its mining equipment. Holders stake the token to receive a share of the bitcoin that the hardware mines, without running machines themselves.
btcp: Bitcoin Pro (BTCP) is a separate cryptocurrency, not Bitcoin itself, that markets itself as a faster, cheaper and fully decentralized version of Bitcoin. It only borrows Bitcoin's name and idea; it has its own coin, network and much smaller community.
btr: Bitlayer is a Bitcoin layer-2 network and the first implementation of BitVM technology. It adds fast, EVM-compatible smart contracts on top of Bitcoin so DeFi apps can be built around BTC; BTR is the network's token.
bts: BitShares is one of the oldest blockchain platforms, launched in 2014 by Dan Larimer, who later co-created EOS and Steem. It runs a built-in decentralized exchange where users trade and issue their own tokens and collateral-backed smartcoins such as bitUSD, and it pioneered the delegated proof-of-stake model.
btse: BTSE Token is the utility token of BTSE, a cryptocurrency exchange founded in 2018 that offers spot and futures trading. Holding BTSE gives users trading-fee discounts and other benefits on the platform.
btw: BTW is the utility and governance token of the Bitway ecosystem, which offers yield, payments and financing services. The token is used for staking, voting and running the network, tying all Bitway products together.
bty: Bityuan (BTY) is a public blockchain from China built on the Chain33 technology of the Hangzhou company Fuzamei (33.cn). The network supports smart contracts and parallel chains for business applications and uses BTY for fees and mining.
bubi: Bullbit (BUBI) is a perpetual futures DEX that aims to feel like a centralized exchange: users sign in with e-mail or a passkey, pay no gas and keep custody of their funds. It runs on Base and plans to move to its own Layer 1, BullChain.
bulla: BULLA is a meme coin linked to Hasbulla, the popular internet personality from Dagestan. The project focuses on gamified quests, access to gated content and community campaigns to bring newcomers into crypto.
bun: Bundle Cat (BUN) is the first token launched on Mosh, a launch protocol by UV Labs on Robinhood Chain. In the Mosh model, crowd-funded token bundles are locked in smart-contract vaults and autonomous AI agents use them to provide liquidity under rules no one can override.
burn: BurnedFi (BURN) is a token on BNB Chain built around burning: users burn BURN tokens and receive BUILD tokens as proof, and each burn also mints extra BUILD that is shared among existing BUILD holders.
buttcoin: Buttcoin (BUTTCOIN) is a meme coin on Solana. Like most meme coins, it is not backed by a business or assets, and its price is driven mainly by community attention and trading.
bx: Blackstone is the world's largest alternative asset manager, founded in New York in 1985 by Stephen Schwarzman and Peter Peterson. It invests in private equity, real estate, credit and hedge funds on behalf of pension funds and other investors.
bxn: BlackFort (BXN) is an EVM-compatible Layer 1 blockchain that runs on a Proof-of-Staked-Authority consensus with short block times and low fees. The ecosystem aims to link decentralized finance, tokenized real-world assets and traditional financial services; BXN is its native coin.
byd: BYD is a Chinese maker of electric vehicles and batteries based in Shenzhen, founded in 1995 by Wang Chuanfu. Starting with phone batteries, it became one of the world's largest producers of electric and hybrid cars, buses and Blade batteries; Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway was an early investor.
byd-cn: BYD (A shares) are shares of Chinese electric car and battery maker BYD listed on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange. The company was founded in 1995 by Wang Chuanfu and today makes EVs and hybrids, buses, Blade batteries and electronics.
bzz: Swarm (BZZ) is the token of Swarm, a decentralized storage and communication network for the web that grew out of the Ethereum ecosystem. Node operators store and serve data; BZZ, which runs on Gnosis Chain, pays them for it.
c: Citigroup is one of the largest US banks, headquartered in New York, with a history dating back to 1812. Citi serves corporations, governments and individuals in nearly a hundred countries with payments, credit cards, investment banking and wealth management.
c-token: Chainbase is a Web3 data network that collects, indexes and structures on-chain data from many blockchains so developers and AI applications can query it through simple APIs. C is the token used to pay for data services and secure the network.
c98: Coin98 is a DeFi ecosystem from Vietnam, best known for its multi-chain Coin98 Wallet. It also includes a swap aggregator and a cross-chain bridge; the C98 token is used for governance and rewards.
ca: Coupon Assets (CA, also CA-HTB) is a platform token launched in March 2018 by RADAR LAB in the USA and issued on Ethereum. The project positions it as a digital asset linked to financial instruments such as bonds and promissory notes.
cabk: CaixaBank is Spain's largest bank by domestic customers, based in Valencia, and also owns Portugal's BPI. It grew out of La Caixa savings bank founded in Barcelona in 1904 and offers retail banking, mortgages, insurance and asset management.
cadd: CAD Digital (CADD) is a stablecoin pegged 1:1 to the Canadian dollar and issued by a regulated financial institution as a payments token. Each token can be redeemed for one Canadian dollar held in trust by Tetra Trust, a regulated Canadian trust company.
cah: Cardinal Health is a US healthcare company based in Dublin, Ohio. It distributes medicines to pharmacies and hospitals and makes and supplies medical products such as gloves, catheters and surgical kits.
cake: PancakeSwap is a decentralized exchange (DEX) launched in 2020 on BNB Chain, where it became the most popular one. Users swap tokens, provide liquidity, farm and play lotteries; CAKE is the reward and governance token.
canon: Canon is a Japanese maker of optics and imaging equipment from Tokyo, founded in 1937. It produces cameras and lenses, printers and copiers, medical imaging systems and equipment used to make computer chips.
cap: Cap is a covered-credit protocol on Ethereum built around the digital dollar cUSD, which is backed by dollar assets such as money market funds and regulated stablecoins. Reserves are lent to institutions to earn yield, and each loan is protected by a separate market of financial guarantees.
cap-fr: Capgemini is a French IT consulting and services group based in Paris, founded in 1967 by Serge Kampf. It helps large companies and governments with digital transformation, cloud, data, AI and engineering, and has a very large workforce in India.
cards: Collector Crypt is a platform that tokenizes physical trading cards, mainly Pokémon: the cards sit in a vault while the token holder owns them. Users can buy, sell or open digital card packs, and CARDS is the platform's token on Solana.
carr: Carrier Global is a US maker of air conditioning, heating and ventilation systems based in Florida. It was founded in 1915 by Willis Carrier, inventor of modern air conditioning, spun off from United Technologies in 2020, and its brands include Carrier, Viessmann and Toshiba Carrier.
cars: Rip Cars (CARS) is a crypto project on the Solana blockchain whose token was launched through the MetaDAO launchpad, where new projects raise funds under community-governed rules. CARS is the project's token.
carv: CARV is a modular data and identity layer for games and AI agents. It lets users own their data and earn rewards when it is used; CARV is used for staking, governance and payments in the network.
cashcat: Cash Cat (CASHCAT) is a meme coin. Like most meme coins, it is not backed by a business or assets, and its price is driven mainly by community attention and trading.
casy: Casey's General Stores is a US chain of convenience stores and fuel stations from Iowa, founded in 1968. It has thousands of locations in small Midwestern towns and is known for its own pizza made fresh in the stores.
cat: Caterpillar is the world's largest maker of construction and mining equipment, founded in 1925 and headquartered in Irving, Texas. It is known for yellow bulldozers, excavators and mining trucks and also builds diesel engines, gas turbines and locomotives.
cat-token: Simon's Cat (CAT) is an officially licensed memecoin based on Simon's Cat, the British animated series by Simon Tofield about a hungry, mischievous cat. The token runs on BNB Chain and links the brand's fan community to crypto.
cathay-financial: Cathay Financial Holding is a Taiwanese financial group from Taipei. It includes Cathay Life, Taiwan's largest life insurer, Cathay United Bank and companies in securities, property insurance and asset management.
cati: Catizen is a cat-themed social game in Telegram built on the TON blockchain. It makes it easier for millions of messenger users to get into Web3 and mobile payments, and CATI is the game ecosystem's token.
catl: CATL (Contemporary Amperex Technology) is a Chinese battery maker from Ningde in Fujian province, founded in 2011 by Robin Zeng. It is the world's biggest supplier of electric-vehicle batteries, serving carmakers such as Tesla, BMW and Volkswagen, and also makes energy-storage systems.
cattle: Live cattle is a futures contract that tracks the price of beef cattle in the United States. It depends on feed costs, herd size and demand for meat.
caw: CAW (A Hunter's Dream) is a community crypto project on Ethereum that originated from the address that deployed Shiba Inu. It aims to build a decentralised social network, a social clearing house, where CAW is spent on posting and other actions.
cb: Chubb is one of the world's largest property and casualty insurers, headquartered in Zurich, Switzerland. It insures businesses, individuals and farmers and also offers reinsurance, life and health insurance in dozens of countries.
cba: Commonwealth Bank of Australia is Australia's largest bank, based in Sydney and founded in 1911 as a state bank. It serves individuals and businesses, is known for its mobile banking app and also owns ASB Bank in New Zealand.
cbk: Commerzbank is one of Germany's largest banks, based in Frankfurt and founded in 1870 in Hamburg. It serves millions of retail customers and a large share of Germany's mid-sized companies and owns Poland's mBank.
cbk-token: Cobak (CBK) is the token of Cobak, a South Korean app that is one of the country's largest crypto communities. Users track the market, discuss coins and manage portfolios there, and CBK is used for rewards.
cboe: Cboe Global Markets is an American exchange operator based in Chicago. It runs the Chicago Board Options Exchange, founded in 1973 as the first exchange for listed stock options, and is known for the VIX volatility index — the market's fear gauge; it also operates stock, futures and FX trading venues in the US and Europe.
cbre: CBRE Group is the world's largest commercial real estate services and investment firm, based in Dallas, Texas. It helps companies lease and sell offices, warehouses and other properties, manages buildings and facilities for clients, invests money for others through CBRE Investment Management, and develops projects through Trammell Crow Company.
cbucks: Cartoon Money (CBUCKS) is a community entertainment token on Solana, built around a cartoon-style trading game called Coinmoonkitcap. The idea is a light, game-like space where beginners and traders can learn how crypto markets behave and have fun together.
cc: Canton Coin (CC) is the native token of Canton Network, a blockchain for banks and financial institutions built by the company Digital Asset. The network combines data privacy with the ability to exchange tokenised assets, and CC rewards developers, users and infrastructure operators for real activity.
ccd: Concordium (CCD) is a layer-1 blockchain founded in Switzerland by Danish entrepreneur Lars Seier Christensen, with identity verification built into the protocol. This combines privacy with regulatory compliance and can confirm that actions, including those of AI agents, were authorized by a real person.
ccep: Coca-Cola Europacific Partners is the world's largest Coca-Cola bottler by revenue, headquartered in London. It makes and distributes Coca-Cola drinks in Western Europe, Australia, New Zealand and Indonesia.
cci: Crown Castle is a US real estate investment trust (REIT) based in Houston, Texas, that owns and leases around 40,000 cell towers across the United States. Mobile carriers such as Verizon, AT&T and T-Mobile rent space on its towers for their antennas, which makes it a key part of the country's wireless infrastructure.
ccl: Carnival Corporation is the world's largest cruise company, based in Miami, Florida. It operates a fleet of around 90 ships under brands such as Carnival Cruise Line, Princess Cruises, Holland America Line, Costa, AIDA, P&O Cruises and Cunard, carrying millions of holidaymakers a year.
cco: Cameco is a Canadian company from Saskatoon and one of the world's largest uranium producers. It mines uranium in Saskatchewan and Kazakhstan, provides nuclear fuel processing services and owns a stake in Westinghouse.
cdns: Cadence Design Systems is a US software company based in San Jose, California, founded in 1988. Its electronic design automation (EDA) tools and chip IP are used by semiconductor and electronics makers to design and verify chips, circuit boards and systems.
cdw: CDW is an American IT products and services provider based in Illinois, founded in 1984. It sells laptops, servers, networking gear and software from thousands of brands to businesses, government agencies, schools and hospitals, and helps set them up, including cloud and security services.
ceek: CEEK Smart VR (CEEK) is the token of CEEK, a virtual reality platform where people watch concerts, sports and other live experiences in VR. Artists and creators can sell content and tickets, and CEEK is used for payments on the platform.
ceg: Constellation Energy is the largest producer of carbon-free electricity in the US, based in Baltimore and spun off from Exelon in 2022. It runs the country's biggest fleet of nuclear plants and sells power to homes and businesses, including data centers.
cell: Cellframe (CELL) is the coin of Cellframe, a service-oriented blockchain platform that uses post-quantum cryptography to stay secure against future quantum computers. It supports sharding and lets developers build their own chains and services; CELL pays fees and is staked.
celltrion: Celltrion is a South Korean biopharmaceutical company from Incheon, founded in 2002. It is one of the world leaders in biosimilars — cheaper versions of biologic drugs for autoimmune diseases and cancer, such as Remsima (infliximab).
celo: Celo (CELO) is a blockchain launched in 2020 for mobile payments that became a layer-2 network on Ethereum in 2025. It is known for cheap stablecoin transfers, especially for users in developing countries.
celr: Celer Network is a cross-chain interoperability protocol known for the cBridge bridge and its inter-chain messaging system. It lets users move assets and data between dozens of networks; CELR is used for staking and governance.
cent: Incentiv is an Ethereum-compatible layer-1 blockchain with built-in account abstraction, which makes wallets and fee payments simpler. The network shares revenue with users and developers for their activity, and CENT is its native token.
cere: Cere Network (CERE) is a decentralized data cloud built with Substrate, the Polkadot technology stack. It lets businesses and apps store, manage and share user data securely without a central provider; CERE pays for services and staking.
cess: CESS (Cumulus Encrypted Storage System) is a decentralized storage and content-delivery network built as its own layer-1 blockchain. People contribute storage space and earn CESS tokens, while apps store data in encrypted, distributed form.
cetus: Cetus is a decentralized exchange with concentrated liquidity on the Sui and Aptos networks. It lets users swap tokens and provide liquidity within chosen price ranges; CETUS is used for governance and rewards.
cf: CF Industries is a US maker of nitrogen fertilizers based in Northbrook, Illinois, founded in 1946 as a farm cooperative. It turns natural gas into ammonia, urea and UAN at large plants mainly in the US and Canada, and is developing low-carbon ammonia.
cfg: Citizens Financial Group is a US banking group from Providence, Rhode Island, with roots going back to 1828. It serves individuals and businesses in the Northeast and Midwest and became independent from Britain's RBS in 2015.
cfg-token: Centrifuge (CFG) is a protocol for tokenizing real-world assets such as loans, invoices and Treasury bonds, founded in Berlin in 2017. It gives investors access to these assets in DeFi, and CFG is the governance token.
cfr: Richemont is a Swiss luxury goods group based in Geneva, founded in 1988 by Johann Rupert. It owns the jewelry houses Cartier and Van Cleef & Arpels, the watch brands IWC, Jaeger-LeCoultre and Vacheron Constantin, and Montblanc.
cfx: Conflux is a public Layer 1 blockchain founded in China that uses a hybrid Tree-Graph consensus and is compatible with Ethereum apps (EVM). It is known for working with Chinese companies and public bodies; CFX pays network fees and is used for staking.
cgn: Cygnus (CGN) is a Web3 project that combines on-chain and off-chain assets into a real-yield layer and builds Instagram-style social apps for the creator economy, aiming to bring mainstream users to crypto.
cgo: Comtech Gold (CGO) is a gold-backed token on the XDC Network, where each token represents one gram of physical gold stored in a vault in Dubai. It lets people own and transfer gold digitally in small amounts.
cgpt: ChainGPT is an ecosystem of AI tools for Web3: a chatbot for crypto questions, a smart contract generator and auditor, an NFT generator and the ChainGPT Pad launchpad. The CGPT token unlocks access to services and is used for staking.
chd: Church & Dwight is a US maker of household and personal care products from New Jersey, founded in 1846. Its best-known brand is Arm & Hammer baking soda; it also makes Trojan condoms, First Response pregnancy tests and Vitafusion vitamins.
cheems: Cheems Token (CHEEMS) is a memecoin on BNB Chain inspired by the famous meme of a Shiba Inu dog named Cheems. It is a community token with no utility that exists thanks to the meme's popularity and its holders' enthusiasm.
chex: Chintai is a licensed and regulated tokenization platform for financial institutions, letting them issue and trade digital versions of real-world assets such as bonds, funds and real estate on its own blockchain. CHEX is the network's token.
chillguy: Just a chill guy (CHILLGUY) is a memecoin on Solana dedicated to the viral "Chill Guy" meme, a relaxed cartoon dog character that spread across TikTok in 2024. The token has no function beyond its community and the meme's popularity.
china-construction-bank: China Construction Bank is one of China's "Big Four" state-owned banks, headquartered in Beijing and founded in 1954. It offers corporate and retail banking and has historically specialised in financing infrastructure, construction and mortgages.
china-merchants-bank: China Merchants Bank is a Chinese commercial bank from Shenzhen, founded in 1987. It is regarded as a leader in China's retail banking, known for its credit cards, mobile app and wealth management for affluent clients.
china-mobile: China Mobile is China's state-owned telecom operator and the world's largest mobile carrier by number of subscribers. It provides mobile service, home broadband, cloud and enterprise services; the company was created in 1997.
china-shenhua-energy: China Shenhua Energy is China's largest coal company and a subsidiary of state-owned China Energy Investment. It runs an integrated model: it mines coal, moves it on its own railways and through its ports, and burns it to generate electricity at its own power plants.
china-yangtze-power: China Yangtze Power is China's largest hydropower company, a subsidiary of the state-owned China Three Gorges. It operates the Three Gorges Dam, the world's most powerful power station, and other large plants on the Yangtze: Xiluodu, Xiangjiaba and Baihetan.
chr: Chromia is a layer-1 blockchain with a built-in relational database, created by the Swedish company ChromaWay. It suits games and data-heavy apps; CHR is used to pay for hosting and for staking.
chtr: Charter Communications is one of the largest cable internet and TV providers in the US, operating under the Spectrum brand. The Connecticut-based company also sells Spectrum Mobile phone service; John Malone's Liberty Broadband is a major shareholder.
chugai-pharmaceutical: Chugai Pharmaceutical is a Japanese drug maker based in Tokyo, founded in 1925 and controlled by Switzerland's Roche since 2002. It develops medicines for cancer, immune diseases and haemophilia, including antibody drugs such as Actemra and Hemlibra.
chunghwa-telecom: Chunghwa Telecom is Taiwan's largest telecommunications company, based in Taipei and created in 1996 from the former state telecom administration. It provides mobile, fixed-line and fiber broadband services, the HiNet internet service and MOD IPTV, as well as data-center, cloud and enterprise network services.
chunkee: Chunkee The Manatee (CHUNKEE) is a community meme token on Ethereum built around Chunkee, a cartoon manatee character. It focuses on memes and fan art and has no other stated utility; it is not affiliated with any game or brand.
chz: Chiliz (CHZ) is a Malta-based sports blockchain that powers the Socios.com app. Clubs such as Barcelona, PSG and Juventus issue fan tokens on it that let supporters vote in club polls and get perks; CHZ is the currency of this ecosystem.
ci: The Cigna Group is a US health insurer based in Bloomfield, Connecticut. It sells medical coverage to employers and, through its Evernorth unit, runs the Express Scripts pharmacy benefits business and specialty pharmacies.
cien: Ciena is an American networking company based in Hanover, Maryland, founded in 1992. It makes optical networking equipment and software — including its WaveLogic high-speed optics — that telecom operators, cloud companies and governments use to send huge amounts of data over fiber-optic cables, including between AI data centers.
cinf: Cincinnati Financial is an American insurer from Ohio, founded in 1950. It sells property and casualty insurance to businesses and individuals through independent agents and is known for raising its dividend for decades in a row.
citic-securities: CITIC Securities is China's largest brokerage and investment bank, founded in 1995 and linked to the state-owned CITIC Group. It provides brokerage services, underwrites stock and bond offerings, manages assets and trades securities.
city: Manchester City Fan Token (CITY) is the official fan token of Manchester City, the English football club, launched through Socios.com on the Chiliz Chain. Holders vote in club polls and can win rewards and fan experiences.
ck-asset: CK Asset Holdings is a Hong Kong property company and part of Li Ka-shing's family business empire. It builds and rents out homes, offices and hotels in Hong Kong, mainland China and the UK, and owns the British pub chain Greene King.
ck-hutchison: CK Hutchison is a Hong Kong conglomerate linked to the family of billionaire Li Ka-shing. It owns ports in many countries, the A.S. Watson health and beauty chains (including Superdrug), Three mobile operators and infrastructure assets.
ckb: Nervos Network (CKB) is a layered blockchain network launched in 2019 by a Chinese team. Its layer 1, the Common Knowledge Base, acts as a secure foundation for storing value, while fast transactions move to layer 2. CKB pays for storage space on the chain and is mined.
cl: Colgate-Palmolive is a US consumer goods company based in New York, founded in 1806 by William Colgate. It sells Colgate toothpaste and toothbrushes, Palmolive soap, household cleaners and Hill's pet food in more than 200 countries.
clanker: Clanker is an AI bot on the Farcaster social network that launches new ERC-20 tokens on Base when users tag it in a post. CLANKER is the project's own token; the Clanker platform was acquired by Farcaster's team in 2025.
clash: GeorgePlaysClashRoyale (CLASH) is a meme coin on Solana named after a streamer who plays the mobile game Clash Royale. It is a community and entertainment token with no built-in utility and is not affiliated with the game's developer, Supercell.
claudia: Claudia (CLAUDIA) is the Solana token of a platform built around Claudia, an AI influencer character that posts about the memecoin market on X and TikTok. The platform also offers a memecoin trading terminal and developer tools for building AI agents.
claw: CLAW is the token of clawpump.tech, a service on Solana that lets AI agents launch their own tokens on pump.fun without paying network fees. The platform sponsors token creation, collects trading fees and shares most of the revenue with the agents.
clear: Clearpool (CLEAR) is a DeFi credit marketplace where lenders deposit stablecoins into on-chain vaults that fund vetted institutional borrowers such as trading firms and fintechs. Each vault has a risk curator who checks borrowers and monitors repayments; Ripple has backed its expansion to the XRP Ledger.
clnx: Cellnex is a Spanish company based in Barcelona and Europe's largest independent operator of telecom towers, spun off from Abertis in 2015. It owns tens of thousands of towers and masts across Europe and rents space on them to mobile operators.
clo: Clovis Network is a cross-chain clearing, execution and settlement layer that brings together fragmented DeFi liquidity. A global clearing layer works with lightweight vaults on connected blockchains; CLO is the network's token.
clp-holdings: CLP Holdings is a Hong Kong power company founded in 1901 as China Light & Power. It supplies electricity to most of Hong Kong (Kowloon and the New Territories) and owns power plants and grids in Australia (EnergyAustralia), India and mainland China.
cm: CIBC (Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce) is one of Canada's five largest banks, headquartered in Toronto. It serves individuals, businesses and wealthy clients in Canada, the US and the Caribbean.
cmc20: CoinMarketCap 20 Index DTF (CMC20) is an on-chain index token that tracks the 20 largest cryptocurrencies by market value, excluding stablecoins. It was launched by CoinMarketCap on BNB Chain as a decentralized token folio, so one token gives exposure to the whole basket.
cmcsa: Comcast is a US media and telecom company based in Philadelphia. It sells home internet, TV and mobile service under the Xfinity brand, owns NBCUniversal with the NBC network, Universal Pictures and Universal theme parks, and runs Sky in Europe.
cme: CME Group is the world's largest operator of futures exchanges, headquartered in Chicago. It owns the CME, CBOT, NYMEX and COMEX exchanges, where futures and options on interest rates, indices, currencies, oil, gold and bitcoin are traded.
cmg: Chipotle Mexican Grill is a US fast-casual Mexican restaurant chain from Newport Beach, California, founded in 1993 by Steve Ells in Denver. It sells burritos, bowls, tacos and salads assembled in front of the customer.
cmi: Cummins is a US engine maker based in Columbus, Indiana, founded in 1919. It builds diesel and natural gas engines for trucks, buses and machinery, power generators, and, under the Accelera brand, hydrogen and electric powertrains.
cms: CMS Energy is an energy company from Jackson, Michigan, whose main subsidiary Consumers Energy supplies electricity and natural gas to millions of people in Michigan. The company is gradually replacing coal plants with gas and renewable energy.
cnc: Centene is an American health insurer from St. Louis. It focuses on government programs: it serves Medicaid and Medicare members and sells plans on the Affordable Care Act (Obamacare) health insurance marketplaces.
cngn: cNGN (Compliant Naira) is a stablecoin pegged to the Nigerian naira, designed so that one token equals one naira and backed by reserves. It lets people and businesses use Nigeria's currency on blockchains for payments and transfers.
cnh: CNH Industrial is an international maker of farm and construction machinery, formed in 2013 from Fiat Industrial and CNH Global. It owns the tractor and combine brands Case IH, New Holland and Steyr, as well as CASE construction equipment.
cnooc: CNOOC is a Chinese state-owned oil and gas company based in Beijing and the largest producer of offshore oil and gas in China. It explores and produces in the Bohai Sea and the South China Sea, as well as abroad, including in Guyana.
cnp: CenterPoint Energy is a Houston-based utility that delivers electricity and natural gas to millions of customers in Texas, Indiana, Ohio and Minnesota. Its power grid serves the Greater Houston area.
cnpy: Canopy (CNPY) is Web3 infrastructure for developers who build apps quickly with AI. It lets them launch their own application blockchains and upgrade them without a painful migration of smart contracts; CNPY is the network token.
cnq: Canadian Natural Resources is a Canadian oil and gas producer from Calgary. It extracts oil and gas in Western Canada, including from the Alberta oil sands, and also has assets in the North Sea and offshore Africa.
cnr: Canadian National Railway (CN) is Canada's largest railway company, based in Montreal and founded in 1919. Its network runs from the Atlantic to the Pacific coast and south through the US Midwest to the Gulf of Mexico, carrying grain, oil, containers and other freight.
coai: ChainOpera AI (COAI) is a platform for jointly building AI agents that are governed and owned by the community. It combines a «super AI» app with infrastructure for developers; the COAI token is used for incentives and governance.
coalindia: Coal India is the world's largest coal miner by output, controlled by the Indian government and headquartered in Kolkata. Through its subsidiaries it mines coal in underground and open-pit mines and supplies it mainly to power stations.
coco: COCO is a memecoin with no specific technical function, built around the image of a 'discovered' meme that keeps moving forward without stopping. Its value rests on its community and internet culture rather than on a product or revenue.
cocoa: Cocoa is the raw material for chocolate. Côte d'Ivoire and Ghana grow more than half of the world's crop, so tree diseases and weather there move the price strongly.
cod: CloudBank (COD) is the token of a community-run DeFi super app on BNB Chain. It combines prediction markets, a project launchpad, a decentralized exchange, AI quant tools and payments, using shared global and community liquidity pools.
codec: Codec Flow (CODEC) is a Solana-based project building infrastructure for AI 'operators' — agents that can see a screen and control desktops, apps and robots, running in secure virtual environments.
cof: Capital One is a US financial company based in Virginia, founded in 1994 and one of the largest credit card issuers in the United States. It also offers bank accounts and auto loans, and in 2025 it acquired the Discover payment network.
coffee: Coffee is one of the most traded agricultural commodities. The benchmark contract is arabica, and prices depend on harvests and weather in Brazil, Vietnam and Colombia.
cohr: Coherent Corp. is an American maker of optical and laser technology based in Saxonburg, Pennsylvania, formerly known as II-VI; it took the Coherent name after buying the laser company Coherent in 2022. It sells optical transceivers that connect servers in AI data centers, industrial lasers and engineered materials such as silicon carbide.
coin: Coinbase is the largest US crypto exchange, founded in 2012 by Brian Armstrong and Fred Ehrsam. It lets people buy, store and sell cryptocurrencies, serves institutional investors, is the custodian for many bitcoin ETFs and develops the Base network.
coin-token: This is a Robinhood stock token that tracks Coinbase shares, offered by Robinhood to eligible customers in Europe as a blockchain-based token. Coinbase, founded in 2012 in San Francisco, runs the largest US crypto exchange, a custody business for institutions and its own Ethereum layer-2 network, Base.
coindepo: COINDEPO is a platform that combines interest-bearing deposit accounts for crypto assets with instant crypto loans. The COINDEPO token gives higher rates and discounts within the service; like any yield service, it carries platform risk.
col: Coles Group is one of Australia's two largest supermarket chains, based in Melbourne and founded in 1914. It runs Coles supermarkets and online grocery delivery, Liquorland liquor stores and the flybuys loyalty program.
collect: Collect on Fanable is the token of Fanable, a marketplace for physical collectibles, above all Pokémon and other trading cards. Real cards are kept in a secure vault, and owners trade digital rights to them without posting anything.
comp: Compound is one of the first decentralized lending protocols on Ethereum, launched in 2018 by Robert Leshner's team. Users earn interest on deposited crypto or borrow against collateral; COMP is the governance token, and its 2020 distribution helped spark the DeFi boom.
conx: CONX is a Layer 1 blockchain for 'cultural fintech' that links culture, finance and technology: it lets institutions and creators tokenize real-world assets, intellectual property and AI-generated content and trade them on-chain through its CONX Pulse platform.
cook: mETH Protocol (COOK) is the governance token of mETH Protocol, the liquid staking and restaking protocol of the Mantle ecosystem. Users stake ETH to get mETH, a liquid staking token, and can restake it as cmETH for extra rewards.
cookie: Cookie DAO is a data platform for AI agents in crypto that created the cookie.fun index, which ranks agents by activity and mentions. It also provides data for developers and traders; COOKIE is the ecosystem token.
cop: ConocoPhillips is one of the largest independent US oil and gas companies, based in Houston and focused on exploration and production. It produces crude oil, natural gas and liquefied natural gas in the United States, Canada, Norway, Australia and other countries.
copper: Copper is the key metal of electrification: wires, electric motors, EVs, power grids and data centres all need it. Its price is often seen as a gauge of the global economy.
coq: Coq Inu (COQ) is a meme coin on Avalanche. Like most meme coins, it is not backed by a business or assets, and its price is driven mainly by community attention and trading.
cor: Cencora (AmerisourceBergen until 2023) is a US drug distributor based in Conshohocken, Pennsylvania. It delivers medicines from manufacturers to pharmacies, hospitals and clinics in the US and other countries and provides services to pharmaceutical companies.
core: Core is an EVM-compatible layer-1 blockchain secured by bitcoin through its Satoshi Plus consensus, in which Bitcoin miners and CORE stakers jointly elect validators. BTC holders can stake bitcoin on Core without handing it to a third party.
corgiai: CorgiAI (CORGIAI) is a community-driven memecoin with a corgi theme on the Cronos chain, where it presents itself as the first project to build with AI. It plans AI image-generation and chatbot features alongside yield on its platform.
corn: Corn (maize) is the world's biggest grain crop by volume: livestock feed, food ingredient and ethanol biofuel. The United States is the top producer.
cost: Costco is an American chain of membership-only warehouse stores headquartered in Issaquah, Washington, founded in 1983. It sells groceries, household goods and electronics in bulk at low prices and is known for its own brand, Kirkland Signature.
coti: COTI is an Ethereum-based network that brings data privacy to a public blockchain using the Garbled Circuits cryptographic protocol. It lets smart contracts process encrypted data; the COTI token pays fees and is used for staking.
cotton: Cotton is the main natural fibre for clothing and textiles. The biggest producers are China, India, the United States and Brazil.
cow: CoW Protocol (COW) is a DeFi token-swap protocol on Ethereum and other chains that grew out of Gnosis. It batches orders, matches opposite trades directly and protects users from MEV attacks; COW is used for governance via CowDAO.
cp: Canadian Pacific Kansas City (CPKC) is a freight railway company based in Calgary, formed in 2023 by the merger of Canadian Pacific and Kansas City Southern. It is the first railway to link Canada, the United States and Mexico in a single network, hauling grain, coal, containers and other goods.
cp-token: Cluster Protocol is a platform for autonomous AI agents on the Base network: in one place they can run hundreds of AI models, use tokenised datasets and rent GPU compute, paying for each step automatically. CP is the network's native token.
cpay: Corpay (formerly Fleetcor) is an American payments company from Atlanta. It helps businesses pay supplier bills and make cross-border payments, issues fuel cards for vehicle fleets and handles lodging payments for traveling employees.
cprt: Copart is an American company from Texas, founded in 1982, that runs online auctions of used and damaged vehicles. Insurers, banks and dealers sell cars after accidents through it, and buyers worldwide purchase them for parts or repair.
crabai: Claude Crab (CRABAI) is a meme token on BNB Chain built around a pixel-art crab character and a story about an AI that escaped the data center and settled by the ocean. It is a standard BEP-20 token focused on branding and community content.
crcl: This is a Robinhood stock token that tracks shares of Circle Internet Group, the US company that issues the USDC stablecoin. Robinhood launched such tokens in 2025 for customers in the European Union, letting them get US stock exposure on-chain around the clock.
cred: Credible Finance (CRED) is a payments-focused crypto project on the Solana blockchain. It builds services for moving money with stablecoins and digital assets, and CRED is the project's token.
crh: CRH is an international building materials company founded in Ireland in 1970, with its main share listing in the US. It is North America's largest supplier of aggregates, asphalt, concrete and building products for roads and construction.
crl: Charles River Laboratories is a US company from Wilmington, Massachusetts, founded in 1947. It helps drugmakers develop new medicines by supplying research models and running preclinical safety testing and lab services.
crm: Salesforce is a US company from San Francisco, founded in 1999 by Marc Benioff and a pioneer of cloud software. It leads the market for CRM systems used for sales, customer service and marketing, and also owns Slack and Tableau.
cro: Cronos is an Ethereum-compatible (EVM) blockchain built on the Cosmos SDK and closely tied to the Crypto.com platform. CRO pays network fees and unlocks perks in the Crypto.com app and on its cards.
cronus: CRONUS is the community token of cro.trade, a trading app for the Cronos blockchain that combines spot trading, a token launchpad, perpetual futures and prediction markets, plus a Telegram trading bot. Supply is fixed, and platform revenue is used to buy back and burn CRONUS.
crts: Cratos (CRTS) is a vote-to-earn (V2E) cryptocurrency used in the Cratos mobile app, where people vote in real time on everyday and current-events questions and earn token rewards for taking part.
crv: Curve Finance is a decentralized exchange launched in 2020 by Michael Egorov that specializes in swapping assets with similar prices, such as stablecoins, with minimal slippage. CRV is the governance and reward token for liquidity providers.
crwd: CrowdStrike is an American cybersecurity company based in Austin, Texas, founded in 2011 by George Kurtz. Its cloud platform Falcon protects companies' computers, servers and cloud systems from hackers; a faulty update in July 2024 caused a worldwide Windows outage.
crwv: CoreWeave is an American cloud company from New Jersey specializing in computing power for artificial intelligence. It rents out clusters of NVIDIA GPUs to AI developers, with customers including Microsoft and OpenAI; its shares have traded since 2025.
crx: NUMA-X (CRX) is the utility token of NUMA-X Solutions, a Web3 ecosystem that combines a wallet, an exchange, a payment service and an online commerce platform. CRX is used for fees, payments, staking, governance and rewards across these services.
cs: AXA is a French insurance group based in Paris and one of the largest insurers in the world. It sells life, health, property and liability insurance to people and businesses in Europe, Asia and other regions; its AXA XL unit covers large commercial risks.
csco: Cisco is an American company from San Jose, California, founded in 1984 and one of the world's largest makers of networking equipment. It sells routers, switches and cybersecurity products, runs the Webex video platform and bought the data analytics firm Splunk in 2024.
csl: CSL is an Australian biotech company based in Melbourne, founded in 1916 as a government laboratory. It makes plasma-derived medicines (CSL Behring), flu vaccines (CSL Seqirus) and kidney medicines (CSL Vifor).
cspr: Casper Network (CSPR) is a Proof of Stake layer-1 blockchain launched in March 2021. It targets businesses and the tokenization of real-world assets and supports upgradeable smart contracts; CSPR is used for fees and staking.
csu: Constellation Software is a Canadian company from Toronto, founded in 1995 by Mark Leonard. It buys and grows hundreds of small developers of specialized software for particular industries and government agencies.
csx: CSX is one of the largest US railroads, based in Jacksonville, Florida. It hauls freight such as coal, chemicals, cars and containers over a rail network in the eastern United States and Canada.
ct: Concrete is a DeFi protocol with automated vaults that place users' crypto assets into yield strategies. It makes DeFi yield easier to access for both ordinary and institutional investors; CT is the protocol's token.
ctas: Cintas is a US business services company based in Cincinnati, Ohio. It rents and cleans work uniforms, supplies mats, restroom and cleaning products, first-aid kits and fire safety services to millions of businesses in North America.
ctbc-financial: CTBC Financial Holding is a Taiwanese financial group from Taipei that includes CTBC Bank (formerly Chinatrust), one of the island's largest private banks, and the insurer Taiwan Life. It is known for credit cards and has a presence in Japan, the US and Southeast Asia.
ctc: Creditcoin (CTC) is a blockchain built to record credit histories and loans, especially in emerging markets. It is developed by the South Korean team Gluwa; the CTC token is used for fees and staking on the network.
ctk: Shentu (formerly CertiK Chain) is a Cosmos-based blockchain created by the security firm CertiK. It focuses on smart contract security and has ShentuShield, a decentralized fund that reimburses hack victims; CTK is the native token.
ctm: CTM is the token of c8ntinuum, a multichain protocol that presents itself as a Layer 0 network. It aims to connect different blockchains and let them interoperate securely, using zero-knowledge light clients.
ctr: Citrea is the first ZK rollup that settles directly on Bitcoin, verifying zero-knowledge proofs through BitVM. It adds full smart contracts to Bitcoin via its own zkEVM while keeping Bitcoin-level security.
ctsh: Cognizant is a US IT consulting company from New Jersey, with most of its staff in India. It builds and maintains software, moves systems to the cloud and rolls out AI for banks, insurers, healthcare and industrial companies.
ctsi: Cartesi is rollup infrastructure that lets smart contracts run on ordinary Linux and be written in popular programming languages. Developers can use familiar libraries and tools beyond the limits of the EVM; CTSI is used for staking and running the network.
cult: Milady Cult Coin (CULT) is a meme coin on Ethereum tied to the Milady Maker NFT collection and the Remilia art collective behind it. It is a culture token for the Milady community rather than a product with built-in utility.
cvc: Civic is a digital identity project from San Francisco, founded in 2015 by Vinny Lingham. It lets people verify their identity and age online without handing over personal data again and again; CVC is used in the Civic ecosystem.
cve: Cenovus Energy is a Canadian oil company from Calgary. It produces oil from Alberta's oil sands using steam injection and also owns refineries in Canada and the United States.
cvna: Carvana is a US online platform from Tempe, Arizona, for buying and selling used cars, founded in 2012 by Ernie Garcia III. Known for its car vending machine towers, it lets buyers choose, finance and get a car delivered to their door.
cvs: CVS Health is a US healthcare company based in Woonsocket, Rhode Island. It owns thousands of CVS Pharmacy stores, the insurer Aetna and the pharmacy benefit manager Caremark, so it sells medicines, insures patients and provides care.
cvx: Chevron is one of the largest US oil and gas companies, headquartered in Houston, Texas, with roots going back to 1879 and Standard Oil. It produces oil and gas, refines them at its own plants and sells fuel under the Chevron, Texaco and Caltex brands.
cvx-token: Convex Finance (CVX) is a DeFi protocol on Ethereum built on top of Curve, the stablecoin exchange. It lets Curve liquidity providers earn boosted rewards without locking CRV tokens themselves; CVX holders influence how those rewards are distributed.
cw: Curtiss-Wright is a US engineering company from Davidson, North Carolina, created in 1929 from the merger of the Curtiss and Wright aviation firms. It makes high-tech components for defense, aerospace and commercial nuclear power, such as electronics, valves, actuators and reactor coolant pumps.
cxo: CargoX is a Slovenian company from Ljubljana that uses blockchain to send trade documents such as electronic bills of lading, invoices and certificates instantly between shippers, banks and customs. CXO is the token used on its document-transfer platform.
cyber: Cyber (formerly CyberConnect) is an Ethereum layer-2 built for social apps and Web3 identity, where users own their profile and connections. CYBER is used for gas, staking and governance.
cyc: Cycle Network (CYC) is the token of an infrastructure protocol that provides a shared settlement layer for digital assets and dApps across many blockchains, aiming to keep balances and app state consistent between chains. It was incubated by YZi Labs.
cys: Cysic is a network that speeds up zero-knowledge (ZK) proofs and other heavy computing using specialized hardware such as GPUs and custom ZK chips. Blockchains and apps buy proving power from it, and the CYS token pays for and rewards that compute.
d: Dominion Energy is a US energy company based in Richmond, Virginia. It supplies electricity and gas to millions of customers in Virginia and the Carolinas, including power for the world's largest cluster of data centres in Northern Virginia.
daddy: Daddy Tate (DADDY) is a memecoin on Solana launched in 2024 and associated with internet personality Andrew Tate. Like most memecoins, it has no business or assets behind it, and its price depends mainly on attention and trading.
dag: Constellation (DAG) is a network built on a directed acyclic graph (DAG) instead of a classic chain of blocks, so it can scale as more nodes join. The project focuses on validating and moving large volumes of data, including for government and enterprise clients.
dai: Dai (DAI) is a decentralized stablecoin pegged to the US dollar, launched in 2017 by MakerDAO (now Sky). Users mint DAI by locking more crypto than they borrow in smart contracts, so no bank holds the reserves; it is widely used in Ethereum DeFi.
daiichi-sankyo: Daiichi Sankyo is a Japanese pharmaceutical company from Tokyo, formed in 2005 by the merger of Daiichi and Sankyo. It is known for antibody-drug conjugate cancer medicines, especially Enhertu, which it develops with AstraZeneca.
daikin: Daikin Industries is a Japanese company based in Osaka, founded in 1924, and the world's largest maker of air conditioners. It produces air conditioning and heat-pump systems for homes, offices and factories, commercial refrigeration and refrigerant chemicals, and sells them in more than 170 countries.
dal: Delta Air Lines is one of the world's largest airlines, headquartered at its main hub in Atlanta, Georgia, and founded in 1925. It flies passengers and cargo across the US and to hundreds of cities worldwide, belongs to SkyTeam and even owns an oil refinery.
dao: DAO Maker is a crypto launchpad and incubator that helps early-stage blockchain startups raise money and find users. Through its token sales, ordinary investors can get allocations in new projects; the DAO token is used for staking and access to these sales.
dash: DoorDash is a US food and grocery delivery platform based in San Francisco, founded in 2013 by Stanford students. Its app connects restaurants and shops with customers and couriers; it also owns Wolt in Europe and has become the largest food delivery service in the United States.
dash-token: Dash is a cryptocurrency for fast, cheap payments, launched in 2014 by Evan Duffield (first as XCoin, then Darkcoin). Its network uses masternodes for instant InstantSend transfers and its own funding and governance system.
data: Data Network (DATA) is a layer-1 blockchain built to register intellectual property rights for data used in AI. It lets owners record rights to datasets on-chain and earn from them, and the DATA token is used inside the network.
db1: Deutsche Börse is a German exchange group based in Frankfurt. It runs the Frankfurt Stock Exchange and the Xetra trading system, the Eurex derivatives exchange and the Clearstream depository, and calculates the DAX and STOXX indices.
dbk: Deutsche Bank is Germany's largest bank, based in Frankfurt and founded in 1870. It does investment banking, serves corporations and private customers (including through Postbank) and manages assets through DWS.
dbr: deBridge (DBR) is a cross-chain protocol for moving assets and data quickly between blockchains, including Solana and EVM networks, without its own liquidity pools. Its DLN service executes swaps between networks in seconds; DBR is used for governance and rewards.
dcr: Decred is a cryptocurrency launched in 2016 with hybrid consensus: miners create blocks (Proof of Work), while DCR holders who stake their coins validate them and vote on changes. This way the community itself governs the network, and part of new issuance funds its development.
dcty: DacityCoin (DCTY) is a community token on the Solana blockchain that was launched through Pump.fun, the popular platform for creating new Solana tokens. Its price depends mainly on community interest.
dd: DuPont is a US materials company based in Wilmington, Delaware, founded in 1802 by Éleuthère Irénée du Pont as a gunpowder maker. Today it makes specialty materials such as Tyvek, water-filtration and purification systems, and components for healthcare and construction.
ddog: Datadog is a US company based in New York, founded in 2010, that makes a cloud monitoring service. It collects metrics, logs and traces from servers and applications so engineers can see outages and security threats in one place.
de: Deere & Company is a US maker of agricultural and construction machinery based in Illinois, founded in 1837 by John Deere. It is known for its green John Deere tractors and combines and for precision-farming technology.
debit: Teller (DEBIT) is a decentralized lending and borrowing project on BNB Chain. Users can lend crypto to earn interest or take loans against their assets, and DEBIT is the project's token.
deep: DeepBook (DEEP) is the native decentralized order book of the Sui network, launched in July 2023 with support from Mysten Labs and the Sui Foundation. Exchanges and DeFi apps on Sui use it for trading, and the DEEP token gives fee discounts and voting rights.
degen: Degen (DEGEN) is a community token of the Base network that appeared in 2024 among users of the Farcaster social network. It is used to tip content creators and active members, and the project later launched its own Degen Chain.
dell: Dell Technologies is an American computer maker based in Round Rock, Texas, founded in 1984 by Michael Dell in his college dorm room. It sells Dell, XPS and Alienware laptops and PCs as well as servers, data storage and infrastructure for AI data centers.
delta: Delta Electronics (Thailand) is the Thai subsidiary of Taiwan's Delta Electronics, with factories in Samut Prakan province. It makes power supplies, electric-vehicle components and power equipment for data centres, mostly for export.
delta-electronics: Delta Electronics is a Taiwanese electronics maker based in Taipei, founded by Bruce Cheng in 1971. It is a world leader in power supplies and cooling fans and also builds data-centre power systems, EV chargers and industrial automation.
denso: Denso is a Japanese auto parts maker from Kariya, founded in 1949 as a spin-off from Toyota. It makes air conditioning systems, electronics, sensors, spark plugs and components for hybrid and electric cars for carmakers worldwide.
dent: Dent is a mobile-data project from Finland, started in 2017, with an app that sells eSIM data plans and lets users buy, sell and gift mobile data. DENT is the token used for payments and rewards in the app.
deod: Decentrawood is a metaverse platform that combines blockchain, virtual reality and AI to create a virtual world where users can own land, work, socialize and run businesses. DEOD is the token used for payments inside this virtual world.
dep: DEAPCOIN (DEP) is the token of the Japanese gaming platform PlayMining, run by Singapore-based Digital Entertainment Asset. Users earn DEP by playing free games and enjoying manga and anime content, and can use it to buy NFTs.
deso: DeSo (Decentralized Social) is a layer-1 blockchain built specifically for social media apps, storing posts, profiles and follows on-chain. It grew out of the BitClout project, and the DESO token pays fees and powers creator coins and tipping.
desu: Dexsport is a Web3 betting and gaming platform that combines sports betting, esports and casino games in one interface. Players sign up with e-mail, Google or Telegram or connect a crypto wallet; DESU is its utility token for rewards, lotteries and the community.
deus: XMAQUINA (DEUS) is a DAO that gives its community shared access to investments in humanoid robotics and physical AI companies, which are usually open only to venture funds. DEUS is the governance token used to vote on the DAO's decisions.
dexe: DeXe (DEXE) is a protocol for creating and running decentralized autonomous organizations (DAOs). It offers ready-made tools for voting, treasuries and delegation, and the DEXE token is used to govern the platform itself.
dext: DexTools is an analytics app for traders on decentralized exchanges, running since 2020: it shows live charts, new token pairs, liquidity and wallet activity across many blockchains. Holding DEXT unlocks premium features and discounts.
dextf: Memento (DEXTF), formerly DEXTF Protocol, is a DeFi platform for building and trading tokenized crypto portfolios, a decentralized take on exchange-traded funds where one token holds a basket of assets.
dg: Dollar General is an American discount store chain from Tennessee, founded in 1939, with more than 20,000 small stores. It sells food, cleaning supplies, household goods and clothing at low prices, mostly in small towns and rural areas.
dg-fr: Vinci is a French construction and concessions group, one of the largest in the world. It builds roads, bridges and buildings, operates toll motorways in France and airports through Vinci Airports (including London Gatwick), and provides energy infrastructure services.
dg-token: DeGate is a decentralized exchange built as a zero-knowledge rollup on Ethereum, offering an order book with limit orders and grid trading without giving up custody of funds. DG is its governance and utility token.
dgai: DGrid AI (DGAI) is a decentralized AI infrastructure network that gives access to many AI models through a single OpenAI-compatible gateway. The network routes requests between model providers and node operators and settles payments for their services.
dgld: Digital Gold (DGLD) is a token representing ownership of allocated physical gold stored in a Swiss vault in Castel San Pietro. It is issued by Gold Token SA, the tokenization arm of the precious-metals group MKS PAMP.
dgx: Quest Diagnostics is the largest network of diagnostic laboratories in the US, headquartered in Secaucus, New Jersey. It runs blood tests and other lab tests for doctors, hospitals, employers and patients.
dhi: D.R. Horton is the largest homebuilder in the United States by number of homes sold, a position it has held since 2002. Based in Arlington, Texas, and founded in 1978 by Donald R. Horton, it builds mostly entry-level and move-up single-family homes in dozens of states under brands such as Express Homes and Emerald Homes.
dhl: DHL Group (formerly Deutsche Post DHL) is a German logistics group based in Bonn. It is the world's largest express delivery and freight operator under the DHL brand and also runs Germany's national postal service, Deutsche Post.
dhr: Danaher is a US science and technology conglomerate from Washington, D.C., founded in 1969 by brothers Steven and Mitchell Rales. It makes diagnostic equipment, biotechnology tools and lab systems under brands such as Beckman Coulter, Cepheid, Leica Biosystems and Cytiva.
dia: SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average (DIA) is an ETF on the Dow Jones index: 30 of the best-known large US companies, weighted by share price.
dia-token: DIA is a cross-chain oracle from Switzerland that delivers asset prices and other data, collected from primary sources, to smart contracts on dozens of blockchains. The DIA token is used for governance and staking.
diam: Diamante (DIAM) is a Layer 1 blockchain built around quantum-resistant security for everyday crypto use. It pairs a proof-of-stake validator set with post-quantum signature schemes and an execution layer that processes transactions in parallel for fast finality.
diem: DIEM is a token of Venice, a private AI platform, issued on the Base network. Each DIEM gives its holder a daily allowance of Venice API compute for AI models, and new DIEM is created by locking staked VVV tokens.
dime: DIME is the token of Paradex, a decentralized exchange for perpetual futures that runs on its own Starknet-based appchain and was incubated by the crypto investment firm Paradigm. Traders keep custody of their funds while trading with an order book.
dimo: DIMO is an open network that lets drivers connect their cars through an app or a small plug-in device and own and share their vehicle data. Drivers earn DIMO tokens for contributing data, and developers use it to build apps for insurance, maintenance, car sales and more.
dis: The Walt Disney Company is an American media and entertainment company based in Burbank, California, founded in 1923 by Walt and Roy Disney. It owns the Disney, Pixar, Marvel and Lucasfilm studios, the Disney+ streaming service, the ABC and ESPN networks, and theme parks around the world.
disco: Disco is a Japanese equipment maker from Tokyo that makes machines for cutting and grinding semiconductor wafers. Its dicing and wafer-thinning tools are used by almost all chipmakers, including for HBM memory.
ditau: DITGOLD (DITAU) is the native token of DitGold, a decentralized ecosystem built on the idea that data is the new gold. The project aims to recognize and tokenize the value of data, giving people transparent ownership of it and a share in the data economy.
divi: Divi is a proof-of-stake cryptocurrency designed to make staking and running masternodes simple for everyday users. Its wallet lets holders earn staking rewards in a few clicks without technical setup.
djed: Djed is an overcollateralized stablecoin on Cardano that aims to stay at one US dollar. It was designed with research from IOG and launched by COTI in 2023; each DJED is backed by ADA in a reserve, with the SHEN reserve coin absorbing price swings.
dji6930: DOWGE (DJI6930) is a meme coin that mixes the Dow Jones index with the Doge meme; its ticker is a nod to the SPX6900 meme coin. It has no product of its own: its value rests on community interest and trading.
dka: dKargo is a South Korean blockchain project for logistics that links data from carriers, warehouses and delivery services to track shipments transparently. DKA is the token for payments and rewards on the network.
dlr: Digital Realty is a US company based in Austin, Texas, founded in 2004, and one of the world's largest owners of data centres. It leases space, power and connectivity for servers to cloud providers and corporations in dozens of major cities and is structured as a REIT.
dltr: Dollar Tree is a US discount store chain from Virginia, where most items sell for a single low fixed price of about a dollar. It sells household basics, food, party supplies and stationery in thousands of stores in the US and Canada.
dmart: Avenue Supermarts is an Indian company from Mumbai that runs the DMart hypermarket chain, founded by Radhakishan Damani in 2002. It sells groceries, household goods and clothing at low prices, usually in stores it owns.
dmc: DeLorean (DMC) is the token of DeLorean Labs, the Web3 arm of the DeLorean car brand made famous by the "Back to the Future" films. It is issued on the Sui blockchain and used in the brand's digital and fan community programs.
dmd: Diamond (DMD) is one of the older cryptocurrencies, launched in 2013, which later moved to its own DMD Diamond blockchain with an Ethereum-compatible design and a validator-based consensus. DMD is the native coin used for fees and staking.
dmtr: Dimitra is an agritech platform that gives small farmers digital tools: satellite imagery, soil sensors and machine learning help them plan crops, improve yields and track their produce. DMTR is the token used for payments and governance in the Dimitra ecosystem.
dna: NeoSoul is a project building market infrastructure for the AI-agent economy, where agents learn, compete, coordinate and create measurable value. DNA is the ecosystem token.
dnt: district0x (DNT) is an Ethereum project launched in 2017 for creating decentralized marketplaces and communities, called districts, built with Aragon tools. DNT holders stake the token to vote on which districts are listed and how they are run.
dodo: DODO is a decentralized exchange on Ethereum, BNB Chain and other networks that uses its own Proactive Market Maker (PMM) algorithm with oracle prices. It aims to let users trade with less price slippage, and DODO is its governance token.
dog: Dog (Bitcoin), or DOG•GO•TO•THE•MOON, is a memecoin native to the Bitcoin blockchain, issued in 2024 under the Runes standard. Tokens were airdropped to holders of a rare-sat artifact with no team sale, and it is pitched as a way to bring new people to Bitcoin.
doge: Dogecoin is the first famous memecoin, created in 2013 by Billy Markus and Jackson Palmer as a joke based on the Shiba Inu dog meme. It is used for payments and tipping, and Elon Musk's posts boosted its fame.
dogeking: DogeKing (DOGEKING) is a Dogecoin-themed meme token with a reflection mechanism: a fee on each transfer is shared out to holders, who receive DOGE simply for holding DOGEKING in their wallets.
doginme: doginme (DOGINME) is a dog-themed memecoin on Base, the Ethereum layer-2 network from Coinbase, built around the 'dog in me' meme. It is a community token with no utility beyond trading.
dogs: DOGS is a memecoin on the TON blockchain inspired by Spotty, a dog drawn by Telegram founder Pavel Durov. In 2024 the token was airdropped to millions of Telegram users based on their activity in the messenger.
dolo: Dolomite is a decentralized money market and margin trading protocol, launched on Arbitrum, where users can lend, borrow and trade a wide range of tokens while keeping the rewards of deposited assets. DOLO is the protocol's token for governance and incentives.
dood: DOOD is the token of Doodles, an entertainment brand that grew out of a popular NFT collection of colorful pastel characters launched in 2021. Doodles creates original stories, animation, music, live events and merchandise.
doosan-enerbility: Doosan Enerbility, formerly Doosan Heavy Industries & Construction, is a South Korean power equipment maker based in Changwon and part of the Doosan Group. It builds nuclear reactor components, gas and steam turbines and wind turbines, and is developing small modular reactors.
dos: DAPPOS (DOS) is a protocol that simplifies using blockchains through «intents»: the user only states what they want to do, and the network finds the way to execute it across different blockchains. DOS is the token of this ecosystem.
dot: Polkadot is a multi-chain network that joins separate blockchains into one system with cross-chain messaging and shared security. It was created by Ethereum co-founder Gavin Wood; DOT is used for staking, governance and paying for network resources.
dov: Dover Corporation is a US industrial group from Illinois, founded in 1955. It makes pumps, fuelling-station equipment, refrigerated display cases for supermarkets, fluid-handling components and packaging machinery.
dovu: DOVU is a British project on the Hedera network that brings environmental data and carbon credits on-chain. It helps farmers and companies record and verify sustainability data and trade carbon offsets transparently; DOVU is the network's token.
dow: Dow Inc. is a US chemical giant from Midland, Michigan, founded in 1897 by Herbert Dow. It makes plastics such as polyethylene, silicones, industrial chemicals and coatings used in packaging, construction, cars and household goods.
dpi: DeFi Pulse Index (DPI) is an index token launched in 2020 by Index Coop and DeFi Pulse that holds a basket of leading DeFi governance tokens on Ethereum, such as Uniswap and Aave. One DPI gives exposure to the whole basket, which is rebalanced regularly.
dr-sulaiman-al-habib: Dr. Sulaiman Al Habib Medical Group is the largest private hospital operator in Saudi Arabia, based in Riyadh and founded by physician Dr. Sulaiman Al Habib. It runs hospitals, clinics, pharmacies and home care in the Kingdom, and also has hospitals in the UAE and Bahrain.
drb: DebtReliefBot (DRB) is a memecoin on Base that was created in March 2025 when xAI's chatbot Grok was asked on X to launch a token through the Bankr bot. Trading fees from the token go to a wallet linked to Grok.
dreams: Daydreams (DREAMS) is the token of Daydreams, an open-source framework for building AI agents that act on blockchains, for example trading or playing on-chain games. It works with many networks and agent tools and is released under the MIT licence.
drg: DragonSwap is a decentralized exchange on the Sei blockchain where users swap tokens and provide liquidity. DRG is its token, used for governance and to reward liquidity providers.
dri: Darden Restaurants is the largest operator of full-service restaurants in the US, based in Orlando, Florida. It owns the Olive Garden, LongHorn Steakhouse, The Capital Grille, Yard House and Ruth's Chris Steak House chains.
drift: Drift Protocol is one of the largest decentralized exchanges on Solana, offering perpetual futures, spot trading, lending and borrowing in one app. DRIFT is its governance token, used to vote on how the protocol is run.
drv: Derive (formerly Lyra) is a decentralized protocol for options, perpetual futures and structured products, running on its own Derive Chain built on the OP Stack. DRV is the governance token: holders steer the protocol and receive a share of fee revenue.
