dsy: Dassault Systèmes is a French 3D design software company founded in 1981 as part of the Dassault group. Engineers in aerospace, automotive and machinery use its CATIA and SOLIDWORKS programs; it also makes software for life sciences and simulation.
dsync: Destra Network (DSYNC) is a decentralized network for AI: it offers infrastructure to run autonomous agents, decentralized computing and privacy tools in one ecosystem. DSYNC is its deflationary utility token used to pay for services.
dte: DTE Energy is an energy company from Detroit that supplies electricity and natural gas to millions of customers in Michigan. It also develops wind and solar farms and runs energy projects for industry.
dte-de: Deutsche Telekom is Europe's largest telecom company, based in Bonn, and the former state postal and telephone network of Germany. It provides mobile and internet services in Germany and across Europe and controls the US operator T-Mobile US.
dtg: Daimler Truck, based in Stuttgart, is the world's largest maker of trucks and buses; it was spun off from Daimler in 2021. Its brands include Mercedes-Benz Trucks, Freightliner, Western Star, Fuso and Setra buses.
dual: Dual is a tokenization engine for real-world assets that lets businesses build programmable tokens for anything from currencies and loyalty points to real estate, treasuries and physical products. DUAL is the utility token that powers the ecosystem.
duk: Duke Energy is one of the largest US utilities, based in Charlotte, North Carolina. It generates and delivers electricity to millions of customers in the Carolinas, Florida and the Midwest, sells natural gas, and runs a large nuclear fleet.
dusk: Dusk (DUSK) is a layer-1 blockchain from the Netherlands built for regulated financial markets. It lets tokenized securities be issued and traded in line with EU law while protecting privacy; DUSK is used for fees and staking.
dvn: Devon Energy is a US oil and gas producer from Oklahoma City, founded in 1971. It extracts oil, natural gas and natural gas liquids from US shale fields, above all the Delaware Basin of the Permian.
dvo: Divo (DVO) is the token of DIVO, a SocialFi network for the fashion and advertising industry. Creators, agencies and brands use it to publish work, protect ownership of their content with AI tools, get paid and collaborate across borders without intermediaries.
dxcm: DexCom is an American medical technology company from San Diego that makes continuous glucose monitoring systems for people with diabetes. A small sensor on the skin sends sugar levels to a phone or watch every few minutes, without finger pricks.
dydx: dYdX is a decentralized exchange for perpetual futures, founded in 2017 by former Coinbase engineer Antonio Juliano. It now runs on its own blockchain in the Cosmos ecosystem; the DYDX token is used for staking, network security and governance.
dym: Dymension is a modular layer-1 blockchain built with the Cosmos SDK that makes it easy to launch custom rollups called RollApps. It gives them shared security, liquidity and interoperability, and DYM is used for staking, fees and governance.
ebay: eBay is a US online marketplace from San Jose, California, founded in 1995 by Pierre Omidyar. Millions of sellers and buyers trade new and used goods on it, from collectible cards to car parts, by auction or at a fixed price.
echo: EchoStar is a US telecom company from Colorado that merged with DISH Network. It runs DISH satellite TV, the Sling TV streaming service, HughesNet satellite internet and the Boost Mobile wireless brand.
ecl: Ecolab is a US company based in Saint Paul, Minnesota, founded in 1923, that provides water treatment, cleaning, hygiene and infection-prevention products and services. Its customers include restaurants, hotels, hospitals, food plants and factories; it also owns Nalco Water.
ecte: EurocoinToken (ECTE) is a token created for micropayments and international transactions through the Eurocoinpay payment gateway, aimed mainly at brick-and-mortar shops and their customers who want to pay for goods and services in crypto.
ed: Consolidated Edison (Con Edison) is a New York utility with a history dating back to 1823. It supplies electricity, gas and steam to millions of customers in New York City and Westchester County; its Manhattan steam system is one of the largest in the world.
edel: Edel Finance is an on-chain lending network for tokenized stocks. Holders of tokenized shares from issuers such as Ondo and xStocks can lend them out for yield, while traders borrow them to build long or short positions without perpetual futures.
eden: OpenEden is a Singapore-based real-world asset tokenization platform that issues TBILL, a token backed by short-term US Treasury bills. It has also launched the USDO stablecoin; EDEN is the ecosystem token.
edena: EDENA is the token of EDENA Capital Partners, which runs a platform for security token offerings (STOs). It tokenizes real estate, carbon credits, government bonds, ETFs and REITs so investors can buy small fractions and trade them around the clock.
edu: Open Campus (EDU) is a protocol building blockchain infrastructure for education: digital diplomas and certificates and funding for educational content. The project is backed by Animoca Brands and runs its own network, EDU Chain.
eem: iShares MSCI Emerging Markets (EEM) is a BlackRock ETF holding large companies from emerging markets, including China, India and Taiwan.
efa: iShares MSCI EAFE (EFA) invests in large companies from Europe, Australasia and the Far East, excluding the US and Canada.
efi: ElevateFi (EFI) is a DeFi protocol on Polygon offering non-custodial staking vaults, validator delegation and liquidity strategies, including optional pools of real-world assets. A DAO of token holders votes on proposals.
efx: Equifax is one of the three major US credit bureaus, founded in 1899 in Atlanta. It collects credit histories of millions of people and businesses, sells credit reports and scores to lenders and verifies income and employment; in 2017 it suffered a huge data breach.
eg: Everest Group is a reinsurance and insurance company based in Bermuda, founded in 1973. It takes on risks from other insurers worldwide and sells property, casualty and specialty insurance to businesses.
egl1: EGL1 is a meme token built around a bald eagle and American patriotic imagery that calls itself the first superhero meme. It has no practical use beyond its community and trades as a memecoin.
egld: MultiversX (formerly Elrond) is a layer-1 blockchain from Romania that uses sharding for high throughput. Launched in 2020, it supports smart contracts and DeFi; EGLD pays fees and is used for staking and governance.
eigen: EigenCloud (formerly EigenLayer) is a restaking protocol on Ethereum: staked ETH is reused to secure other services and networks. The project was founded by Sreeram Kannan, and the EIGEN token is used for governance and to back guarantees for its verifiable cloud services.
eix: Edison International is a California power company whose main subsidiary, Southern California Edison, supplies electricity to millions of people in Southern California. It is developing the grid, energy storage and infrastructure for electric vehicles.
ekubo: Ekubo Protocol (EKUBO) is a decentralized exchange with concentrated liquidity that started on Starknet and also runs on Ethereum. It keeps all pools in a single contract to cut gas costs and lets developers add custom «extensions» to pools; EKUBO is its governance token.
el: The Estée Lauder Companies is an American beauty group based in New York, founded in 1946 by Estée Lauder and her husband Joseph. It makes skin care, makeup, fragrance and hair-care products under brands such as Estée Lauder, Clinique, MAC, La Mer, Bobbi Brown, Jo Malone London and Tom Ford Beauty.
el-fr: EssilorLuxottica is a French-Italian eyewear giant formed in 2018 by the merger of Essilor and Luxottica. It makes spectacle lenses, frames and sunglasses under brands like Ray-Ban and Oakley, runs optical chains such as Sunglass Hut and makes smart glasses with Meta.
el-token: ELYSIA is a peer-to-peer real-estate investment platform that tokenises properties so many people can co-invest in a building with small amounts and connects sellers with buyers. EL is the platform's token used within its ecosystem.
ela: Elastos is a blockchain platform founded by operating-system veteran Rong Chen to build a user-owned "SmartWeb". Its main chain is merge-mined with Bitcoin, borrowing Bitcoin's hash power for security, and ELA pays for transactions and services in the ecosystem.
ele: Endesa is Spain's largest electricity company, headquartered in Madrid and controlled by Italy's Enel. It generates power at nuclear, gas, hydro and solar plants, owns distribution grids and supplies electricity and gas to millions of customers.
elephant: Elephant Money is a DeFi protocol on BNB Chain built around the ELEPHANT token and its TRUNK stablecoin. Its treasury and token mechanics are meant to fund yield for users holding and staking these tokens.
elf: aelf (ELF) is a layer-1 blockchain from Singapore, launched in 2017, built with a main chain and side chains for scaling. Smart contracts are written in C#, and the project focuses on AI tools for developers.
elg: Escoin (ELG) is a crypto project aimed at the legal sector: it wants to give law firms and their clients a shared digital infrastructure to work together across borders, with the token used inside that network.
elizaos: ElizaOS is an open-source framework for building autonomous AI agents that can talk on social networks and act on blockchains. The project grew out of ai16z, and the ELIZAOS token is used for governance and ecosystem growth.
elsa: HeyElsa is an AI platform that turns plain-language requests into on-chain actions: swaps, bridges, staking, yield search and portfolio management across many networks. It offers an AI copilot for users and widgets, an SDK and APIs for businesses.
elv: Elevance Health (Anthem until 2022) is one of the largest US health insurers, based in Indianapolis. It sells health plans under the Anthem Blue Cross Blue Shield brand, serves Medicare and Medicaid programs and runs the CarelonRx pharmacy business.
emblem: Emblem Vault is a platform that wraps crypto assets from many blockchains, including Bitcoin Ordinals and Counterparty tokens, into tradable NFT vaults. This lets assets from one chain be bought and sold on marketplaces of another; the Emblem token belongs to its ecosystem.
eme: EMCOR Group is a US construction company from Connecticut that installs electrical, mechanical and plumbing systems in buildings. It works on data centres, factories, hospitals and offices and also maintains the systems of existing buildings.
emr: Emerson Electric is a US industrial technology company based in St. Louis, Missouri, founded in 1890. It makes automation systems, control valves, measurement instruments and industrial software used by factories, refineries, chemical and power plants.
en: Bouygues is a French industrial group based in Paris, founded in 1952 by Francis Bouygues. It works in construction (Bouygues Construction and road builder Colas), energy and services (Equans), telecoms through Bouygues Telecom, and media through the TV channel TF1.
ena: Ethena is an Ethereum protocol that issues USDe, a synthetic dollar kept stable by crypto collateral and hedging with futures. ENA is the protocol's governance token; the project was founded by Guy Young.
enb: Enbridge is a Canadian energy company from Calgary that runs one of North America's largest networks of oil and gas pipelines. It also supplies natural gas to homes in Ontario and develops wind and solar power.
enel: Enel is Italy's largest energy company, based in Rome and founded in 1962 as the state power monopoly. It generates electricity, including renewables through Enel Green Power, owns power grids and sells electricity and gas in Italy, Spain (Endesa) and Latin America.
engi: Engie is a French energy company based in Paris, formed from Gaz de France and Suez. It generates electricity, much of it from renewables, owns gas networks and storage in France and provides energy services to cities and businesses.
eni: Eni is an Italian energy company based in Rome, founded in 1953 by Enrico Mattei. It produces oil and gas in dozens of countries, especially in Africa, refines fuel, sells gas and electricity through Plenitude and is growing renewable energy and biofuels.
enj: Enjin Coin (ENJ) is the token of the Enjin ecosystem, which has been building infrastructure for in-game NFT items since 2017. Developers issue in-game objects on Enjin's own blockchain, and ENJ is used to create them, pay fees and stake.
enr: Siemens Energy is a German energy equipment maker based in Munich, spun off from Siemens in 2020. It builds gas turbines, power grid equipment and transformers, and wind turbines through Siemens Gamesa.
ens: Ethereum Name Service (ENS) is a domain name system on Ethereum that replaces long wallet addresses with readable names like name.eth. The service launched in 2017 under Nick Johnson; ENS is the governance token of its DAO.
enso: Enso is a network that brings different blockchains together in one access point for developers: its API and tools let them read data and build and execute transactions with DeFi protocols across many chains. ENSO is the network token.
entg: Entegris is a US supplier of specialty materials for chipmaking based in Massachusetts. It provides semiconductor fabs with ultra-pure chemicals, filters, wafer carriers and contamination-control solutions.
eoan: E.ON is one of Europe's largest energy companies, based in Essen, Germany. It runs electricity and gas distribution grids in Germany and other countries and supplies energy to tens of millions of customers.
eog: EOG Resources is a US oil and gas producer based in Houston, formerly Enron Oil & Gas, which split from Enron in 1999. It extracts oil and natural gas mainly from shale fields in Texas and other US states.
epic: Epic Cash (EPIC) is private digital cash built on the MimbleWimble protocol, which hides transaction amounts and participants. The coin is created by mining and had no pre-allocation to its founders.
epol: iShares MSCI Poland (EPOL) invests in Poland's largest listed companies: banks, energy firms and retailers.
eqix: Equinix is the world's largest colocation data center operator, based in Redwood City, California, and founded in 1998. It rents server space in dozens of major cities and links the networks of cloud providers, banks and telecoms; it is structured as a REIT.
eqt: EQT Corporation is the largest natural gas producer in the United States, headquartered in Pittsburgh. It extracts gas from the Appalachian Basin shale (Marcellus and Utica) and owns pipelines to transport it.
era: Caldera is a rollup-as-a-service platform that helps projects launch their own layer-2 chains on Ethereum, plus Metalayer to connect them. ERA is the token for staking, payments and governance.
erf: Eurofins Scientific is a laboratory testing group headquartered in Luxembourg, founded in 1987 in Nantes, France. Through a global network of labs it tests food, water, the environment, medicines and clinical samples for safety, quality and authenticity.
erg: Ergo is a proof-of-work blockchain launched in 2019 with the eUTXO model and powerful smart contracts for DeFi and financial tools. ERG is mined, and the network is known for its focus on decentralization with no pre-mine.
ern: Ethos Reserve Note (ERN) is a dollar-pegged stablecoin from Ethos Reserve, a DeFi protocol on Optimism. Users mint ERN by locking crypto such as ETH as collateral worth more than the loan, which is how it aims to stay near $1.
es: Eversource Energy is New England's largest energy company, headquartered in Boston and Hartford. It delivers electricity, natural gas and water to millions of customers in Connecticut, Massachusetts and New Hampshire.
ese: Eesee is a Web3 marketplace where people can win NFTs, tokens and other assets through prize draws and drops instead of paying full price. ESE is the platform token, used for rewards and perks.
esp: Espresso (ESP) is a transaction-confirmation network for layer-2 blockchains based on BFT consensus. It gives rollups a near-instant, reliable view of each other's state, making interaction between chains easier and protecting against block reorgs.
ess: Essex Property Trust is a US real estate investment trust (REIT) based in San Mateo, California, founded in 1971. It owns, develops and rents out apartment communities on the West Coast — in Southern and Northern California and the Seattle area.
etc: Ethereum Classic is the original Ethereum chain that kept running after the 2016 hard fork, when most of the community reversed the effects of The DAO hack. ETC sticks to the "code is law" principle and, unlike Ethereum, still uses Proof of Work mining.
eternal: Eternal (formerly Zomato) is an Indian internet company based in Gurugram, founded in 2008. It runs the Zomato food delivery app, the Blinkit quick-commerce grocery service, District for bookings and tickets, and Hyperpure, which supplies restaurants.
eth: Ether (ETH) is the coin of Ethereum, the biggest smart-contract platform, which hosts DeFi, NFTs and stablecoins. Ether pays the network's transaction fees; Ethereum was co-founded by Vitalik Buterin in 2015.
etha: iShares Ethereum Trust (ETHA) is BlackRock's spot ether ETF, launched in 2024, giving brokerage-account access to ETH, the coin of the Ethereum network.
ethdydx: This is the original Ethereum version (ERC-20) of the DYDX token, issued in 2021 for the dYdX derivatives exchange. dYdX later moved to its own blockchain, where DYDX is the native token, and the Ethereum version can be bridged to it.
ethfi: Ether.fi is a liquid restaking protocol on Ethereum that is also growing into a crypto neobank with a card for spending and saving. Users stake ETH and keep it liquid through the eETH token; ETHFI is the governance token.
ethw: EthereumPoW (ETHW) is a fork of Ethereum created in September 2022, when the main network switched from mining to proof of stake. Some miners kept running the old proof-of-work chain, and ETHW is its native coin.
etn: Eaton is a power management company legally domiciled in Dublin, with roots going back to 1911 in the United States. It makes electrical equipment for buildings, data centers and utility grids, as well as components for aircraft and vehicles.
etn-token: Electroneum is an EVM-compatible layer-1 blockchain with transactions in a few seconds and instant finality. Founded in the UK by Richard Ells, the project targets mobile users and payments in developing countries; ETN is its native coin.
etr: Entergy is a US utility from New Orleans, Louisiana. It generates and delivers electricity to millions of customers in Arkansas, Louisiana, Mississippi and Texas and operates several nuclear power plants.
eul: Euler is a DeFi lending protocol on Ethereum where users supply and borrow crypto assets. Its second version lets anyone create their own lending markets with custom risk settings; EUL is the governance token.
eurc: EURC is a euro-pegged stablecoin issued by Circle, the company behind USDC. Each token is backed one-to-one by euro reserves, it is issued under the EU's MiCA rules, and it runs on Ethereum, Solana, Avalanche, Base and other blockchains.
eurcv: EUR CoinVertible (EURCV) is a euro stablecoin issued by SG-FORGE, the digital-assets subsidiary of French bank Société Générale. Each token aims to equal one euro and is backed by reserves; it runs on public blockchains such as Ethereum.
eure: EURe is a euro stablecoin issued by Monerium, a licensed electronic money institution from Iceland. Each token is regulated e-money backed one-to-one by euros and can move on Ethereum, Gnosis, Polygon and other networks or be redeemed via a bank IBAN.
europ: EURØP is a euro stablecoin compliant with the EU's MiCA rules, issued by a licensed French issuer supervised by the regulator ACPR. Each token is backed 1:1 by euros held at EU banks such as Société Générale and can be redeemed for euros.
eurq: Quantoz EURQ is a euro stablecoin issued by Quantoz Payments, a licensed electronic-money institution in the Netherlands. Each EURQ is meant to equal one euro, is backed by reserves and is issued under the EU's MiCA rules.
eurs: STASIS EURO (EURS) is a euro stablecoin issued by STASIS, a company based in Malta. Each token is meant to be backed one-to-one by euro reserves, with regular audits, and it is used to hold and move euros on blockchains such as Ethereum.
ev: Everything (EV) is a project that combines several DeFi protocols into one interconnected ecosystem. The EV token is used for governance, for using the services and for capturing value across all of the project's products.
evaa: EVAA Protocol is a decentralized lending protocol on the TON network. Users can supply crypto to earn interest or borrow against collateral, including directly from Telegram; EVAA is the protocol's governance token.
evrg: Evergy is an electric utility based in Kansas City, Missouri, formed in 2018 by the merger of Westar Energy and Great Plains Energy. It generates and delivers electricity to millions of people in Kansas and Missouri, with a large share coming from wind power.
ew: Edwards Lifesciences is a US medical device maker based in Irvine, California. It specialises in artificial heart valves, including the Sapien transcatheter valves that are implanted without open-heart surgery.
ewbc: East West Bancorp is a bank holding company from Pasadena, California, and the owner of East West Bank. The bank serves people and businesses in the US and specializes in financial links between America and Greater China.
ewg: iShares MSCI Germany (EWG) invests in large German companies such as SAP, Siemens, Allianz and Deutsche Telekom.
ewt: Energy Web Token (EWT) is the native token of Energy Web Chain, an open blockchain for the energy sector from the non-profit Energy Web. Energy companies use it to track renewable power and certificates and to manage distributed devices.
exc: Exelon is one of the largest US utilities, based in Chicago. Through its grid companies ComEd, PECO and BGE, among others, it delivers electricity and gas to millions of customers in Illinois, Pennsylvania, Maryland and Washington, D.C.
exe: Expand Energy is the largest natural gas producer in the United States, formed in 2024 when Chesapeake Energy merged with Southwestern Energy. Based near Houston in Spring, Texas, it produces gas in the Appalachian Marcellus and Utica shales and the Haynesville basin in Louisiana.
exel: Exelixis is a US cancer-drug company from Alameda, California, founded in 1994. Its best-known medicine is cabozantinib, sold as Cabometyx and Cometriq for kidney, liver and thyroid cancers, and it develops new oncology treatments.
exo: Exor is the Agnelli family's investment holding company, based in Amsterdam. It owns key stakes in Ferrari, Stellantis, CNH, Philips and Iveco, as well as the Juventus football club and The Economist.
expd: Expeditors International is a US logistics company from Seattle, founded in 1979. It arranges international air and ocean freight, customs clearance and warehousing for companies without owning its own planes or ships.
expe: Expedia Group is an American online travel company from Seattle, founded in 1996 as a division of Microsoft. Through Expedia, Hotels.com and Vrbo people book hotels, flights, vacation rentals and rental cars.
exr: Extra Space Storage is an American real estate investment trust (REIT) from Salt Lake City. It runs thousands of self-storage facilities where people and businesses rent units to keep their belongings.
f: Ford Motor Company is a US carmaker from Dearborn, Michigan, founded in 1903 by Henry Ford, who introduced assembly-line production. It builds F-Series pickups, Bronco and Explorer SUVs, the Mustang, Transit commercial vans and Lincoln cars.
f-token: SynFutures is a decentralized protocol for perpetual futures that lets users trade any asset and create new futures markets in seconds. Its V3 oAMM model combines an automated market maker with an on-chain order book; F is the protocol token.
fai: Freysa is an AI agent on the Base network, known for a game in which people paid to try to convince it to hand over a prize pool. The project builds autonomous AI agents that manage funds on their own; FAI is the ecosystem token.
fang: Diamondback Energy is a US oil and gas producer from Midland, Texas. It drills for oil and gas only in the Permian Basin of West Texas, the largest oil region in the United States.
fanuc: Fanuc is a Japanese factory automation company based at the foot of Mount Fuji, founded in 1972. It is the world leader in CNC controls for machine tools and also makes industrial robots and machine tools.
far: FAR Labs (FAR) is the team behind Farcana, a team-based multiplayer shooter game with Web3 features. The FAR token is used in its gaming ecosystem for rewards and in-game activity.
farm: Harvest Finance is a DeFi yield aggregator launched in 2020 that automatically moves deposits into farming strategies and reinvests the rewards. FARM is its token; holders can stake it to receive a share of the protocol's profits.
fartcoin: Fartcoin (FARTCOIN) is a meme coin on Solana that appeared in late 2024 out of jokes around the AI agent Truth Terminal. The token has no practical use and exists as an internet joke, so its price depends on community interest.
fast: Fastenal is a US industrial supplies distributor based in Winona, Minnesota, founded in 1967. It sells fasteners, tools and safety gear to factories and builders through a network of branches and vending machines placed right at customers' sites.
fast-retailing: Fast Retailing is a Japanese company from Yamaguchi that owns Uniqlo, Asia's largest clothing chain. It also runs the GU, Theory and Comptoir des Cotonniers brands; founder Tadashi Yanai turned a family shop into a global retailer of basic clothing.
fbomb: Fantom Bomb (fBOMB) is a decentralized finance token issued on several networks, including Fantom, BNB Chain, Avalanche, Arbitrum and Optimism. It is used in the project's DeFi pools and community apps.
fbtc: Fidelity Wise Origin Bitcoin Fund (FBTC) is Fidelity's spot bitcoin ETF, launched in 2024, which holds real bitcoin in Fidelity's own custody.
fct: FirmaChain (FCT) is a South Korean blockchain for electronic contracts. It lets people and companies sign, store and verify agreements and notarized documents on-chain, so the record cannot be forged or disputed; FCT pays for the network's services.
fcx: Freeport-McMoRan is a US mining company based in Phoenix, Arizona, and one of the world's largest copper producers. It runs Indonesia's Grasberg mine, one of the biggest copper and gold deposits on Earth, plus mines in the US and Peru.
fdusd: First Digital USD (FDUSD) is a dollar-pegged stablecoin issued since 2023 by First Digital Labs, part of Hong Kong-based First Digital Group. Each token is backed one-to-one by cash and short-term US Treasuries held in custody, and it is used mostly as a trading pair on major exchanges.
fdx: FedEx is a US logistics company based in Memphis, Tennessee, founded in 1971 by Frederick Smith. It runs one of the world's largest cargo airline fleets and delivers express parcels, freight and e-commerce shipments to more than 220 countries and territories.
fdxf: FedEx Freight is a leading US less-than-truckload (LTL) carrier that was spun off from FedEx as a separate company. It moves shipments too small to fill a whole truck, combining freight from many shippers across the US, Canada and Mexico.
fe: FirstEnergy is a US power company from Akron, Ohio. Through its regulated utilities it transmits and distributes electricity to millions of customers in Ohio, Pennsylvania, New Jersey, West Virginia and Maryland.
fely: Felysyum (FELY) is the token of a crypto ecosystem built around education and e-commerce: SkillFullHub teaches crypto and blockchain, Felynova funds creators' ideas, Felyzone is a marketplace, and the Aidora program supports education for people in need.
femsaubd: FEMSA is a Mexican conglomerate from Monterrey, founded in 1890 as a brewery. It owns OXXO, Latin America's largest convenience store chain, pharmacies and a stake in the Coca-Cola bottler Coca-Cola FEMSA.
fer: Ferrovial is an infrastructure company founded in 1952 in Madrid that moved its headquarters to the Netherlands in 2023. It builds and operates toll highways, including Canada's 407 ETR and express lanes in Texas, and also manages airports and construction projects.
fer-etf: Ferrovial is an infrastructure company founded in 1952 in Madrid that moved its headquarters to the Netherlands in 2023. It builds and operates toll highways, including Canada's 407 ETR and express lanes in Texas, and also manages airports and construction projects.
ferg: Ferguson is one of the largest distributors of plumbing, waterworks, heating and air conditioning products in the US and Canada. A company with British roots founded in 1953, it supplies professional installers, builders and utilities.
fet: The Artificial Superintelligence Alliance (ASI) was formed in 2024 by merging the AI projects Fetch.ai, SingularityNET and Ocean Protocol. It builds decentralized infrastructure for artificial intelligence and autonomous agents; FET is the alliance's shared token.
ff: FF is the token of Falcon Finance, a "universal collateral" protocol: users deposit crypto or tokenized real-world assets and mint the synthetic dollar USDf against them. This gives liquidity without selling the assets; FF is used for governance and staking.
ffh: Fairfax Financial Holdings is a Canadian insurance and investment holding company based in Toronto, led since 1985 by Prem Watsa and often compared to Berkshire Hathaway. Through companies such as Northbridge, Odyssey Group and Allied World it sells property and casualty insurance and reinsurance worldwide and invests the premiums for the long term.
ffiv: F5, Inc. is a US technology company from Seattle, founded in 1996. It sells software, hardware and cloud services that keep websites and apps fast and secure, including its BIG-IP load balancers, NGINX and web application firewalls.
fhe: Mind Network is a project that uses fully homomorphic encryption (FHE) so that AI agents and apps can compute on data without decrypting it. This brings privacy to Web3 and AI; FHE is the network token used for staking and payments.
fida: Bonfida is a project in the Solana ecosystem known for the Solana Name Service, which lets people register readable .sol domains instead of long wallet addresses. FIDA is its governance token.
fight: FIGHT is the token of a combat-sports fan ecosystem on Solana, run by Concept Labs under an official multi-year UFC license. Fans use it to join fighter communities, take part in prediction games, get merch and tickets, stake and vote.
fil: Filecoin is a decentralized data storage network where anyone can rent out spare disk space and get paid in FIL. It was created by Juan Benet's company Protocol Labs, also known for the IPFS protocol, and its mainnet launched in 2020.
firo: Firo (formerly Zcoin) is a privacy-focused cryptocurrency launched in 2016. It uses its own protocols such as Lelantus Spark to hide the sender, receiver and amount of a transaction; FIRO is mined.
fisv: Fiserv is an American fintech company from Milwaukee that provides banks and credit unions with account-processing and payment-processing software. It also owns Clover, a platform of payment terminals and point-of-sale systems for shops and restaurants.
fitb: Fifth Third Bancorp is a US regional banking group headquartered in Cincinnati, Ohio, and founded in 1858. It serves individuals and businesses in the Midwest and Southeast with accounts, loans, mortgages, payment services and wealth management.
fix: Comfort Systems USA is an American mechanical and electrical contractor based in Houston, Texas, founded in 1997. It designs, installs and maintains heating, ventilation and air-conditioning (HVAC), plumbing and electrical systems for large buildings such as data centers, factories, hospitals and schools across the United States.
flex: Flex is one of the world's largest contract electronics manufacturers, registered in Singapore with headquarters in Austin, Texas. It builds products for other brands, including data-centre equipment, car and medical electronics and consumer devices.
flip: Chainflip (FLIP) is a decentralized protocol for swapping native crypto assets between different blockchains, for example bitcoin for ETH, without wrapped tokens or bridges. Validators stake FLIP, and part of the fees is used to burn the token.
flock: FLock.io is a decentralized network for training and validating AI models, built by a team of researchers including Oxford alumni. Participants contribute compute and data and earn FLOCK for their part in training models.
floki: FLOKI is a memecoin launched in 2021 and named after Floki, Elon Musk's Shiba Inu dog. It has grown into a multi-chain token with its own ecosystem, including the Valhalla game, DeFi services and educational products.
flow: Flow (FLOW) is a layer-1 blockchain for consumer apps, created by Canadian studio Dapper Labs, the makers of CryptoKitties. NBA Top Shot and other digital collectibles run on it; FLOW is used for fees and staking.
flr: Flare is an Ethereum-compatible blockchain specialized in data: built-in oracles deliver prices and information from other networks and the internet. Its FAssets technology lets tokens without smart contracts, such as XRP, be used in DeFi.
fluid: Fluid is a DeFi protocol from the Instadapp team on Ethereum that combines lending and a decentralized exchange on shared liquidity, so collateral can work harder. The FLUID token replaced the former INST token and is used for governance.
flux: Flux is a decentralized cloud infrastructure where thousands of independent nodes provide computing power to run apps and websites. FLUX is mined and used to pay for services and to collateralize nodes.
fmg: Fortescue is an Australian mining company from Perth, founded in 2003 by Andrew Forrest. It mines iron ore in the Pilbara region, mostly for Chinese steelmakers, and is investing in green energy and hydrogen.
fo: Official FO (FO) is a memecoin on the Solana blockchain. It has no product or business behind it, so its price depends on community attention and trading activity.
fogo: Fogo is a layer-1 blockchain compatible with the Solana Virtual Machine, built on the Firedancer validator client and designed for on-chain trading, with very low latency and near-instant finality. FOGO is the network's native token for fees and staking.
fold: The Interfold is an open protocol for confidential shared computation: several parties add private data to a calculation without revealing it to each other. Uses include secret voting, sealed-bid auctions and confidential analytics; FOLD is the network token.
folks: Folks Finance (FOLKS) is a cross-chain DeFi lending protocol: users deposit crypto to earn interest or borrow against collateral across different blockchains from a single interface. The project grew up in the Algorand ecosystem, and FOLKS is its governance token.
fonq: FONQ is the token of an AI-powered Web3 finance platform that offers market insights, analytics and portfolio tracking for crypto and traditional markets. Users earn FXP reward points in the app and can convert them into FONQ.
form: Four (FORM), formerly BinaryX, is the token of the ecosystem linked to Four.meme, a popular memecoin launchpad on BNB Chain. FORM is used for staking, rewards and taking part in ecosystem projects.
fort: Forta is a decentralized blockchain security monitoring network where bots analyze transactions in real time and warn about hacks, scams and anomalies. FORT is used to stake nodes and pay for services.
forth: Ampleforth Governance (FORTH) is the governance token of Ampleforth, the protocol behind AMPL, a token whose supply adjusts daily to move its price toward a target. FORTH holders vote on protocol upgrades and parameters.
fox: Fox Corporation is Rupert Murdoch's US media company, created in 2019 after the 21st Century Fox film studio was sold to Disney. It owns Fox News, the Fox broadcast network, Fox Sports channels and the Tubi streaming service; these are the voting Class B shares.
fox-token: FOX is the governance token of ShapeShift, the crypto platform founded by Erik Voorhees in 2014 that became a community-run DAO in 2021. ShapeShift lets users swap, trade and manage assets across many blockchains without an account.
foxa: Fox Corporation is an American media company based in New York, formed in 2019 when Disney bought most of 21st Century Fox. It owns Fox News, Fox Sports, the Fox broadcast network and local TV stations, and the free streaming service Tubi; it is controlled by the Murdoch family. This listing is its Class A share.
foxsy: Foxsy AI is a Web3 gaming project with play-to-earn games, including a Telegram mini app, where AI plays a central role in gameplay. It is active on Solana and MultiversX, and FOXSY is used for rewards and in-game payments.
fp: Fren Pet is an on-chain virtual pet game on the Base network. Players buy and care for a digital pet with the FP token, keep it alive with items and can attack other pets to earn points and rewards.
froggie: Froggie (FROGGIE) is a community meme coin on BNB Chain inspired by the "Neural Frog" (神经蛙), a popular frog meme and sticker character in Chinese internet culture, especially on WeChat.
front: Frontier (FRONT) is the token of Frontier, a multi-chain crypto wallet app that brings DeFi, staking and token swaps across many blockchains into one place.
frtc: FART COIN (FRTC) is a playful token on BNB Chain built around daily lucky draws, where holders can try their luck to win rewards. The project presents itself as transparent and community-run.
fslr: First Solar is the largest US maker of solar panels, based in Tempe, Arizona and founded in 1999. Unlike most rivals, it uses thin-film cadmium telluride technology instead of silicon and builds its panels in its own factories in the US, India and Southeast Asia.
ft: Flying Tulip is a DeFi project led by Andre Cronje, the creator of Yearn Finance, to build one on-chain exchange that combines spot trading, lending, perpetual futures and options. FT is its token; early buyers got an on-chain right to redeem it for their original contribution.
fti: TechnipFMC is a UK-registered oilfield equipment company formed in 2017 by merging France's Technip with America's FMC Technologies. It designs and supplies subsea equipment and systems for offshore oil and gas fields.
ftnt: Fortinet is a US cybersecurity company based in Sunnyvale, California, founded in 2000. It is best known for its FortiGate firewalls and FortiOS operating system, and sells network security, secure remote access and cloud protection to businesses and governments.
ftrb: Faith Tribe is a collaborative fashion platform where independent designers create, test and sell digital and physical clothing. The blockchain records design ownership, and the FTRB token is used for rewards, voting and payments in the ecosystem.
ftv: Fortive is a US industrial technology company based in Everett, Washington, spun off from Danaher in 2016. It makes Fluke measurement tools, workplace-safety and gas-detection systems, and software for maintaining equipment, buildings and hospitals.
fubon-financial: Fubon Financial is a Taiwanese financial group based in Taipei and controlled by the Tsai family. It brings together Taipei Fubon Bank, insurer Fubon Life, a brokerage and a property insurer, and also has banking businesses in mainland China and Vietnam.
fuel: Fuel Network (FUEL) is a fast execution layer for Ethereum. Its own virtual machine, FuelVM, processes transactions in parallel, and apps are written in Sway, a language made for smart contracts; FUEL is used for fees and staking.
fujitsu: Fujitsu is one of Japan's largest IT companies, based in Tokyo and founded in 1935. It provides IT services, consulting, cloud and data centers, software and servers to businesses and governments, and it co-developed the Fugaku supercomputer with the RIKEN research institute.
fun: FUNToken (FUN) is a token for online gaming and the iGaming industry, launched in 2017. It is used for bets, payments and rewards on gaming platforms, with transparent settlement on the blockchain.
fuse: Fuse is a blockchain project founded in 2019 that focuses on payments and mobile-friendly Web3 apps, offering businesses low-cost, Ethereum-compatible infrastructure for wallets, loyalty programs and stablecoin payments. The FUSE token pays fees and is used for staking.
fuzzy: Fuzzybear (FUZZY) is a memecoin on the XRP Ledger named after a well-known XRPL address, Fuzzybear, which in 2014 placed a famous order on the ledger's built-in exchange offering 1 XRP for 1 BTC.
fwog: Fwog (FWOG) is a memecoin on Solana launched in 2024, built around a cute image of a small frog. It is driven by its community and has no utility beyond trading.
fxn: f(x) Protocol (FXN) is an Ethereum DeFi protocol from the AladdinDAO team. It issues the fxUSD stablecoin backed by ETH-based collateral and offers leveraged ETH positions; FXN is the governance token.
fxnw: FastX Network (FXNW) is a decentralized artificial-intelligence infrastructure for Web3 applications. The project aims to connect AI services with blockchain apps, and the FXNW token is used for payments and participation in the network.
g: Generali is Italy's largest insurer, founded in 1831 in Trieste. It sells life, property and health insurance across Europe, Asia and Latin America and also runs a large asset management business.
g-it: Generali is Italy's largest insurer, founded in 1831 in Trieste. It sells life, property and health insurance across Europe, Asia and Latin America and also runs a large asset management business.
g-token: Gravity (G) is a layer-1 blockchain from Galxe, one of the largest platforms for Web3 quests and on-chain identity. The G token replaced the GAL token and is used for fees, staking and across Galxe services.
gaib: GAIB is a project that turns AI infrastructure, such as GPU computing hardware and its financing, into on-chain assets that people can hold and earn yield from. GAIB is the token of its ecosystem.
gains: Gains Network is the team behind gTrade, a decentralized platform for leveraged trading of crypto, forex, stocks and commodities. It runs on Polygon, Arbitrum and Base, and its token is used for staking and earns a share of trading fees.
gal: GAL is the former token of Galxe, a Web3 rewards and digital-credentials platform where projects run campaigns to attract users. GAL has migrated to G, the token of Galxe's Gravity network, so old coins are exchanged for new ones.
gala: GALA is the token of Gala Games, a US blockchain gaming platform founded in 2019 by Eric Schiermeyer. It is used to buy in-game items and NFTs, reward network node operators and vote; Gala also runs music and film branches.
galaxy-entertainment: Galaxy Entertainment is a Hong Kong company and one of the six licensed casino operators in Macau. It owns the Galaxy Macau, StarWorld and Broadway Macau resorts, earning from gaming, hotels, dining and entertainment, and is controlled by the family of Lui Che Woo.
gama: Gama Token (GAMA) is the utility token of the GAMA Web3 gaming platform. Players win GAMA as rewards in games, while losses burn tokens, so the capped supply shrinks over time.
gas: Gas (GAS) is the second token of the NEO network, used to pay fees for transactions and running smart contracts. NEO holders automatically receive GAS as a reward, so the two coins work as a pair: NEO for governance, GAS as fuel.
gasoline: RBOB gasoline is the US futures contract for petrol. Its price depends on crude oil, the summer driving season and how busy refineries are.
gbpa: Agant GBP (GBPA) is a stablecoin linked to the British pound at 1:1, issued by Agant, a UK company. It puts sterling on the blockchain so it can be used for payments, transfers and trading in crypto, as an alternative to dollar-based stablecoins.
gcoin: Playnance (GCOIN) is a blockchain ecosystem for online games, contests and prediction markets, built as a layer-3 network on Arbitrum. GCOIN is used in the platform's games, tournaments and DeFi features.
gd: General Dynamics is a US defense company from Reston, Virginia. It builds Gulfstream business jets, nuclear submarines, Abrams tanks and armored vehicles, and provides IT services to the US government.
ge: GE Aerospace is a US jet engine maker based in Cincinnati, the successor of the General Electric conglomerate founded in 1892 with Thomas Edison's involvement. After the 2024 split it focuses on engines for passenger and military aircraft and their servicing.
gebn: Geberit is a Swiss maker of sanitary products based in Rapperswil-Jona, founded in 1874. It is known for concealed toilet cisterns, wall-mounted installation frames, pipes and drainage systems sold to builders and plumbers across Europe.
gehc: GE HealthCare is an American medical technology company based in Chicago, spun off from General Electric in 2023. It makes imaging machines such as CT and MRI scanners, ultrasound and X-ray systems, patient monitors and the contrast agents and radiopharmaceuticals used in scans, for hospitals worldwide.
gen: Gen Digital, formerly NortonLifeLock, is a US consumer cybersecurity company based in Tempe, Arizona. It sells antivirus, privacy and identity-protection products under the Norton, Avast, AVG, Avira, LifeLock and CCleaner brands, and owns the fintech app MoneyLion.
genius: Genius (GENIUS) is the token of Genius Terminal, an on-chain terminal for professional crypto trading with a focus on privacy. It combines swaps, cross-chain transfers and wallet management in one interface to make DeFi easier to use.
geod: GEODNET is a decentralized network of ground stations that receive navigation satellite signals (GPS and other GNSS) and provide corrections for centimeter-level positioning. Drones, farm machinery and robots use this data; station owners earn GEOD for running them.
gev: GE Vernova is an American energy company based in Cambridge, Massachusetts, spun off from General Electric in 2024. It makes gas turbines, wind turbines, equipment for nuclear and hydro power, and technology for electricity grids.
gfi: Goldfinch is a decentralized credit protocol on Ethereum that lends stablecoins to real-world businesses, mostly fintech lenders in emerging markets, without requiring crypto collateral; borrowers are vetted off-chain instead. GFI is the protocol's governance token.
gfnorteo: Banorte (Grupo Financiero Banorte) is one of Mexico's largest banks, headquartered in Monterrey and founded in 1899. The group provides banking, insurance and pension savings management.
gfs: GlobalFoundries is a US contract chipmaker based in Malta, New York, created in 2009 from AMD's factories. It makes chips for cars, smartphones and communications at fabs in the United States, Germany and Singapore.
ggbr: Goldfish Gold (GGBR) is a gold-backed token: each one represents 1/1000 of a troy ounce. The metal is held in a Wyoming trust as gold still in the ground at a deposit, not in bars, so the token gives on-chain access to that asset.
ghst: Aavegotchi is a blockchain game by Pixelcraft Studios in which players collect pixel-art ghost NFTs, each backed by interest-earning Aave tokens, and use them in mini-games and a virtual world called the Gotchiverse. GHST is the in-game currency and governance token of its DAO.
ghx: GamerCoin (GHX) is the token of GamerHash, a Polish platform where gamers share their computer's spare processing power and earn rewards. GHX is used for payments inside the platform, such as its store and tournaments.
giga: Gigachad (GIGA) is a Solana meme coin inspired by the "Gigachad" internet meme about the ideal man with a chiselled jaw. It has no technical function and rests on its community and meme culture.
giggle: Giggle Fund (GIGGLE) is a BNB Chain meme token linked to Giggle Academy, an education initiative backed by Binance founder Changpeng Zhao. Part of the token's trading fees goes to donations for free education.
gild: Gilead Sciences is an American biopharmaceutical company based in California, founded in 1987. It is known for its HIV drugs (Biktarvy), hepatitis C treatments (Sovaldi, Harvoni) and the COVID-19 drug Veklury, and is expanding in cancer and inflammatory diseases.
gis: General Mills is a US packaged-food company based in Minneapolis, founded in 1866. Its brands include Cheerios cereal, Pillsbury dough, Nature Valley bars, Old El Paso Mexican foods and Blue Buffalo pet food.
givn: Givaudan is a Swiss company from Vernier, Geneva, founded in 1895 and the world's largest maker of flavors and fragrances. It creates tastes for food and drinks and scents for perfumes, cosmetics and household products.
gld: SPDR Gold Shares (GLD) is the biggest fund backed by physical gold: every share is backed by gold bars held in vaults.
gld-token: This is a tokenized version of SPDR Gold Shares (GLD) offered by Robinhood, tracking the price of the world's largest gold ETF. The fund itself holds physical gold bars in vaults, so its price follows the price of gold.
gle: Société Générale is one of France's largest banks, founded in Paris in 1864. It provides retail banking in France and runs an investment bank, car leasing through Ayvens and subsidiary banks in Africa and Central Europe.
glm: Golem (GLM) is one of the first decentralized computing projects, founded in Poland in 2016. Its network lets people rent out or rent computing power, for example for rendering and AI tasks; GLM is the payment token on Ethereum.
glmr: Moonbeam is an Ethereum-compatible smart contract network that runs as a parachain on Polkadot. It lets developers deploy Ethereum-style apps while connecting to other Polkadot chains, and GLMR pays fees, secures the network through staking and is used for governance.
glw: Corning is a US glass and materials maker from Corning, New York, founded in 1851. It is known for Gorilla Glass for smartphones and also makes optical fiber, display glass, ceramic filters for cars and lab glassware.
gm: General Motors is a US carmaker based in Detroit, founded in 1908. It builds vehicles under the Chevrolet, GMC, Cadillac and Buick brands, is developing electric cars and has a financing arm, GM Financial.
gmee: GAMEE (GMEE) is the token of GAMEE, a mobile and Telegram gaming platform owned by Animoca Brands. Players compete in casual games and tournaments, and GMEE is used for entries, rewards and in-game items.
gmexicob: Grupo México is a Mexican conglomerate based in Mexico City and one of the world's largest copper producers through its subsidiary Southern Copper, with mines in Mexico and Peru. It also runs Ferromex, Mexico's largest railroad, and infrastructure businesses.
gmg: Goodman Group is an Australian industrial-property company based in Sydney. It develops, owns and manages warehouses, logistics centers and, increasingly, data centers close to big cities in Australia, Asia, Europe and the Americas, leasing them to e-commerce, logistics and technology companies.
gmt: GMT is the governance token of STEPN, a move-to-earn app where users earn rewards for walking and running in NFT sneakers. The project was created by the Australian studio Find Satoshi Lab, and GMT is also used in its other products.
gmx: GMX is a decentralized exchange for perpetual futures and leveraged spot trading on Arbitrum and Avalanche. Traders trade straight from their wallets, liquidity providers earn a share of fees, and GMX is the governance and fee-sharing token.
gno: Gnosis is an ecosystem that began in 2015 as a prediction-market platform. It gave rise to the popular Safe multisig wallet, and today it develops the Gnosis Chain blockchain and payment services such as the Gnosis Pay card. GNO is used for staking and governance.
gnot: Gno.land is a layer-1 smart-contract platform developed by NewTendermint, the team of Cosmos co-founder Jae Kwon. Contracts are written in Gno, a deterministic, interpreted version of the Go language; GNOT is the network's token for fees and governance.
goat: Goatseus Maximus (GOAT) is a Solana memecoin launched in 2024 on pump.fun. It became famous because Truth Terminal, an experimental AI chatbot on X, kept promoting the joke behind it, making GOAT the first big 'AI agent' memecoin.
gods: Gods Unchained is a free-to-play digital trading card game by Immutable, where players truly own their cards as NFTs on Immutable's Ethereum layer-2 network. The GODS token is used to craft cards, trade and vote on the game's future.
gohome: GOHOME is a meme token born from a January 2025 incident on the White House website, when the words Go Home appeared on its page. The community turned the episode into a meme, and the token trades purely as a meme asset with no product behind it.
gold: Gold is the classic safe-haven asset that has served as a store of value for thousands of years. Central banks, jewellers and investors buy it, especially in times of crisis, inflation or war.
gold-token: Stairway to Gold (GOLD) is a faith-themed memecoin on Solana inspired by the Bible verse Matthew 6:24. The project encourages long-term holding and says its supply is locked until the coin reaches a set market value.
gomining: GoMining is a digital Bitcoin mining platform backed by real data centers: users buy virtual miners as NFTs and receive daily rewards in BTC. The GOMINING token is used to pay maintenance fees, get discounts and for staking.
goog: Alphabet is the parent company of Google, based in Mountain View, California. It earns mainly from search and YouTube advertising, plus Google Cloud, Android and subscriptions, and develops the Gemini AI and Waymo robotaxis. Class C shares (GOOG) carry no voting rights.
googl: Alphabet is the parent company of Google, based in Mountain View, California; Google was founded in 1998 by Larry Page and Sergey Brin. It owns Google Search, YouTube, Android, Chrome, Google Cloud and the Gemini AI. Class A shares (GOOGL) carry voting rights.
googl-token: This is a Robinhood stock token that tracks Alphabet Class A shares, the parent company of Google, YouTube and Android. Robinhood launched such tokens in 2025 for customers in the European Union, letting them get US stock exposure on-chain around the clock.
gp: Graphite Protocol (GP) is a blockchain project for creators. Its Creator Suite products give artists and content makers simple tools to use Web3 without deep technical knowledge; GP is the network's token.
gpc: Genuine Parts Company is a US distributor of automotive and industrial replacement parts from Atlanta, founded in 1928. It owns the NAPA Auto Parts network and the industrial parts business Motion Industries.
gpn: Global Payments is a US payments company from Atlanta. It processes card payments for shops, restaurants and online businesses in dozens of countries and sells software for accepting payments, including through the Heartland and Genius brands.
gps: GoPlus Security (GPS) is a Web3 security network that checks tokens, smart contracts and addresses for scams and malicious activity. Its API is built into many wallets and exchanges; the GPS token is used to pay for security services.
gram: Gram (formerly Toncoin) is the native coin of the TON blockchain (The Open Network), originally conceived by Telegram's founders, the Durov brothers. The network is deeply integrated into Telegram, where the coin is used for transfers, fees, the built-in wallet and mini apps.
grass: Grass is a network where users share their unused internet bandwidth for rewards through a browser extension or app. This capacity helps collect public web data for training AI; the GRASS token runs on Solana.
griffain: Griffain is a project in the Solana ecosystem that lets users manage on-chain operations through AI agents: swapping tokens, providing liquidity and other DeFi actions. GRIFFAIN is the platform's token.
grmn: Garmin is a Swiss-American electronics maker founded in 1989 in Kansas by Gary Burrell and Min Kao. It is known for GPS navigators, sports watches and fitness trackers, as well as avionics for aircraft and marine electronics.
grnd: SuperWalk (GRND) is a South Korean move-to-earn app for walking and running. Users buy NFT sneakers to earn GRND tokens for moving at the right pace, while the basic mode lets them earn the WALK token without NFTs.
grove: Grove is a credit infrastructure protocol that connects stablecoin capital with traditional finance. It allocates stablecoin liquidity into real-world assets such as tokenized funds and credit, and provides financing and liquidity to institutions on-chain.
grt: The Graph is an indexing protocol for blockchain data, often called the "Google of blockchains": it organizes data from Ethereum and other networks so apps can query it quickly through open APIs called subgraphs. GRT pays for queries and is staked by indexers who run the network.
grvt: GRVT is a hybrid crypto exchange for perpetual futures built on ZKsync technology. It combines the speed of a centralized exchange with self-custody of assets and privacy; GRVT is the platform's token.
gs: Goldman Sachs is one of the world's best-known investment banks, founded in 1869 in New York. It advises on large mergers and acquisitions, arranges share offerings, trades securities and manages money for wealthy clients and institutions.
gt: GateToken (GT) is the native token of the Gate (Gate.io) crypto exchange, founded in 2013. It gives discounts on trading fees and access to new token launches, and it pays fees on the exchange's own blockchain network.
gtc: Gitcoin is a platform for funding open-source software and public goods in Web3, founded in 2017 by Kevin Owocki. It is known for grant rounds using quadratic funding; GTC is the governance token of Gitcoin DAO.
gulf: Gulf Development is a Thai energy and infrastructure group from Bangkok, formed in 2025 by merging Gulf Energy Development with Intouch. It owns gas-fired and renewable power plants and a large stake in mobile operator AIS; it was founded by Sarath Ratanavadi.
gun: GUNZ is an Avalanche-based blockchain created by Gunzilla Games for the shooter game Off The Grid. In-game items exist as NFTs, and GUN is used to pay fees and trade them.
gwei: ETHGas (GWEI) is an Ethereum blockspace infrastructure protocol that splits space in blocks into tradable units. It lets users buy block space in advance and get fast transaction confirmations.
gww: W. W. Grainger is a US industrial supplies distributor based in Illinois, founded in 1927. It sells tools, spare parts, safety gear and maintenance equipment to factories, hospitals and government agencies, and operates in Japan through MonotaRO.
h: Humanity Protocol (H) is a blockchain that verifies that each user is a unique human through Proof of Humanity, including palm scans. Its goal is to protect Web3 services from bots and fake accounts, and the H token is used in the network.
h-etf: Hyatt is a US hotel company based in Chicago whose first hotel opened in 1957 near Los Angeles airport. It manages and franchises brands such as Park Hyatt, Grand Hyatt, Andaz and Alila, plus all-inclusive resorts; the Pritzker family has long been its main owner.
h2o: H2O is the hub token of the Hydration Omnipool, a decentralized exchange in the Polkadot ecosystem that keeps all liquidity in one single pool. Every trade is routed through H2O, and trading fees and partial impermanent-loss protection are paid out in it.
haedal: Haedal Protocol is a liquid staking protocol on the Sui blockchain: users stake SUI and receive haSUI, a token they can keep using in DeFi while earning staking rewards. HAEDAL is the protocol's governance token.
hai: Hacken (HAI) is the token of Hacken, a blockchain cybersecurity company founded in Ukraine in 2017 that audits smart contracts and crypto exchanges. HAI is used within its security ecosystem and for rewards.
hair: HairDAO is a decentralized science (DeSci) community that funds and runs research into hair loss treatments. Members use the HAIR token to govern the DAO and share in the results of its research and products.
hal: Halliburton is one of the world's largest oilfield services companies, founded in 1919 and headquartered in Houston. It provides drilling, hydraulic fracturing, well cementing and reservoir evaluation services to oil and gas producers.
hal-in: Hindustan Aeronautics (HAL) is India's state-owned aerospace and defense manufacturer, based in Bengaluru and founded in 1940. It builds Tejas fighter jets, helicopters and aircraft engines and maintains Indian Air Force aircraft.
hana: Hana Network is a Web3 social and entertainment project backed by YZi Labs (formerly Binance Labs), known for its Hanafuda points game. It combines social features, NFTs and on-chain rewards on BNB Chain; HANA is its token.
hana-financial: Hana Financial Group is a South Korean financial group from Seoul and the parent company of Hana Bank. It offers banking, credit cards, brokerage, insurance and foreign-exchange services; Hana Bank is one of Korea's leaders in foreign exchange.
handy: HANDY is a blockchain games and content platform that rewards users with virtual assets. Its main product HandyPick is a prediction game where users guess event outcomes and earn bonuses, while advertisers reach an audience from different countries.
hanwha-aerospace: Hanwha Aerospace is a South Korean defence and aerospace manufacturer from Changwon, part of the Hanwha group. It builds K9 self-propelled howitzers, infantry fighting vehicles, aircraft engines and space systems, exporting to Poland and other European countries.
harold: Harold (HAROLD) is a memecoin inspired by "Hide the Pain Harold", the famous internet meme of a smiling older man whose expression hides discomfort. It is a community token built around humor.
has: Hasbro is a US toy and game company from Pawtucket, Rhode Island, founded in 1923. It owns brands such as Monopoly, Transformers, Nerf, Play-Doh, My Little Pony and Peppa Pig, plus Dungeons & Dragons and Magic: The Gathering through Wizards of the Coast.
hash: Provenance Blockchain is a public proof-of-stake layer-1 network built with the Cosmos SDK and launched in 2018, aimed at financial services such as loans, mortgages and fund administration. HASH is its native token for fees, staking and governance.
hava: HAVA is a crypto token on the Polygon network issued by HAVA Foundation Limited in Hong Kong. The project aims to link digital assets with real-world commerce: e-commerce apps, cross-border payments and digital vouchers.
hban: Huntington Bancshares is a regional banking group from Columbus, Ohio, founded in 1866. It serves consumers and businesses in the US Midwest with accounts, auto loans, mortgages, small-business lending and wealth management.
hbar: Hedera is a public network built on hashgraph technology, invented by Leemon Baird, for fast payments, tokenisation and enterprise apps. It is governed by a council of large companies including Google and IBM; HBAR pays fees and secures the network through staking.
hca: HCA Healthcare is the largest private hospital operator in the United States, based in Nashville, Tennessee, and founded in 1968. It runs hundreds of hospitals, surgery centers and urgent care clinics across the US and the UK.
hcltech: HCLTech is one of India's largest IT services companies, based in Noida near Delhi and part of the HCL group founded by Shiv Nadar in 1976. It provides software and engineering services, cloud and digital transformation, cybersecurity and its own software products to large companies around the world.
hd: Home Depot is the world's largest home improvement retail chain, founded in 1978 and based in Atlanta. It sells building materials, tools, garden equipment and household goods in the US, Canada and Mexico, serving both homeowners and professional builders.
hd-hyundai-heavy-industries: HD Hyundai Heavy Industries is one of the world's largest shipbuilders, based in Ulsan, South Korea, with roots going back to 1972. It builds tankers, LNG carriers, container ships and naval vessels, and also makes marine engines.
hdfcbank: HDFC Bank is India's largest private-sector bank, based in Mumbai and founded in 1994. It offers retail and corporate banking, credit cards and loans, and in 2023 it merged with its parent, the mortgage lender HDFC.
hdn: Hydranet (HDN) is a decentralized exchange built as a Layer 3 on Arbitrum, designed for trustless cross-chain swaps between native assets such as Bitcoin and Ethereum without wrapped tokens or custodians.
heatoil: Heating oil is a refined oil product used for home heating and closely related to diesel fuel. Its price follows crude oil and winter demand.
hei: Heidelberg Materials (formerly HeidelbergCement) is one of the world's largest cement makers, based in Heidelberg and founded in 1874. It produces cement, concrete and aggregates in more than 50 countries and is developing carbon capture technology.
hei-token: Heima is a blockchain project formerly known as Litentry, a parachain in the Polkadot ecosystem. After rebranding it focuses on chain abstraction and digital identity, so users can work across many blockchains with one account; HEI is the network token.
heia: Heineken is a Dutch brewer from Amsterdam, founded in 1864 by Gerard Adriaan Heineken. The world's second-largest brewer, it sells Heineken, Amstel, Desperados, Birra Moretti and Tiger beers and Strongbow cider in more than 190 countries.
hemi: Hemi is a modular blockchain protocol that joins Bitcoin and Ethereum into one "supernetwork"; one of its co-founders is early Bitcoin developer Jeff Garzik. Smart contracts on Hemi can see bitcoin data, and HEMI is used for staking and governance.
hen3: Henkel is a German consumer and industrial goods company based in Düsseldorf, founded in 1876. It is a world leader in adhesives, sealants and coatings for industry with brands such as Loctite and Technomelt, and sells household and beauty products such as Persil, Pril, Schwarzkopf and Fa; this listing is its preferred share.
hera: Hera Finance (HERA) is a multichain DEX aggregator that uses AI to search many decentralized exchanges and find the best route and price for swapping one token into another.
hero: Metahero is a project built around 3D scanning technology that turns real people and objects into ultra-realistic digital avatars and models for games, social media, fashion and the metaverse. HERO is the token on BNB Chain used to pay for scans and services.
hez: Hermez Network was a zero-knowledge rollup that made cheap, fast token transfers on top of Ethereum. In 2021 the project joined Polygon, became Polygon Hermez (later Polygon zkEVM), and HEZ holders could swap their tokens for MATIC.
hft: Hashflow is a multichain decentralised exchange where prices are quoted by professional market makers, which protects trades from slippage and front-running. It runs on Ethereum, Arbitrum, Solana, BNB Chain and other networks; HFT is the governance token.
hfun: Hypurr Fun (HFUN) is a token on Hyperliquid that was created as a test for the HypurrFun Telegram trading bot. It has no sale and no planned utility; its supply is capped at 1 million tokens, 30% of which went to PURR holders.
hig: The Hartford is an American insurance company based in Hartford, Connecticut, founded in 1810 and known for its stag logo. It sells property and casualty insurance for small and large businesses, workers' compensation, group benefits such as disability and life cover, and auto and home insurance including the AARP program.
hikvision: Hikvision is a Chinese video surveillance maker from Hangzhou, founded in 2001. It is one of the world's largest suppliers of security cameras, video recorders and security systems and also sells home products under the EZVIZ brand.
hims-token: Hims & Hers Health, Inc. • Robinhood Token is a tokenized version of Hims & Hers shares issued by Robinhood for its customers in the European Union. It follows the price of the US-listed stock and can be traded around the clock on a blockchain.
hindunilvr: Hindustan Unilever is India's largest consumer goods company, based in Mumbai and a subsidiary of Britain's Unilever. It makes soaps, shampoos, laundry products, tea and foods under brands such as Lux, Dove, Surf Excel, Brooke Bond and Lipton.
hitachi: Hitachi is a Japanese industrial and technology conglomerate based in Tokyo, founded in 1910. It develops digital IT solutions (Lumada), power equipment and electricity grids, railway systems and industrial automation.
hive: Hive is a blockchain that split from Steem in 2020 after the community rejected Justin Sun's takeover of Steemit. It rewards authors and readers for content, transactions on the network carry no fees, and it hosts the social network PeakD and the game Splinterlands.
hkex: HKEX (Hong Kong Exchanges and Clearing) operates the Hong Kong stock exchange, its futures market and clearing houses. It also owns the London Metal Exchange (LME), and the Stock Connect programme links it with the Shanghai and Shenzhen exchanges.
hlt: Hilton Worldwide is a US hotel company based in McLean, Virginia, founded by Conrad Hilton in 1919. It manages and franchises thousands of hotels worldwide under brands such as Hilton, Waldorf Astoria, Conrad, DoubleTree and Hampton.
hmm: Thinking Cat (HMM) is a meme coin. Like most meme coins, it is not backed by a business or assets, and its price is driven mainly by community attention and trading.
hmstr: Hamster Kombat is a tap-to-earn game in Telegram where players run a virtual crypto exchange as a hamster CEO. It became one of the most-played Telegram games in 2024; HMSTR is its token, distributed to players in an airdrop on the TON blockchain.
hnr1: Hannover Re is one of the world's largest reinsurers, based in Hanover, Germany, and founded in 1966. It insures other insurance companies against big risks such as natural catastrophes, as well as property, casualty, life and health policies; its majority owner is the German insurance group Talanx.
hnt: Helium (HNT) is a decentralized wireless network where people install hotspots and earn tokens for providing coverage. It first served IoT devices and now develops the Helium Mobile cellular service; since 2023 it has run on the Solana blockchain.
ho: Thales is a French defense and aerospace company from Paris. It makes radars, air defense systems, communications equipment, avionics and satellites, as well as cybersecurity and digital identity products such as SIM cards and passport chips.
hogs: Lean hogs is a futures contract on the price of pork carcasses in the United States. It is driven by feed costs, exports to Asia and animal diseases.
hollar: HOLLAR (Hydrated Dollar) is a decentralized dollar stablecoin from Hydration, the DeFi network on Polkadot formerly known as HydraDX. Users mint HOLLAR by borrowing against crypto collateral in Hydration's money market.
holn: Holcim is a Swiss cement and building materials maker from Zug, founded in 1912 in the village of Holderbank. It produces cement, concrete, aggregates and roofing in dozens of countries; in 2025 it spun off its North American business as Amrize.
holo: Holoworld (HOLO) is a platform for creating AI-agent virtual characters without coding: they can chat, livestream and interact with people across social networks. The project is developed by the studio Hologram Labs, and HOLO is the ecosystem token.
home: HOME is the token of DeFi App, an app that brings trading, swaps and yield across different blockchains into one interface without gas or complex setup. HOME holders take part in governance and get benefits on the platform.
hon: Honeywell is a US industrial conglomerate headquartered in Charlotte, North Carolina, with roots going back to the late 19th century. It makes avionics and aircraft engines, building and factory automation systems, sensors and industrial software.
hon-hai: Hon Hai Precision Industry, better known as Foxconn, is a Taiwanese company based in New Taipei, founded in 1974 by Terry Gou. It is the world's largest contract electronics maker, assembling iPhones and other devices for Apple and many brands, and builds AI servers.
hona: Honeywell Aerospace is a US maker of aviation and defense systems, separated from the Honeywell conglomerate into its own company. It produces avionics, radars, navigation and flight control systems, auxiliary power units and engines for planes, helicopters and spacecraft.
honda: Honda Motor is a Japanese car and motorcycle maker from Tokyo, founded by Soichiro Honda in 1948. It is the world's largest motorcycle maker and also builds Honda and Acura cars, engines, generators and the HondaJet business jet.
honey: HONEY is the token of Hivemapper, a decentralized mapping network on Solana. Drivers mount Hivemapper dashcams in their cars to collect street-level imagery for a constantly updated world map and earn HONEY for their contributions, while companies pay to use the map data.
hood: Robinhood Markets is a US fintech company based in Menlo Park, California, founded in 2013. Its app popularised commission-free stock trading and also offers crypto and options trading, retirement accounts and credit cards.
hookr: Hookr.fun (HOOKR) is a token-launch platform on Robinhood Chain, the blockchain network started by the US trading app Robinhood. Anyone can create and trade new tokens there, and HOOKR is the platform's own token.
hopr: HOPR is a privacy protocol from Switzerland that runs a decentralized mixnet, hiding who is talking to whom when data moves across the internet. People who run HOPR nodes relay traffic and earn HOPR tokens for it.
hot: Holo (HOT) is the token of Holo, a project building hosting for apps on Holochain, a platform for distributed applications that does not use a classic blockchain. Computer owners can rent out space and processing power for hosting and earn rewards.
hoya: HOYA is a Japanese company from Tokyo, founded in 1941 as an optical glass maker. It makes eyeglass lenses, contact lenses, medical endoscopes (Pentax Medical), and photomasks and glass substrates for electronics.
hp: Hippo Protocol (HP) is a layer-1 blockchain built for healthcare. It aims to let patients and medical organizations store and share health data securely under the patient's control, and HP is the network's native token.
hpe: Hewlett Packard Enterprise is a US technology company based in Houston, spun off from Hewlett-Packard in 2015. It sells servers, data storage systems, Aruba and Juniper networking equipment and cloud services to businesses.
hpl: HyperLend (HPL) is the token of HyperLend, a decentralized lending and borrowing protocol on HyperEVM, the smart-contract layer of the Hyperliquid blockchain. Users deposit crypto to earn interest or borrow against their collateral.
hpp: House Party Protocol (HPP) is a Layer 2 blockchain network built for AI applications by the team behind Aergo from South Korea. Aergo tokens move to HPP, which is used to pay network fees, stake and vote.
hpq: HP Inc. is a US maker of laptops, PCs and printers from Palo Alto, successor to Hewlett-Packard, which was founded in a garage in 1939. It sells computers, printers and ink, HyperX gaming gear and Poly hybrid-work devices.
hsbc-holdings: HSBC is a British-Asian banking group headquartered in London, founded in 1865 in Hong Kong as the Hongkong and Shanghai Banking Corporation. One of the world's largest banks, it earns most of its profit in Asia, especially Hong Kong.
hsk: HashKey Platform Token (HSK) is the ecosystem token of HashKey, a Hong Kong financial group that runs a licensed crypto exchange. It is used on the HashKey Chain network and to reward participants in the ecosystem.
hst: Host Hotels & Resorts is the largest US lodging real estate investment trust (REIT), based in Bethesda, Maryland, and was spun off from Marriott in 1993. It owns luxury and upper-upscale hotels run under brands such as Marriott, Ritz-Carlton, Hyatt, Hilton and Four Seasons.
hsy: The Hershey Company is an American maker of chocolate and sweets from Hershey, Pennsylvania, founded by Milton Hershey in 1894. It is known for Hershey's bars, Reese's, Kit Kat (in the US) and snacks such as SkinnyPop.
ht: Huobi Token (HT) is the exchange token of Huobi, a crypto exchange founded in Beijing in 2013 by Leon Li that renamed itself HTX in 2023. The token gave discounts on trading fees and access to exchange services.
htm: Hatom (HTM) is the token of Hatom, a DeFi protocol on the MultiversX blockchain. Its main products are a lending and borrowing market and liquid staking of EGLD; HTM is used for governance and rewards.
htr: Hathor (HTR) is the coin of Hathor Network, a layer-1 blockchain that combines a DAG structure with a classic blockchain. It is known for letting anyone create tokens in a few clicks without writing smart contracts, and it is merge-mined with Bitcoin.
htx: HTX is the governance token of HTX DAO, the ecosystem around the HTX crypto exchange (formerly Huobi), which is linked to Justin Sun. Token holders vote on the project's development and get perks in the exchange's services.
hubb: Hubbell is a US maker of electrical equipment based in Connecticut, founded in 1888 by Harvey Hubbell, inventor of the detachable electric plug. It makes power-grid components, outlets, switches, lighting and wiring systems.
hum: Humana is a US health insurer from Louisville, Kentucky, founded in 1961. It is one of the largest providers of Medicare Advantage plans for older Americans and runs clinics, pharmacies and home care through CenterWell.
huma: Huma Finance is a PayFi network that provides liquidity for payments and receivables financing on blockchain, notably on Solana. It lets users earn from real-world payment flows; HUMA is the governance token.
hunt: HUNT is the token of Hunt Town, a South Korean team of builders behind Steemhunt and the Mint Club token-creation platform. On Mint Club anyone can launch tokens priced by a bonding curve, often using HUNT as the reserve asset.
hwm: Howmet Aerospace is a US company based in Pittsburgh that makes engineered metal parts for aircraft engines and airframes, such as turbine blades, fasteners and structural components, plus forged aluminum wheels for trucks. It was spun out of Arconic, the former Alcoa, in 2020.
hype: Hyperliquid is its own layer-1 blockchain, best known for the decentralised exchange of the same name for perpetual futures and spot trading. HYPE is used for staking, fees and governance; the project is led by Jeff Yan.
hyper: Hyperlane is a permissionless interoperability protocol: anyone can connect their blockchain and send messages and tokens across dozens of networks. HYPER is the token for staking and governance.
hyundai-mobis: Hyundai Mobis is a South Korean auto parts maker from Seoul and a key company of Hyundai Motor Group. It produces chassis and cockpit modules, safety systems, electronics and electric-vehicle components, and supplies spare parts for Hyundai and Kia.
hyundai-motor: Hyundai Motor is South Korea's largest carmaker, headquartered in Seoul and founded in 1967. It builds Hyundai cars and the premium Genesis brand, ranks with Kia among the world's three largest car groups and owns Boston Dynamics.
