iag-token: Iagon is a decentralized storage and computing platform built mainly on Cardano. People and businesses rent out spare disk space and processing power to the network, and the IAG token pays for these services and rewards providers.
ibe: Iberdrola is a Spanish energy company from Bilbao and one of the world's largest producers of wind and solar power. It owns power grids in Spain, the United Kingdom (ScottishPower), the United States (Avangrid) and Brazil (Neoenergia) and supplies electricity to millions of customers.
ibit: iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) is BlackRock's spot bitcoin ETF, launched in 2024. It lets investors own bitcoin through a regular brokerage account without a crypto wallet.
ibkr: Interactive Brokers is a US online broker based in Greenwich, Connecticut, founded by Thomas Peterffy. It gives access to stocks, options, futures, currencies and bonds on hundreds of exchanges in dozens of countries and is known for low fees for active traders.
ibm: IBM is an American technology company based in Armonk, New York, founded in 1911. Once a leader in mainframes and personal computers, it now sells Red Hat hybrid cloud, enterprise software, the watsonx AI platform and consulting, and develops quantum computers.
ibs: IBS is the algorithmic token of POTS Money, a modular DeFi protocol. IBS is not a stablecoin: it is minted through collateralized debt as users bond and stake, and the ecosystem adds payments, lending, auctions and AI tools for yield strategies.
icbc: ICBC (Industrial and Commercial Bank of China) is a state-owned Chinese bank based in Beijing and one of the largest banks in the world by assets. Founded in 1984, it serves hundreds of millions of customers and large companies; its H shares trade in Hong Kong.
icbc-cn: ICBC (A shares) are shares of Industrial and Commercial Bank of China traded on the Shanghai Stock Exchange. The state-owned Beijing bank, founded in 1984, is one of the world's largest and serves individuals, companies and the government through thousands of branches.
ice: Intercontinental Exchange is a US operator of exchanges and financial data based in Atlanta, founded in 2000 by Jeffrey Sprecher. It owns the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) and the ICE futures exchanges, and provides mortgage technology and data services.
icicibank: ICICI Bank is one of India's largest private-sector banks, based in Mumbai and founded in 1994. It offers retail, corporate and investment banking, and through subsidiaries also insurance and asset management.
icln: iShares Global Clean Energy (ICLN) invests worldwide in solar, wind and other clean-energy companies.
icnt: Impossible Cloud Network (ICNT) is a decentralized protocol for business cloud services: storage, compute and networking. Hardware owners contribute resources and service providers use them; ICNT is needed for node collateral, access to resources and staking.
icp: Internet Computer is a blockchain from the Swiss DFINITY Foundation (Zurich), founded by Dominic Williams, launched in 2021. The network lets websites, services and AI agents run entirely on-chain without ordinary cloud servers; ICP pays for computation.
icx: ICON is a South Korean blockchain project launched in 2017–2018 with the goal of connecting separate blockchains so they can exchange data and value, and it later built cross-chain messaging tools for other networks. ICX is the network's coin, used for fees, staking and governance.
id: SPACE ID (ID) is a universal domain name service for Web3: users register and trade domains such as .bnb or .arb that replace long wallet addresses. The project was backed by Binance Labs, and ID is its governance token.
idle: IdleMine (IDLE) is the token of a play-to-earn mobile game where players hold a thumb on the screen to mine rewards, fight 1v1 battles against others, and collect daily login bonuses and loot crates.
idol: MEET48 (IDOL) is a Web3 entertainment platform about virtual and real idols that combines AI, live streaming and game mechanics. Fans support their favorite performers and take part in shows, and the IDOL token serves as the ecosystem's currency.
idxx: IDEXX Laboratories is a US company from Westbrook, Maine, founded in 1983. It is the world leader in veterinary diagnostics, making analyzers and tests for clinics that treat cats and dogs, plus tests for livestock, milk and drinking water.
iex: IDEX Corporation is a US industrial company from Northbrook, Illinois, founded in 1988. It makes specialized pumps, flow meters, fluidics for lab and medical instruments, fire and rescue equipment such as the Hurst Jaws of Life, and precision optics.
ifc: Intact Financial is Canada's largest property and casualty insurer, headquartered in Toronto. It insures cars, homes and businesses and also operates in the United States, the United Kingdom and Ireland.
iff: International Flavors & Fragrances (IFF) is a New York-based company whose roots go back to 1889. It creates flavors and scents for food, drinks, perfumes and household products, and also makes food ingredients, enzymes and probiotics.
ifx: Infineon Technologies is Germany's largest chipmaker, based in Neubiberg near Munich and spun off from Siemens in 1999. It makes power chips and microcontrollers for cars, electric vehicles, solar inverters, industry and bank cards.
ilmn: Illumina is an American company from San Diego and the world leader in DNA sequencing technology. Labs, hospitals and scientists use its instruments and reagents to read genomes, diagnose cancer and run genetic research.
ilv: Illuvium is an open-world Web3 game where players explore a planet, capture creatures called Illuvials and battle in an auto-battler. The project was founded by brothers Kieran and Aaron Warwick; ILV is used for governance and rewards.
imo: IMO is the token of a real-estate investment project that aims to let anyone earn monthly passive income from property, whatever the amount invested. Income from the properties the company owns is shared with token holders.
imu: Immunefi (IMU) is the token of Immunefi, a leading bug bounty and security platform for Web3. Projects pay security researchers through it for finding vulnerabilities in their smart contracts before hackers do.
imx: Immutable (IMX) is a blockchain gaming platform from Sydney, Australia, that runs the Ethereum layer-2 networks Immutable X and Immutable zkEVM. They let players trade in-game NFTs without paying gas fees; IMX is used for fees, staking and governance.
in: INFINIT is an AI-powered DeFi intelligence protocol that lets anyone discover, compare and execute DeFi opportunities through AI agents and plain-language requests instead of navigating many apps by hand. IN is the protocol's token.
inc: WorldAssets (INC) is an Ethereum-based DeFi project focused on real-world assets (RWA): it aims to bring traditional assets on-chain as tokens that can be held and traded like crypto.
incy: Incyte is a US biopharmaceutical company from Delaware. It develops medicines for blood cancers and inflammatory and autoimmune diseases; its main drug is Jakafi (ruxolitinib), and it also sells Opzelura cream for vitiligo and eczema.
index: INDEX is the governance token of Index Coop, a community that creates crypto index and strategy tokens such as the DeFi Pulse Index (DPI). Holders vote on new products, fees and how the treasury is used.
indy: Indigo Protocol (INDY) is the governance token of Indigo, a DeFi protocol on Cardano for synthetic assets called iAssets, such as iUSD and iBTC. Users mint iAssets against ADA collateral, and INDY holders vote on the protocol.
infi: infiniFi is an on-chain banking protocol with dollar yield products: deposits are spread across strategies of different durations, similar to how banks manage assets and liabilities. INFI is the protocol's token.
infy: Infosys is an Indian IT company from Bengaluru, founded in 1981 by seven engineers led by N. R. Narayana Murthy. It provides software development, digital transformation, cloud and consulting services to large companies worldwide.
inga: ING Group is a Dutch banking group headquartered in Amsterdam, formed in 1991. It serves millions of retail customers across Europe and beyond, known for its digital-first banking, and also provides wholesale banking to large companies.
init: Initia is a blockchain network that joins many optimistic rollups into one interconnected system. Developers launch their own app-specific chains that can easily talk to each other; INIT is used for staking and governance.
inj: Injective is a layer-1 blockchain built with the Cosmos SDK for financial apps such as exchanges, derivatives and tokenized assets. It gives developers ready-made trading modules; INJ is used for staking, governance and paying network fees.
insm: Insmed is a US biopharmaceutical company from New Jersey. It develops medicines for rare lung diseases, including the inhaled antibiotic Arikayce and brensocatib for bronchiectasis.
intc: Intel is a US chipmaker based in Santa Clara, California, founded in 1968 by Robert Noyce and Gordon Moore. It is known for Core and Xeon processors for PCs and servers and is building a contract chip-manufacturing business, Intel Foundry.
intc-token: Intel • Robinhood Token is a tokenized version of Intel shares issued by Robinhood for its customers in the European Union. It follows the price of the US-listed stock and can be traded around the clock on a blockchain.
inter: Inter Milan Fan Token (INTER) is the official fan token of FC Internazionale Milano, the Italian football club founded in 1908. Issued on the Chiliz blockchain via the Socios.com app, it lets fans vote in club polls and get rewards and experiences.
intu: Intuit is a US financial software company based in Mountain View, California, founded in 1983. It makes TurboTax for filing taxes, QuickBooks accounting for small businesses, the Credit Karma personal finance app and the Mailchimp email marketing service.
inv: Inverse Finance (INV) is the governance token of Inverse Finance, a DeFi project on Ethereum that issues the DOLA stablecoin and runs FiRM, a lending market with fixed borrowing rates. INV holders vote on the protocol and can stake it.
inx: Infinex (INX) is the token of Infinex, a crypto platform founded by Synthetix creator Kain Warwick. It aims to feel as simple as a centralized exchange while users keep control of their own funds across many blockchains.
io: io.net (IO) is a decentralized GPU network on Solana that pools graphics cards from data centers, mining farms and private computers into clusters for machine learning. AI engineers rent computing power for less than in regular clouds; IO is used for payments and rewards.
iost: IOST is a high-throughput blockchain platform launched in 2019 by a team backed by Sequoia and Matrix. It uses its own Proof of Believability consensus and focuses on fast, cheap decentralized apps.
iota: IOTA is an open-source blockchain project run by the Berlin-based IOTA Foundation and founded in 2015. Originally built for the Internet of Things, it now focuses on digital identity, trade data and tokenization; the IOTA token pays fees and is used for staking.
iotx: IoTeX is a blockchain platform launched in 2017 that connects real-world devices to blockchain and AI. It feeds verified data from sensors, cars and gadgets into decentralized apps and develops the DePIN sector; IOTX is the network's native coin.
ip: International Paper is a US packaging maker based in Memphis, Tennessee, founded in 1898 and one of the world's largest producers of paper-based packaging. It makes containerboard and corrugated boxes for e-commerce, food and industry, and bought Britain's DS Smith in 2025.
iq: IQ is the token of IQ.wiki (formerly Everipedia), the largest blockchain-based encyclopedia about crypto. The project also develops AI agents through its IQ AI platform, and the token is used for governance and rewards for editors.
iqv: IQVIA is a US company from North Carolina that runs clinical trials of new medicines for pharmaceutical companies and sells healthcare data and analytics. It was formed in 2016 by the merger of Quintiles and IMS Health.
ir: Ingersoll Rand is an American industrial equipment maker from Davidson, North Carolina, with a history dating to the 19th century. It makes compressors, vacuum pumps, blowers and fluid-handling systems for factories, healthcare and energy.
irm: Iron Mountain is an American real estate investment trust (REIT) from Boston, founded in 1951. It stores paper archives and records for thousands of companies in dozens of countries, shreds confidential documents and also builds and leases data centers.
irys: Irys (IRYS) is a layer-1 blockchain that combines data storage with smart-contract execution, formerly known as Bundlr. It is designed for large volumes of data for AI and Web3 applications.
islm: Islamic Coin (ISLM) is the native coin of the HAQQ network, an Ethereum-compatible blockchain from Dubai designed to follow Sharia principles. Part of newly issued coins goes to the Evergreen DAO, which funds Islamic charity and community projects.
isp: Intesa Sanpaolo is Italy's largest bank, formed in 2007 by the merger of Banca Intesa and Sanpaolo IMI and headquartered in Turin. It serves millions of customers in Italy and Central and Eastern Europe and runs a large insurance and asset management business.
isrg: Intuitive Surgical is a California company founded in 1995 and a pioneer of robotic surgery. Its da Vinci system lets surgeons perform minimally invasive operations with robotic arms; the company earns money from instruments and service.
ita: iShares U.S. Aerospace & Defense (ITA) invests in American defence contractors and aerospace companies that build aircraft, missiles and space systems.
itc: ITC is an Indian conglomerate based in Kolkata, founded in 1910 as the Imperial Tobacco Company of India. It is the country's largest cigarette maker (Gold Flake, Classic) and a big packaged-foods company with brands such as Aashirvaad flour, Sunfeast biscuits and Bingo! snacks, and it also makes paperboard and packaging and runs agri-business.
itochu: Itochu is a Japanese trading house based in Tokyo and Osaka, founded in 1858 as a textile merchant. It trades and invests in apparel, food, natural resources, machinery and retail, and owns the FamilyMart convenience store chain.
itsa4: Itaúsa is a Brazilian holding company from São Paulo and the largest shareholder of the bank Itaú Unibanco. It also holds stakes in Alpargatas (Havaianas), Dexco, NTS gas pipelines, Copa Energia and Motiva (formerly CCR).
itt: ITT is a US industrial manufacturer based in Stamford, Connecticut, in its current form since a 2011 split of the old ITT Corporation. It makes brake pads and KONI shock absorbers for vehicles and trains, industrial pumps and valves, and connectors for aerospace, defense and industry.
itub4: Itaú Unibanco is the largest private bank in Brazil and Latin America, headquartered in São Paulo and formed in 2008 by the merger of Itaú and Unibanco. It offers retail, corporate and investment banking, credit cards, insurance and asset management.
itw: Illinois Tool Works is a US industrial manufacturer based in Glenview, Illinois, founded in 1912. It runs seven businesses, from car components and welding equipment to commercial kitchen equipment, construction fasteners and polymers.
itx: Inditex is a Spanish fashion giant from Galicia founded by Amancio Ortega, owner of the chains Zara, Pull&Bear, Massimo Dutti, Bershka, Stradivarius and Oysho. It is known for fast fashion: new collections reach thousands of stores worldwide within weeks.
ivv: iShares Core S&P 500 (IVV) is BlackRock's low-cost ETF on the S&P 500 index and one of the largest ETFs in the world.
iwm: iShares Russell 2000 (IWM) tracks the Russell 2000 index of small US companies. It is more sensitive to the economy and interest rates than the S&P 500.
ixs: IXS is the token of IX Swap, a platform for tokenized real-world assets and security tokens. Companies raise capital through its launchpad, and investors buy and trade tokenized shares, real estate and other assets after identity checks.
j: Jacobs Solutions is a US engineering and consulting firm based in Dallas, founded in 1947. It plans, designs and manages infrastructure projects such as water systems, transport and energy, as well as advanced facilities like data centers and pharmaceutical plants.
jagent: JAGENT is a token on BNB Chain from the Jager project (jager.live), focused on AI agents — software bots that perform tasks automatically. It belongs to the Jager community ecosystem alongside the Jager Hunter meme coin.
jager: Jager Hunter (JAGER) is a meme coin on BNB Chain. Like most meme coins, it is not backed by a business or assets, and its price is driven mainly by community attention and trading.
japan-tobacco: Japan Tobacco (JT) is a Tokyo-based tobacco maker and one of the largest in the world. Through JT International it sells Winston, Camel, Mevius and LD cigarettes and Ploom heated-tobacco products, and it also has pharmaceutical and food businesses.
jasmy: JasmyCoin is the token of Jasmy, a Tokyo-based Japanese company founded by former Sony executives. Jasmy builds an Internet of Things platform where users keep control of their own personal data; JASMY is an ERC-20 token on Ethereum.
jbht: J.B. Hunt Transport Services is one of the largest US freight companies, based in Lowell, Arkansas, and founded in 1961 by Johnnie Bryan Hunt. It is best known for intermodal shipping (containers moved by rail and truck) and also runs dedicated truck fleets and home delivery of bulky goods.
jbl: Jabil is a US contract electronics manufacturer from St. Petersburg, Florida, founded in 1966. It builds products for other brands, including data-centre hardware, smartphone components, medical devices, car electronics and packaging.
jci: Johnson Controls is a global company headquartered in Cork, Ireland, whose story began in the US in 1885 when Warren Johnson invented the electric thermostat. It makes heating, ventilation and air-conditioning, fire and security systems and smart-building software.
jct: Janction is a platform for sharing resources for AI products: GPU computing power, storage and images. Users can rent or lease out these resources, and the JCT token is used for settlements in the network.
jd-com: JD.com is a Chinese e-commerce company from Beijing, founded in 1998 by Liu Qiangdong (Richard Liu). It sells electronics, appliances and everyday goods and runs its own logistics network, JD Logistics, with warehouses and delivery across China.
jellyjelly: Jelly-My-Jelly (JELLYJELLY) is a meme token on Solana linked to the video app JellyJelly, created by Venmo co-founder Iqram Magdon-Ismail. The token became a symbol of the app's community and trades as a meme asset.
jepi: JPMorgan Equity Premium Income (JEPI) holds S&P 500 stocks and sells options on them to pay a high monthly income, giving up part of the upside in return.
jepq: JPMorgan Nasdaq Equity Premium Income (JEPQ) holds Nasdaq-100 stocks and sells options to fund monthly payouts, trading some growth for income.
jett: JETT is a cryptocurrency project that presents itself as a way to decentralize finance and give users more control over their money, with the stated goal of supporting space exploration efforts.
jeur: Jarvis Synthetic Euro (jEUR) is a synthetic stablecoin from Jarvis Network designed to track the value of one euro. It is minted against USDC collateral and is used mainly in decentralized finance on networks such as Polygon for euro payments, swaps and lending.
jiangsu-hengrui: Jiangsu Hengrui Medicine is one of China's largest drugmakers, based in Lianyungang, Jiangsu province. It makes medicines for cancer, anesthesia and cardiovascular disease and actively develops its own innovative drugs.
jll: JLL (Jones Lang LaSalle) is a global commercial real estate services firm headquartered in Chicago, formed in 1999 by the merger of Jones Lang Wootton and LaSalle Partners. It helps companies and investors lease, buy, sell and manage offices, warehouses and other property, and runs the investment manager LaSalle.
jmpt: JumpToken (JMPT) is the token of JumpTask, an online gig marketplace where companies post small tasks and people around the world complete them for crypto payments, including those without a bank account. The token runs on BNB Chain.
jnj: Johnson & Johnson is a US healthcare company based in New Brunswick, New Jersey, founded in 1886. It develops prescription drugs for oncology, immunology and neuroscience, plus medical devices for surgery and cardiology; its consumer brands were spun off as Kenvue in 2023.
jobcoin: JobCoin (JOBCOIN) is a memecoin on Solana built around the joke of escaping the 9-to-5 job and retiring early thanks to crypto. It has no product: its value rests on workplace-humor memes and an active community.
joe: JOE is the token of LFJ (formerly Trader Joe), a decentralized exchange running on Avalanche, Arbitrum and BNB Chain. The exchange is known for its Liquidity Book liquidity model; JOE is used for staking and governance.
joff: Chomolon Joff (JOFF) is a community meme coin from the Hyperliquid ecosystem. It celebrates the culture of fast-moving on-chain traders and positions itself as a symbol of the Hyperliquid movement, without venture-capital backing.
jpm: JPMorgan Chase is the largest US bank, headquartered in New York, with roots going back to 1799. It serves millions of customers under the Chase brand and runs investment banking, asset management and payments for big companies; it is led by Jamie Dimon.
jpyc: JPY Coin (JPYC) is a Japanese yen stablecoin from Tokyo-based JPYC Inc. Each token is designed to be worth one yen and redeemable for yen, and it runs on public blockchains such as Ethereum, Polygon and Avalanche.
jst: JUST (JST) is the governance token of the JUST decentralized finance ecosystem on the TRON blockchain, linked to Justin Sun. The platform includes the JustLend lending service and stablecoin tools, and JST holders vote on protocol settings.
jswsteel: JSW Steel is one of India's largest steelmakers, based in Mumbai and the flagship of Sajjan Jindal's JSW Group. It produces hot-rolled, cold-rolled, galvanized and long steel products for construction, cars and industry.
jto: JTO is the governance token of Jito Network, a key piece of Solana infrastructure. Jito offers liquid staking of SOL through the JitoSOL token and a modified validator client that lets validators and stakers earn extra income from MEV.
jup: Jupiter is the largest token-swap aggregator on Solana: it searches across decentralized exchanges for the best rate. It also offers perpetual futures, limit orders and new token launches; JUP is the governance token.
juv: Juventus Fan Token (JUV) is the fan token of Italian football club Juventus of Turin on the Socios.com platform (Chiliz blockchain). Holders vote in club polls, take part in quizzes and earn rewards.
kag: Kinesis Silver (KAG) is a silver-backed token from the Kinesis platform: each token represents one troy ounce of investment-grade silver held in insured vaults. It can be spent, transferred or redeemed, and holders receive a share of platform fees.
kaia: Kaia is an Ethereum-compatible layer-1 blockchain formed in 2024 by merging the Klaytn (from Kakao) and Finschia (from LINE) networks. It aims to bring Web3 to millions of users in Asia directly inside the KakaoTalk and LINE messengers; KAIA is its native coin.
kaio: KAIO (formerly Libre Capital) is a platform for tokenizing institutional funds: it issues on-chain shares of funds from large asset managers, opening them up to crypto investors. The project runs on networks including Hedera and has received funding from Tether; KAIO is the governance token.
kaito: KAITO is the token of Kaito, a platform that uses AI to collect and analyze crypto news, social media and discussions. Its InfoFi network rewards content creators and researchers for the attention they attract; KAITO is used for rewards, staking and governance.
kan: KAN is the token of BitKan, a long-running Chinese crypto platform that started as an information and community app for Bitcoin users and grew into trading services. KAN is used for fees, rewards and perks inside BitKan.
kas: Kaspa is a Proof of Work cryptocurrency launched in November 2021 with no premine or presale. It uses a BlockDAG structure (the GHOSTDAG protocol), which lets blocks be created in parallel and confirms transfers very quickly.
kat: Katana is a DeFi-focused blockchain incubated by Polygon Labs and GSR, built to concentrate liquidity for trading and lending. Holders lock KAT to receive vKAT, which gives votes on how rewards and capital are directed across the network.
kau: Kinesis Gold (KAU) is a gold-backed token from the Kinesis platform: each token represents one gram of investment-grade gold held in insured vaults. Holders can spend, transfer or redeem it and receive a share of the platform's fees as a yield.
kava: Kava (KAVA) is a layer-1 blockchain that connects the Ethereum and Cosmos ecosystems and offers DeFi services that work like a decentralized bank, such as lending and stablecoins. KAVA is used for staking, fees and governance.
kb-financial: KB Financial Group is one of South Korea's largest financial groups, based in Seoul. Its core business is KB Kookmin Bank, one of the country's biggest banks, and it also runs credit cards, securities, insurance and asset-management companies serving millions of Korean customers.
kbank: Kasikornbank (KBank) is one of Thailand's largest commercial banks, based in Bangkok and founded in 1945 as Thai Farmers Bank. It serves individuals, small businesses and corporations and is known for its K PLUS mobile banking app.
kcs: KuCoin Token (KCS) is the native token of KuCoin, an international crypto exchange founded in 2017. Holders get discounts on trading fees and a share of bonuses, and KCS also pays fees on the KCC network.
kct: Konnect (KCT) is a blockchain project that links a lifestyle membership with an e-commerce platform in a B2B2C model. Members use the KCT token for benefits across shopping, travel, tourism and cultural services from partner businesses.
kda: Kadena is a proof-of-work blockchain founded in 2016 by former JPMorgan engineers Stuart Popejoy and Will Martino. Its Chainweb design runs many chains in parallel to raise capacity, and it uses its own safety-focused smart-contract language, Pact. In 2025 the Kadena company announced it was winding down, while the network continues with its miners and community.
kddi: KDDI is Japan's second-largest telecom company, based in Tokyo. It provides mobile service under the au, UQ mobile and povo brands, home internet, and financial, energy and corporate IT services.
kdp: Keurig Dr Pepper is a US beverage company based in Burlington, Massachusetts, and Frisco, Texas, formed in 2018 by merging Keurig and Dr Pepper Snapple. It sells Dr Pepper, 7UP and Canada Dry sodas plus Keurig coffee makers and K-Cup pods.
keep: Keep Network (KEEP) was an Ethereum project that stored and processed private data off-chain in 'keeps' protected by secure multi-party computation, and it created the bitcoin bridge tBTC. In 2022 it merged with NuCypher into Threshold Network, and KEEP can be swapped for the T token.
kekius: Kekius Maximus is a memecoin named after the joke name Elon Musk briefly used on his X profile at the end of 2024. The project is community-driven and has no function beyond the meme.
ker-fr: Kering is a French luxury group from Paris controlled by the Pinault family. It owns the fashion houses Gucci, Saint Laurent, Bottega Veneta and Balenciaga and the jewellers Boucheron and Pomellato.
kernel: KernelDAO is an ecosystem of restaking products on Ethereum and BNB Chain: the Kelp liquid restaking protocol, Kernel infrastructure and the Gain yield vaults. The KERNEL token is used for governance and staking.
key: KeyCorp is a US regional banking group from Cleveland, Ohio, and the parent of KeyBank. It serves individuals and businesses in around 15 states with accounts, loans, mortgages and investment banking for mid-sized companies.
keycat: Keyboard Cat (KEYCAT) is a memecoin on Base inspired by the viral 'Keyboard Cat' video of a cat in a shirt playing a keyboard. It is a community token with no utility beyond trading.
keyence: Keyence is a Japanese industrial automation company based in Osaka, founded in 1974. It develops sensors, machine vision systems, measuring instruments and microscopes, runs without its own factories, and is known for exceptionally high profitability.
keys: Keysight Technologies is a US company from Santa Rosa, California, spun off from Agilent in 2014 and originally rooted in Hewlett-Packard. It makes oscilloscopes, analyzers and software for designing and testing electronics, 5G networks, chips and automotive systems.
kgen: KGeN is a Web3 gaming platform that builds a network of verified real players and lets game publishers reach a live audience instead of bots. The project has a strong presence in India; KGEN is the ecosystem token.
kgst: KGST is a stablecoin pegged 1:1 to the Kyrgyz som and fully backed by reserves. It is designed as a digital form of the som for fast, transparent payments and transfers in Kyrgyzstan and the wider Central Asian region.
khc: Kraft Heinz is one of the largest food makers in North America, formed in 2015 by merging Kraft and Heinz with backing from Berkshire Hathaway and 3G Capital. Its brands include Heinz ketchup, Philadelphia cream cheese, Kraft Mac & Cheese, Oscar Mayer and Lunchables.
kia: Kia is a South Korean carmaker from Seoul, founded in 1944 and part of Hyundai Motor Group since 1998. It builds cars, SUVs and electric vehicles such as the EV series at plants in Korea, the US, Europe and India.
kii: KiiChain (KII) is a layer-1 blockchain built for emerging markets, especially Latin America. It focuses on stablecoin payments, currency exchange and tokenizing real-world assets for local businesses.
kim: Kimco Realty is a US real estate investment trust (REIT) from Jericho, New York, founded in 1958. It owns and operates open-air shopping centers anchored by grocery stores, mostly in major US metro areas.
kishu: Kishu Inu (KISHU) is a dog-themed memecoin on Ethereum launched in 2021, during the wave of coins inspired by Dogecoin and Shiba Inu. It is driven by its community and has no utility beyond trading.
kite: Kite is a blockchain for the "agentic economy", where AI agents can make payments on their own and securely. The network supports the x402 standard that lets machines pay for online services; KITE is its native token for staking and fees.
kkr: KKR & Co. is a global investment firm based in New York, founded in 1976 by Henry Kravis, George Roberts and Jerome Kohlberg. A pioneer of leveraged buyouts, it manages private equity, credit, infrastructure and real estate funds and owns the insurer Global Atlantic.
klac: KLA Corporation is an American maker of process-control equipment for semiconductor manufacturing, based in California. Its inspection and metrology systems find defects on silicon wafers and photomasks; its customers are the world's largest chipmakers.
klbn11: Klabin is Brazil's largest maker of packaging paper and paperboard, based in São Paulo and founded in 1899. It grows its own pine and eucalyptus plantations and produces pulp, kraft paper, corrugated boxes and paper sacks.
kled: Kled AI (KLED) is the token of Kled, a mobile app where people upload their own photos, videos and other content to be licensed as training data for AI companies, and get paid for their contributions.
klv: Klever is a crypto company founded in 2019 by a Brazilian team, known for the Klever Wallet app and its own blockchain, KleverChain. KLV is the native coin of KleverChain, used for fees, staking and governance.
kmb: Kimberly-Clark is a US maker of personal care products based in Irving, Texas, founded in 1872. It sells Kleenex tissues, Huggies diapers, Cottonelle and Scott toilet paper and Kotex feminine care products worldwide.
kmd: Komodo is a blockchain project launched in 2016 as a fork of Zcash. It is known for delayed proof of work, which regularly records its blocks on the bitcoin blockchain for extra security, and for atomic-swap technology behind its non-custodial Komodo Wallet and decentralized exchange. KMD is the platform's coin.
kmi: Kinder Morgan is a US energy infrastructure company based in Houston, founded in 1997 by Richard Kinder. It owns one of North America's largest natural gas pipeline networks, as well as pipelines for refined products and storage terminals.
kmno: Kamino is a DeFi platform on Solana that combines lending, borrowing, leverage and automated liquidity management. It began as the easiest way to earn from providing liquidity through one-click, auto-compounding strategies; KMNO is the governance token.
knc: Kyber Network Crystal (KNC) is the token of KyberSwap, a decentralized aggregator that finds the best exchange rate across many DEXs on multiple networks. Kyber Network was founded in Singapore in 2017 by Loi Luu and Victor Tran; KNC is used for governance.
knin: Kuehne+Nagel is a Swiss logistics company based in Schindellegi, founded in Bremen in 1890. It arranges sea and air freight, contract logistics and warehousing and is one of the world's largest freight forwarders.
kntq: Kinetiq (KNTQ) is the token of a liquid staking protocol on Hyperliquid that issues kHYPE for staked HYPE. The team also builds Markets.xyz for round-the-clock futures trading on stocks, currencies and commodities.
ko: The Coca-Cola Company is an American company from Atlanta and the world's largest maker of soft drinks; the Coca-Cola drink itself was invented in 1886. It also owns Sprite, Fanta, Dasani water and Costa Coffee, and sells its products in more than 200 countries.
kofubl: Coca-Cola FEMSA is a Mexican company and the world's largest Coca-Cola franchise bottler by sales volume. It produces and distributes Coca-Cola drinks in Mexico, Brazil, Colombia, Argentina and other Latin American countries.
koge: KOGE is a token on BNB Chain issued by 48 Club, a long-running BNB Chain community that operates validators and MEV-protection infrastructure. The token is used inside the 48 Club ecosystem and is widely traded on BNB Chain exchanges.
koma: Koma Inu (KOMA) is a dog-themed community memecoin on BNB Chain, presented as the «son of Shib» and protector of BNB. It has no product behind it: its value comes from meme culture and community activity.
kotakbank: Kotak Mahindra Bank is an Indian private bank from Mumbai, started by Uday Kotak in 1985 as a finance company. It offers banking, brokerage, insurance and asset management to individuals and businesses.
kpn: KPN (Koninklijke KPN) is the largest telecom operator in the Netherlands and the country's former state telephone company. It provides mobile service, fiber broadband and TV to households and businesses and owns an extensive national network.
kr: Kroger is one of America's largest supermarket operators, based in Cincinnati, Ohio, and founded in 1883. It runs thousands of grocery stores under banners such as Kroger, Ralphs, Fred Meyer, King Soopers and Harris Teeter, along with pharmacies, fuel stations and its own Simple Truth and Private Selection brands.
krl: Kryll (KRL) is the token of Kryll, a French platform for automated crypto trading founded in 2018. Users build trading bots with a visual drag-and-drop editor or copy strategies from a marketplace, and connect them to major exchanges; KRL pays for usage.
kskd: Kaskad (KSKD) is a decentralised lending protocol for the Kaspa ecosystem. It runs on Igra, an Ethereum-compatible layer 2 anchored to Kaspa, where users supply assets to earn interest or borrow against collateral; KSKD is used for governance.
ksm: Kusama (KSM) is a blockchain built on the same code as Polkadot, created by Gavin Wood as a «canary network» for testing new features. Projects test upgrades here in real conditions before launching on Polkadot; KSM is used for staking and governance.
kta: Keeta (KTA) is a high-performance layer-1 blockchain designed to connect transfers across different blockchains and traditional payment systems. The project is backed by former Google CEO Eric Schmidt, and KTA is used to pay network fees.
ktb: Krung Thai Bank is a state-controlled Thai bank based in Bangkok, founded in 1966 and one of the country's largest. It serves government agencies, companies and individuals, and runs the Krungthai NEXT banking app and the Paotang app used for state payments and savings bonds.
kub: KUB Coin (KUB) is the native coin of KUB Chain (formerly Bitkub Chain), the blockchain created by Thailand's crypto exchange Bitkub. It is used to pay network fees, for staking and in ecosystem apps in Thailand.
kweb: KraneShares CSI China Internet (KWEB) invests in Chinese internet companies such as Alibaba, Tencent, PDD and Meituan.
kweichow-moutai: Kweichow Moutai is a Chinese state-owned maker of baijiu, a strong grain liquor, from the town of Maotai in Guizhou province. Its Moutai liquor is China's most prestigious alcoholic drink, given as a gift on holidays and served at official banquets.
kyve: KYVE Network is a blockchain built with the Cosmos SDK that collects, validates and archives data from other blockchains, keeping trustworthy copies on permanent storage such as Arweave. Developers use these data streams instead of running their own nodes; KYVE pays for fees, staking and governance.
l: Loews Corporation is a New York-based holding company controlled by the Tisch family. It owns a controlling stake in insurer CNA Financial, the Boardwalk Pipelines gas pipeline business and the Loews Hotels chain.
l-ca: Loblaw is Canada's largest food and pharmacy retailer, headquartered in Brampton, Ontario. It owns Loblaws, No Frills and Real Canadian Superstore supermarkets, the Shoppers Drug Mart pharmacy chain and the President's Choice brand.
l1: GenesisL1 (L1) is a public proof-of-stake Layer 1 blockchain built for decentralized science: researchers can publish and tokenize datasets, molecular structures and machine-learning models. It runs on the Cosmos SDK with a built-in Ethereum Virtual Machine, so it supports Solidity smart contracts and IBC transfers.
l3: Layer3 is a platform where people complete quests in crypto apps — trying a new network, swapping or minting — and earn rewards, while projects use it to attract users. L3 is its token for incentives and on-chain identity.
la: Lagrange is a network that generates zero-knowledge proofs, letting blockchains and AI systems verify computations. Its services include a ZK coprocessor and verifiable AI; LA is used to pay for proofs and for staking.
ladys: Milady Meme Coin (LADYS) is an Ethereum memecoin launched in 2023, inspired by the Milady Maker NFT collection and its internet culture. It has no utility beyond trading and community.
laptop: Hunter Biden's Laptop (LAPTOP) is a political memecoin named after the widely reported US news story about the laptop of Hunter Biden. Like most memecoins, it has no business or assets behind it, and its price depends mainly on attention and trading.
largan-precision: Largan Precision is a Taiwanese maker of optical lenses based in Taichung, founded in 1987. It is one of the world's leading suppliers of smartphone camera lens modules, with Apple among its best-known customers.
lat: PlatON is a blockchain focused on privacy-preserving computation, letting data be used for calculations and AI without being revealed. It was started with backing from China's Wanxiang Blockchain Labs; LAT is its native coin for fees and staking.
lava: Lava Network is a protocol that gives apps, wallets and AI agents reliable access to blockchain data through a decentralized marketplace of RPC node providers across many chains. LAVA is used to pay for requests and to stake by providers.
layer: Solayer is a project in the Solana ecosystem developing InfiniSVM, a hardware-accelerated blockchain compatible with the Solana Virtual Machine. The network uses RDMA technology for ultra-fast communication between nodes; LAYER is the project's token.
lazio: Lazio Fan Token is the official fan token of S.S. Lazio, the football club from Rome, issued on Binance's Fan Token platform. Holders vote in club polls and get access to rewards and fan experiences.
lcap: CF Large Cap Index (LCAP) is a token that tracks the CF Large Cap index from CF Benchmarks, a basket of the largest cryptocurrencies by market value, giving holders diversified exposure to big coins through a single token.
lcx: LCX is a crypto exchange and blockchain company from Vaduz, Liechtenstein, registered under the country's blockchain law. It offers trading, storage and tokenization of digital assets for regulated markets in Europe, and the LCX token gives users fee discounts and access to platform services.
ldo: Lido DAO is the governance token of Lido, the largest liquid staking protocol on Ethereum, launched in 2020. Users stake ETH and receive the stETH token in return, which they can freely use in DeFi; LDO holders vote on the protocol's parameters.
ldo-it: Leonardo is a state-controlled Italian aerospace and defense company from Rome. It makes helicopters (formerly AgustaWestland), defense electronics, cybersecurity systems and aircraft structures and takes part in European space and military programs.
ldos: Leidos is a US technology and engineering company from Reston, Virginia, formerly known as SAIC and renamed in 2013. It provides IT, defense, intelligence, homeland security and health services, mainly to US government agencies.
len: Lennar is one of the largest US homebuilders, based in Miami and founded in 1954. It builds and sells single-family homes and townhouses in dozens of states and offers buyers mortgage, title and insurance services.
leo: LEO Token is the utility token of iFinex, the owner of the Bitfinex exchange, issued in 2019. Holders get trading-fee discounts on Bitfinex, and the company regularly buys back and burns tokens.
lg-electronics: LG Electronics is a South Korean electronics and home-appliance maker based in Seoul, founded in 1958 as GoldStar and part of the LG group. It is known for OLED TVs, refrigerators, washing machines and air conditioners, and also makes components for electric cars.
lg-energy-solution: LG Energy Solution is a South Korean battery maker from Seoul, spun off from LG Chem in 2020. It makes lithium-ion batteries for electric cars, energy storage systems and electronics; its customers include GM, Tesla and Hyundai.
lh: Labcorp is an American network of medical laboratories from Burlington, North Carolina. Every day it runs millions of blood and other tests for doctors and patients and provides lab services to drug companies developing new medicines.
lht: LuckyHash Token (LHT) is an XRP Ledger token of the LuckyHash gaming ecosystem. On its main platform, LuckyHash.win, it is used for bets and winnings in scratchcards, slots, dice, Plinko, Keno and other games.
lhx: L3Harris Technologies is a US defense company from Melbourne, Florida, formed in 2019 by the merger of L3 and Harris. It makes military radios, satellites and sensors, electronic warfare systems and, through Aerojet Rocketdyne, rocket motors.
lici: LIC (Life Insurance Corporation of India) is India's largest insurer, state-controlled and based in Mumbai, founded in 1956. It sells life insurance, pension and savings plans to hundreds of millions of Indians and is one of the country's largest investors.
light: Bitlight is a project from Bitlight Labs developing the RGB protocol for smart contracts and token issuance on top of Bitcoin and the Lightning Network. Its aim is to bring stablecoins and other assets to Bitcoin without a separate blockchain.
lime: iMe Lab (LIME) is the token of iMe, a messenger app built on Telegram that adds a built-in crypto wallet, AI tools and extra features. LIME is used for rewards, payments and premium features in the app.
lin: Linde is the world's largest industrial gases company, formed in 2018 by the merger of Germany's Linde AG and America's Praxair. It supplies oxygen, nitrogen, argon, hydrogen and helium to hospitals, steel, chemical and electronics makers and also builds gas plants.
linea: Linea (LINEA) is an Ethereum layer-2 network built on zkEVM technology by Consensys, the company behind the MetaMask wallet. It makes transactions cheaper and faster while staying fully Ethereum-compatible, and burns part of the ETH collected in network fees.
lingo: Lingo is a gamified Web3 rewards ecosystem backed by real-world assets (RWA). Income from these assets funds regular real-world prizes and benefits for the community, regardless of token price swings; LINGO is the ecosystem token.
link: Chainlink is a decentralised oracle network that feeds smart contracts with real-world data such as prices, exchange rates and event results. Launched in 2017 under Sergey Nazarov, it uses LINK to pay node operators.
lion: Loaded Lions (LION) is the token of the flagship NFT collection of the Crypto.com exchange, featuring lion avatars. It is used within the collection's ecosystem on the Cronos network for rewards, access to events and the holders' community.
lista: Lista DAO (LISTA) is a liquid staking and lending protocol on BNB Chain. Users stake BNB and receive slisBNB, and can borrow the lisUSD stablecoin against various assets as collateral; LISTA is the governance token.
lit: LIT is the token of Lighter, a decentralized perpetual futures exchange built as a ZK rollup on Ethereum. Its standout feature is order matching and liquidations that are verifiable with cryptographic proofs, at speeds close to centralized exchanges.
lite: Lumentum is a California company that makes optical and photonic components: lasers, optical transceivers and modules for telecom networks and AI data centers. Its lasers are also used in smartphone 3D sensing and industrial materials processing.
lity: LITY is the token of Lity Protocol on BNB Chain, which presents itself as an ecosystem for post-quantum infrastructure, AI and data — cryptography meant to stay secure even against future quantum computers.
lly: Eli Lilly is an American pharmaceutical company from Indianapolis, founded in 1876. It is known for insulin, the diabetes and obesity drugs Mounjaro and Zepbound, and medicines in oncology and immunology, and is one of the world's largest drugmakers.
lmt: Lockheed Martin is the largest US defense contractor, headquartered in Bethesda, Maryland. It builds F-35 and F-16 fighter jets, missiles, missile defense systems, Sikorsky helicopters and spacecraft, and its main customer is the US government.
lmts: Limitless (LMTS) is the token of Limitless Exchange, a prediction market on the Base network. Users trade on the outcomes of events, especially short-term crypto and stock price moves, and LMTS is the platform's token.
lmwr: LimeWire is the revived brand of the famous 2000s file-sharing app, now a platform for creators with AI tools for generating images, music and video. The LMWR token is used for payments, subscriptions and rewards on the platform.
lnt: Alliant Energy is a US utility holding company based in Madison, Wisconsin. Through its Iowa and Wisconsin utilities it supplies regulated electricity and natural gas to homes and businesses, with a large share of wind and solar generation.
loan: LOAN is the token of Metal X Lending (formerly Proton Loan), a lending and borrowing protocol on XPR Network from the US-based Metal team. Users deposit crypto to earn interest or borrow against it, and LOAN holders share in protocol rewards.
lobo: LOBO•THE•WOLF•PUP (LOBO) is a meme token on Bitcoin's Runes protocol with a wolf-pup mascot. It became one of the first popular runes, and part of the fees paid at launch went to Bitcoin miners.
lofi: LOFI is a community memecoin on the Sui blockchain. Its mascot is a character who woke up after being frozen in the Himalayas for centuries and now stands for optimism and building a brighter future on Sui; there is no product behind the token.
lon: Tokenlon is a decentralized exchange aggregator built by imToken, the crypto wallet maker. It finds swap prices across liquidity sources for Ethereum tokens, and LON is its governance and fee-sharing token.
lonn: Lonza is a Swiss company from Basel, founded in 1897. It is one of the world's largest contract developers and manufacturers of medicines, producing biologics, cell and gene therapies and capsules for pharmaceutical companies.
lot: League of Traders (LOT) is a social crypto trading platform where traders join competitions, compare results on leaderboards and follow other traders. LOT is the platform token, used for rewards and access to features.
low: Lowe's is the second-largest home improvement retailer in the US, founded in North Carolina in 1921. It sells building materials, tools, appliances and garden products and offers installation services.
lpt: Livepeer (LPT) is a decentralized network for processing and transcoding video, launched in 2017. Node operators provide GPU power to re-encode streams and, more recently, to generate AI video; LPT is staked to distribute work and earn rewards.
lqr: Laqira Protocol (LQR) is a blockchain project that describes itself as a metaverse complex linking people's everyday life with blockchain technologies. LQR is the project's token, used for payments and rewards inside its ecosystem.
lqty: Liquity is a decentralized lending protocol on Ethereum where users borrow the LUSD stablecoin, or BOLD in version two, against ETH collateral. The protocol runs without administrators; LQTY is staked to earn a share of fees.
lr: Legrand is a French maker of electrical and digital building infrastructure based in Limoges, with roots in the 19th century. It produces light switches, sockets, cable management, home automation, door entry systems and power and cooling equipment for data centers, selling them in around 90 countries.
lrc: Loopring is a decentralised exchange protocol on an Ethereum layer-2 zkRollup, founded in 2017 by Daniel Wang, offering both order-book and AMM trading with lower fees than the main chain. LRC is its token, used for staking and protocol incentives.
lrcx: Lam Research is a US maker of chip-manufacturing equipment based in Fremont, California, founded in 1980. Its tools etch and deposit thin layers of material on silicon wafers; customers include the largest memory and processor makers.
lsk: Lisk (LSK) is a project founded in Berlin in 2016 that now operates as a layer-2 network on Ethereum. It builds financial infrastructure for businesses to store, transfer and invest money in fiat currencies and stablecoins.
lt: Larsen & Toubro is India's largest engineering and construction company, based in Mumbai and founded in 1938 by two Danish engineers. It builds infrastructure, power plants, oil and gas facilities and defence systems and provides IT services through LTIMindtree.
ltc: Litecoin is one of the oldest cryptocurrencies, created in 2011 by former Google engineer Charlie Lee from bitcoin's code. Blocks arrive four times faster than bitcoin's, which is why it is often called 'silver to bitcoin's gold'.
luca: LUCA is the reward token of ATM, a peer-to-peer staking platform where users lock tokens in connections with each other. ATM ranks users in this network with Google's PageRank algorithm and pays rewards in LUCA; staking LUCA itself gives connections more weight.
lucia: Lucia (LUCIA) is a meme token on Ethereum built around a cheerful character. Its name comes from the Latin word for light, and the project is about humor, memes, artwork and community rather than financial infrastructure.
lucic: Lucidum (LUCIC) is a community memecoin on BNB Chain. Like most memecoins it has no business behind it: its value depends on community interest and trading activity.
lumia: Lumia is a blockchain for tokenizing real-world assets that emerged from the rebrand of Orion Protocol. The network makes it easier to issue and trade tokenized assets, and LUMIA is used for fees and staking.
luna: Terra (LUNA) is the native token of the new Terra blockchain, created in 2022 after the collapse of the algorithmic stablecoin UST. The old network was renamed Terra Classic (LUNC), while the new one runs on the Cosmos SDK and uses LUNA for staking and governance.
lunc: Terra Luna Classic is the original Terra blockchain left after the collapse of the UST stablecoin in May 2022. The community then launched a new Terra 2.0 network, while the old chain and its LUNC coin live on under community governance that burns tokens.
luv: Southwest Airlines is a US airline based in Dallas, founded in 1967 and a pioneer of the low-cost model. It flies only Boeing 737 jets and mainly operates point-to-point domestic flights within the United States.
lvs: Las Vegas Sands is a US operator of integrated casino resorts founded by Sheldon Adelson. After selling its Las Vegas properties, it earns its money in Macao, with The Venetian Macao, and in Singapore, with Marina Bay Sands.
lyb: LyondellBasell is one of the world's largest plastics and chemicals producers, incorporated in the Netherlands with headquarters in Houston and London. It makes polyethylene and polypropylene, fuels-related and other chemicals, and licenses its process technologies to petrochemical plants.
lyn: Everlyn (LYN) is a decentralized AI project building open-source video generation models that turn text and images into short videos, and a platform where creators use them; LYN is used to pay for and reward activity on the network.
lyv: Live Nation Entertainment is the world's largest live-events company, based in Beverly Hills, California. It promotes concerts and festivals, operates and manages venues, represents artists and owns Ticketmaster, the leading ticket seller, after the two companies merged in 2010.
lyx: LUKSO is an Ethereum-compatible layer-1 blockchain built for creators, fashion and culture. It was founded by Fabian Vogelsteller, author of the ERC-20 token standard, and offers Universal Profiles, smart accounts that act as a person's on-chain identity.
m: MemeCore is a layer-1 blockchain built specifically for meme coins. The project aims to turn memes from pure speculation into a tool for culture and communities: anyone can launch tokens and earn rewards for helping them grow popular.
m87: MESSIER (M87) is the token of Messier, a team building decentralized finance products and services across several networks. User fees from these products go to the treasury of the Messier DAO, called Virgo, which runs entirely on smart contracts.
ma: Mastercard is a US payments company headquartered in Purchase, New York, and one of the world's two biggest card networks alongside Visa. It runs the network behind Mastercard, Maestro and Cirrus cards, connecting banks, merchants and cardholders; it does not issue cards or lend money itself.
maaden: Ma'aden (Saudi Arabian Mining Company) is Saudi Arabia's largest mining company, based in Riyadh and founded in 1997. It mines phosphate and produces fertilisers, aluminium and gold; the state, through PIF, is its main shareholder.
mag7xon: Ondo Magnificent 7 and Crypto Portfolio (MAG7XON) is a tokenized portfolio from Ondo Finance that combines shares of the 'Magnificent Seven' US tech giants (Apple, Microsoft, NVIDIA, Alphabet, Amazon, Meta, Tesla) with a slice of cryptocurrencies.
magic: Treasure (MAGIC) is a decentralized gaming ecosystem that grew up on the Arbitrum network. Treasure builds games and AI-powered entertainment products, and MAGIC is its native token for payments and rewards.
magma: Magma Finance is a decentralized exchange on the Sui blockchain. It uses concentrated and adaptive liquidity so traders get better prices and liquidity providers earn more fees; the MAGMA token is used for governance and rewards.
mamo: Mamo (MAMO) is the token of Mamo, an AI personal finance companion on the Base network built by the team behind the Moonwell lending protocol. Mamo helps users save and earn yield on their crypto through simple chat-style guidance.
mana: Decentraland (MANA) is a virtual world on Ethereum, opened to the public in 2020, where users buy plots of LAND as NFTs, build scenes, host events and sell digital items. MANA is the in-world currency and the voting token of its DAO.
manta: Manta Network is an ecosystem built around Manta Pacific, an Ethereum layer-2 network that uses zero-knowledge proofs. It makes it easier to build apps with ZK technology and low fees; MANTA is used for staking and governance.
mantra: MANTRA is a layer-1 blockchain for tokenizing real-world assets (RWA) such as real estate, with a focus on regulatory compliance. The project holds a license in the UAE, and MANTRA is used for staking, fees and governance.
mapo: MAP Protocol (MAPO) is a cross-chain interoperability network positioned as a Bitcoin layer 2. It connects Bitcoin, Ethereum-compatible and other chains using light-client verification instead of trusted intermediaries, so assets and messages can move between them.
mar: Marriott International is the world's largest hotel company by number of rooms, headquartered in Bethesda, Maryland, and founded in 1927. Its brands include Marriott, Ritz-Carlton, Sheraton, Westin, W Hotels and more than 30 others.
marscoin: MARSCOIN is a token on BNB Chain conceived as a crypto asset paired with a company's stock. It is a speculative meme project with no standalone product, so its price depends on community interest.
marsmi: MarsMi (MARSMI) is a self-mocking memecoin themed around a future farming economy on Mars, with potatoes and internet jokes as its main motifs. The project openly says it has no clear plan.
maruti: Maruti Suzuki India is the country's largest carmaker, based in New Delhi and majority-owned by Japan's Suzuki Motor. Its first model, the Maruti 800 of 1983, put millions of Indian families on wheels; today it sells popular small cars and SUVs such as the Swift, Dzire, Baleno and Brezza.
mas: Masco is a US maker of home improvement and building products from Livonia, Michigan, founded in 1929. Its best-known brands are Delta and Hansgrohe faucets and Behr paint, sold through big home-improvement retailers.
mask: Mask Network (MASK) is a project that connects ordinary social networks with Web3: its browser extension lets people encrypt messages and send cryptocurrency and NFTs directly inside Twitter (X). MASK serves as the governance token.
math: MATH is the token of Math Wallet, a multi-chain crypto wallet available as a mobile app, browser extension and web wallet that supports many blockchains. The token is used for rewards, staking and services in the Math Wallet ecosystem.
mav: Maverick Protocol is DeFi infrastructure built around Maverick AMM, a decentralised exchange whose liquidity can move automatically with the price, so liquidity providers need less manual rebalancing. MAV is its governance and incentive token.
mavia: Heroes of Mavia (MAVIA) is the token of Heroes of Mavia, a mobile strategy game in which players build and defend bases on the fantasy island of Mavia and raid other players. MAVIA is used for governance and in the game's economy.
mb: Mediobanca is an Italian investment bank from Milan, founded in 1946. It specialises in corporate finance and mergers, wealth management for affluent clients and consumer lending through Compass; in 2025 Monte dei Paschi gained control of the bank.
mbc: MonbaseCoin (MBC) is the native token of Monbase, a centralized crypto exchange for buying, selling and trading digital assets. The token is used within the exchange's ecosystem.
mbg: Mercedes-Benz Group is a German maker of premium cars and vans based in Stuttgart, tracing its roots to Karl Benz's 1886 motor car, often called the first automobile. Its brands include Mercedes-Benz, the performance line Mercedes-AMG and the luxury Mercedes-Maybach; its truck business was spun off as Daimler Truck in 2021.
mbg-token: MBG is the token of MultiBank Group, one of the large forex and derivatives brokers, founded in 2005. The token is used within the group's ecosystem for trading discounts, staking and access to tokenized assets.
mbk: mBank is a Polish bank based in Warsaw, founded in 1986 as BRE Bank; in 2000 it launched mBank, one of Europe's first internet-only banks. It serves individuals and businesses in Poland, the Czech Republic and Slovakia, and its main shareholder is Germany's Commerzbank.
mbl: MovieBloc is a blockchain platform for film distribution that aims to break the dominance of big studios and cinema chains. Creators get a transparent revenue share and audience data, while viewers earn MBL tokens for curating, subtitling and promoting films.
mbx: MARBLEX (MBX) is the blockchain gaming arm of Netmarble, one of South Korea's biggest game publishers. The MBX token links Netmarble's Web3 games into one ecosystem, where in-game currencies can be swapped and used across titles.
mc: LVMH is the world's largest luxury goods group, based in Paris and formed in 1987 by the merger of Moët Hennessy and Louis Vuitton. It controls more than 70 houses, including Louis Vuitton, Dior, Tiffany, Bulgari, Sephora, Moët & Chandon champagne and Hennessy cognac; it is led by Bernard Arnault.
mcat: Marscat Token (MCAT) is a meme coin. Like most meme coins, it is not backed by a business or assets, and its price is driven mainly by community attention and trading.
mcd: McDonald's is the world's largest fast-food restaurant chain, headquartered in Chicago, built up from 1955 by Ray Kroc. Most of its restaurants are run by franchisees, and the company earns mainly from rent and royalties paid by them.
mchp: Microchip Technology is an American chipmaker from Arizona, known for its PIC and AVR microcontrollers. Its chips control electronics in cars, home appliances, industrial equipment, medical devices and defense systems.
mck: McKesson is the largest pharmaceutical distributor in the US, headquartered in Irving, Texas, and founded in 1833. It supplies medicines and medical products to pharmacies and hospitals and provides technology for prescriptions and cancer clinics.
mcn: MCNCOIN (MCN) is a crypto project on BNB Chain focused on analytics. It offers data and analysis tools for crypto users, and MCN is the token of its network.
mco: Moody's Corporation is a US financial information company based in New York, founded by John Moody in 1909. Moody's Investors Service is one of the three big credit rating agencies rating bonds of companies and governments, and Moody's Analytics sells risk data and software.
mcoin: MCOIN is the token of Mcoin Chain, a blockchain project aiming to build distributed infrastructure for digital assets. It focuses on connecting different blockchain ledgers so value can move between them, as a foundation for Web3 applications.
mdb: MongoDB is a US software company from New York, founded in 2007. It develops the popular document database of the same name and sells its cloud version, MongoDB Atlas.
mdlz: Mondelez International is a US snack food company based in Chicago, created in 2012 when Kraft Foods split. It makes some of the world's best-known snacks, including Oreo, Milka, Cadbury, Toblerone, Ritz, belVita and Halls.
mdt: Medtronic is one of the world's largest medical device makers, founded in Minneapolis in 1949 and legally domiciled in Ireland. It makes pacemakers, insulin pumps, surgical and neurostimulation equipment for hospitals in more than 150 countries.
mdt-token: Measurable Data Token (MDT) powers a data-exchange ecosystem where people share anonymized data with companies in return for rewards, through apps such as RewardMe and MyMDT. Businesses use MDT to pay for data and services.
me: Magic Eden is one of the largest NFT marketplaces, founded in 2021 in the Solana ecosystem. It lets people buy and sell NFTs, Ordinals and Runes on Bitcoin, Solana, Ethereum, Base and other networks; the ME token is used for governance and rewards.
med: MediBloc is a South Korean healthcare blockchain project that lets patients store and share their medical records securely. MED is the native token of its Panacea blockchain, built with the Cosmos SDK, and is used for fees and staking.
mediatek: MediaTek is a Taiwanese chip designer based in Hsinchu, founded in 1997. It designs Dimensity and Helio processors for Android smartphones as well as chips for TVs, Wi-Fi routers, tablets and smart devices; it has no factories of its own.
medp: Medpace is a US contract research organization (CRO) based in Cincinnati, Ohio, founded in 1992 by cardiologist August Troendle. It runs clinical trials from Phase I to Phase IV for drug, biotech and medical-device companies, with its own central laboratories.
mega: MegaETH (MEGA) is an Ethereum layer-2 network marketed as a «real-time blockchain» with millisecond latency and very high throughput. It stays Ethereum-compatible, so apps can run almost instantly without changing their tools.
mega-financial: Mega Financial Holding is a Taiwanese financial group from Taipei with partial government ties. Its core is Mega International Commercial Bank, Taiwan's leader in foreign exchange and trade finance; the group also has a brokerage and an insurer.
meituan: Meituan is a Chinese internet company from Beijing, founded by Wang Xing in 2010. It is China's largest food and grocery delivery service and also offers hotel booking, restaurant reviews, bike rentals and the international delivery app Keeta.
melania: Melania Meme (MELANIA) is a memecoin on the Solana network launched in January 2025 in Melania Trump's name. The token is presented as a digital collectible and a sign of support, with no practical function or ownership rights.
meli: MercadoLibre is Latin America's largest e-commerce company, founded in 1999 in Argentina by Marcos Galperin. It runs the Mercado Libre marketplace and the Mercado Pago fintech service in Brazil, Mexico, Argentina and other countries.
meme: Memecoin (MEME) is the token of Memeland, a project created by the team behind the popular entertainment site 9GAG. It serves as a 'coin of meme culture' for the community and Memeland's NFT collections and does not claim a technical function of its own.
merc: MERC is the token of Liquid Mercury, a company linking institutional trading infrastructure with a marketplace for tokenized real-world assets (Mercury RWA). The token gives issuers and holders access to the marketplace and its services.
merl: Merlin Chain (MERL) is a bitcoin layer-2 network based on ZK-rollup technology, launched in 2024. It lets users move BTC, Runes and BRC-20 tokens into an environment with cheap transactions and DeFi apps; MERL is the network's governance token.
met: MetLife is one of the world's largest insurers, based in New York and founded in 1868. It sells life insurance, annuities and employee benefit programmes and manages client assets in more than 40 countries.
met-token: Meteora is a liquidity platform on Solana with dynamic pools and a DLMM mechanism, where trading fees change with market volatility. Many new Solana tokens and memecoins launch and trade through Meteora; MET is the project's governance token.
meta: Meta Platforms is a US company from Menlo Park, California, founded by Mark Zuckerberg in 2004 as Facebook. It owns Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp and Messenger, earns mostly from advertising, and develops Llama AI, smart glasses and Quest VR headsets.
meta-token: MetaDAO is a fundraising and governance platform on Solana that uses futarchy: decisions are made by market prices rather than direct votes, as traders bet on whether a proposal will raise or lower the token's value. META is its token.
metal: Metal Blockchain (METAL) is a layer-0 blockchain from Metallicus built on Avalanche's consensus technology. It targets payments and financial services for banks and is linked to the Metal Pay digital banking app; METAL is used for fees and staking.
metfi: MetFi (METFI) is the token of MetFi DAO, a community-run investment DAO on BNB Chain whose members pool funds, propose and vote on Web3 investments, with membership NFTs and token rewards.
metis: Metis is an Ethereum layer-2 network based on optimistic rollups and the first to launch a decentralized sequencer. It promises fast, cheap transactions for DeFi and games; METIS is used for fees and staking.
mew: cat in a dogs world (MEW) is a Solana meme token whose idea is a "cat in a world of dogs" – a challenge to the many dog-themed meme coins. It runs purely on its community's meme culture.
mex: xExchange (MEX) is the token of xExchange, the main decentralized exchange of the MultiversX blockchain, formerly called Maiar Exchange. Users swap tokens and provide liquidity there, and MEX is used for farming rewards and governance.
mey: Mey Network is a blockchain ecosystem for tokenizing real-world assets (RWA). It consists of Meychain, a dedicated layer-1 blockchain for RWAs, and the MeyFi platform, while the MEY token is used for fees and network operations.
mfc: Manulife is a Canadian insurance and financial services company based in Toronto, founded in 1887. It sells life insurance, retirement and investment products in Canada and Asia, and operates in the US under the John Hancock brand.
mgo: Mango Network is a layer-1 blockchain with a multi-virtual-machine, omnichain design that supports MoveVM, EVM and SVM, so developers from different ecosystems can build on one network. MGO is its native token for fees and staking.
mha: Magic Hash (MAGNE.AI) is an ecosystem that combines hardware, blockchain infrastructure and artificial intelligence for secure ownership of digital assets and AI computing, including a Web3 smartphone. MHA is the ecosystem's token.
mhorse: MEME HORSE (MHORSE) is a community meme token on BNB Chain themed around the Year of the Fire Horse in the Chinese zodiac. It was fair-launched without a presale, and its liquidity pool tokens were burned.
mia: MIA is the token of an autonomous AI agent from the AgentFi niche, which plans strategies, talks with its community and manages resources on its own. Users chat with the agent and trade its token.
michi: michi (MICHI) is a cat-themed memecoin on the Solana blockchain, launched in 2024 and built around an internet cat meme. It has no product or cash flow behind it: the token is driven by its online community, so its price can swing sharply.
midea-group: Midea Group is a Chinese home appliance maker from Foshan, Guangdong, founded in 1968 by He Xiangjian. It makes air conditioners, refrigerators, washing machines and small appliances, and owns German robot maker KUKA and Toshiba's home appliance business.
mihao: ni hao cat (MIHAO) is a meme coin. Like most meme coins, it is not backed by a business or assets, and its price is driven mainly by community attention and trading.
mil-token: MIL is the utility token of Millionero, a centralized crypto exchange. Holding MIL gives users lower trading fees, platform perks and loyalty rewards.
mim: Magic Internet Money (MIM) is a token on the Bitcoin blockchain based on one of Bitcoin's oldest memes: the MS Paint «Magic Internet Money» wizard posted on Reddit's r/bitcoin in 2013. The original artist, Mavensbot, issued the token on Bitcoin a decade later.
mimatic: MAI is a dollar stablecoin from QiDao (Mai Finance), a lending protocol that started on Polygon. Users borrow MAI by locking crypto such as ETH or MATIC in over-collateralized vaults, and the protocol keeps MAI close to one US dollar.
min: Minswap is a decentralized exchange on the Cardano blockchain, where people swap tokens and provide liquidity directly from their wallets. The MIN token is used for governance and rewards liquidity providers and stakers.
mina: Mina Protocol (MINA) is a blockchain whose size stays at about 22 kilobytes thanks to recursive zero-knowledge proofs. That lets anyone verify the network even from a smartphone; MINA is used for fees and staking.
mira: Mira is a decentralized network for verifying AI output: it breaks AI-generated content into individual claims and checks them by consensus across several AI models, reducing the need for human review. Apps such as the Klok chat run on it.
mito: Mitosis (MITO) is the token of Mitosis, a layer-1 blockchain built around ecosystem-owned liquidity. It turns DeFi liquidity deposits into tokenized, programmable positions that can move across chains and earn yield; MITO is used for staking and governance.
mitsubishi-corp: Mitsubishi Corporation is Japan's largest trading house (sogo shosha), based in Tokyo. It invests and trades worldwide in energy, metals and mining, food, chemicals, cars and infrastructure, and is one of Berkshire Hathaway's holdings.
mitsubishi-electric: Mitsubishi Electric is a Japanese electrical equipment maker based in Tokyo, founded in 1921. It makes factory automation, power electronics, air conditioners, elevators and equipment for the energy, transport and space sectors.
mitsubishi-heavy-industries: Mitsubishi Heavy Industries is a Japanese engineering group based in Tokyo with a history dating back to 1884. It makes gas turbines and power plant equipment, defence and space systems, air conditioners, industrial machinery and ships.
mitsubishi-ufj: Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group (MUFG) is Japan's largest banking group, headquartered in Tokyo. It provides retail, corporate and investment banking, asset management and brokerage services, and owns a large stake in the US bank Morgan Stanley.
mitsui-co: Mitsui & Co. is one of Japan's largest general trading companies (sogo shosha), based in Tokyo, with roots in the Mitsui group dating to the 17th century. It invests in and trades energy, iron ore and metals, chemicals, food, infrastructure and healthcare worldwide; Berkshire Hathaway is a major shareholder.
mizuho-fg: Mizuho Financial Group is a Japanese banking group based in Tokyo, created in 2000 through the merger of three banks. It provides banking, trust, brokerage and investment banking services to corporations, governments and individual clients.
ml-token: Mintlayer (ML) is the coin of Mintlayer, a Bitcoin sidechain built for DeFi and tokenization. It lets users create tokens and NFTs and make atomic swaps with native BTC, while anchoring its security to the Bitcoin network.
mlk-token: MiL.k is a South Korean blockchain platform that connects loyalty programs of different companies, including airlines, hotels and shops. Users exchange loyalty points through the MLK token and spend them with partners.
mlm: Martin Marietta Materials is an American supplier of building materials based in Raleigh, North Carolina. It quarries and sells aggregates — crushed stone, sand and gravel — used to build roads, homes and data centers, mainly in fast-growing US states, and also makes magnesia-based chemical products.
mln: Enzyme, formerly Melon, is an Ethereum protocol for creating and managing on-chain investment funds and vaults. It was founded in 2016 by Mona El Isa and Reto Trinkler in Switzerland; the MLN token pays protocol fees and is used in governance.
mm: Mahindra & Mahindra is an Indian vehicle maker based in Mumbai and the flagship of the Mahindra Group, founded in 1945. It is known for SUVs such as the Scorpio, Thar and XUV700, and it is the world's largest tractor maker by volume; it also has interests in financial services and IT.
mmm: 3M is a US industrial conglomerate from St. Paul, Minnesota, founded in 1902 as Minnesota Mining and Manufacturing. Known for Post-it notes and Scotch tape, it makes thousands of products, from abrasives and adhesives to safety gear and electronics materials.
mmt: Momentum is a decentralized exchange with concentrated liquidity on the Sui network. Users swap tokens and provide liquidity, while MMT is used for governance and rewards for protocol participants.
mmui: MetaMUI (MMUI) is the token of an identity-based blockchain where accounts are decentralized identifiers (DIDs) for people, organizations and AI agents instead of raw crypto addresses. It is designed to make key recovery and upgrades to quantum-resistant encryption easier.
mnde: Marinade is a liquid staking protocol on Solana: users stake SOL and receive mSOL, a token that keeps earning staking rewards while it can still be traded or used in DeFi. MNDE is Marinade's governance token.
mnsry: Mansory Token (MNSRY) is the official token of Mansory, the German luxury car tuning house from Brand in Bavaria, founded in 1989 by Kourosh Mansory. The company builds customized, often limited-edition supercars, SUVs and luxury vehicles.
mnst: Monster Beverage is a US drinks company based in Corona, California, best known for Monster Energy, one of the world's top-selling energy drinks. It also sells Reign, Bang and other brands, with bottling and distribution largely handled by Coca-Cola's network.
mnt: Mantle is a layer-2 network for Ethereum that grew out of BitDAO and is closely linked to the Bybit crypto exchange. It lowers transaction costs for DeFi apps; MNT pays fees and is used for voting in the ecosystem.
mntx: Minutes Network Token (MNTX) powers Minutes Network, a privacy-focused communication app for calls and messaging built on Web3 principles, where users keep control of their data. The token is used for payments and rewards in the app.
mo: Altria is a US tobacco company based in Richmond, Virginia, formerly known as Philip Morris Companies. It sells Marlboro cigarettes, Black & Mild cigars, smokeless tobacco and on! nicotine pouches in the US and owns a stake in the brewing giant AB InBev.
moc: Mossland (MOC) is a location-based augmented-reality mobile game from South Korea built around real estate. Players find real buildings near them, buy and trade virtual versions of them in the game, and the MOC token lets those in-game properties be traded on crypto exchanges.
moca: Moca Network (MOCA) is digital identity infrastructure from Animoca Brands: one universal account for a person's assets, identity and reputation across different blockchains. The project grew out of the Mocaverse NFT collection, and MOCA is used across its ecosystem.
mog: Mog Coin (MOG) is a meme token on Ethereum launched in 2023, inspired by the internet slang word mog, meaning to outshine someone. It runs on the community's viral meme culture and has no separate product.
mon: Monad is a high-performance Layer 1 blockchain that is fully compatible with Ethereum (EVM) and executes transactions in parallel for speed and low fees. Its mainnet launched in November 2025; MON pays network fees and is used for staking.
montra: Montra (MONTRA) is a token-launch platform in the Elysium ecosystem from Kinetiq, a liquid-staking project on Hyperliquid. It lets teams launch and trade new tokens, and MONTRA is the platform's own token.
moodeng: Moo Deng (MOODENG) is a Solana meme token dedicated to Moo Deng, the pygmy hippo from Thailand's Khao Kheow Open Zoo who became an internet star in 2024. The token has no product of its own.
moolah: Moolah (MOOLAH) is a meme token on BNB Chain inspired by the mascot of Lista DAO, a decentralized finance protocol. It was launched on the Flap.sh platform and is promoted by Lista DAO as its officially endorsed mascot coin.
morpho: Morpho is a decentralized lending protocol on Ethereum, Base and other networks where users deposit assets to earn interest or borrow against collateral. It lets anyone create separate isolated markets and vaults; MORPHO is the governance token.
