move: Movement is a blockchain network that brings the Move programming language to developers, including in the Ethereum ecosystem. Move was created at Meta for the Diem project and focuses on smart-contract safety; MOVE is the network's token.
movr: Moonriver is a fully Ethereum-compatible smart contract parachain on Kusama and the sister network of Moonbeam in the Polkadot ecosystem. It serves as a place to launch and test new dApps; MOVR pays fees and is used for staking and governance.
mpc: Marathon Petroleum is a US oil refiner from Findlay, Ohio, one of the largest in the country, spun off from Marathon Oil in 2011. It runs a network of refineries that make gasoline, diesel and jet fuel and controls the pipeline company MPLX.
mplx: Metaplex (MPLX) is the leading tokenization platform on Solana: its standards and tools are used to create most NFTs and many tokens on that network. MPLX is the protocol's governance token.
mpwr: Monolithic Power Systems is a US chipmaker based in Kirkland, Washington, founded in 1997 by Michael Hsing. It designs power-management chips for servers and AI accelerators, cars, industrial equipment and consumer electronics.
mqg: Macquarie Group is an Australian investment group based in Sydney, founded in 1969. It is known as one of the world's largest infrastructure investors — roads, airports, energy — and also does banking and commodities trading.
mrk: Merck & Co. (known as MSD outside the US and Canada) is an American pharmaceutical company from New Jersey with roots going back to 1891. It makes the cancer drug Keytruda, the HPV vaccine Gardasil and medicines for animals.
mrk-de: Merck KGaA is a German science and technology company based in Darmstadt and the world's oldest pharmaceutical company, founded in 1668. It makes medicines, laboratory chemicals and equipment, and materials for semiconductors and displays.
mrna: Moderna is a US biotech company based in Cambridge, Massachusetts, founded in 2010, that develops medicines based on messenger RNA (mRNA). It is best known for its Spikevax COVID-19 vaccine and also sells an RSV vaccine, mRESVIA, while developing vaccines and cancer treatments.
mrsh: Marsh McLennan is a US professional services firm from New York and the world's largest insurance broker, founded in 1871. It brings together Marsh (insurance), Guy Carpenter (reinsurance), Mercer (HR consulting) and Oliver Wyman (management consulting).
mrvl: Marvell Technology is an American designer of semiconductors for data infrastructure, founded in 1995. It makes chips for data centres, networking, storage and cars, including custom AI processors built for the big cloud companies.
ms: Morgan Stanley is a US investment bank headquartered in New York, founded in 1935. It manages wealth for affluent clients, trades securities and advises on mergers and acquisitions; it also owns the E*Trade brokerage platform.
msci: MSCI is a New York company that builds stock market indexes followed by thousands of funds and ETFs worldwide, such as MSCI World and MSCI Emerging Markets. It also sells risk analytics, ESG ratings and data to investors.
msft: Microsoft is a US technology company based in Redmond, Washington, founded in 1975 by Bill Gates and Paul Allen. It develops Windows, Office, the Azure cloud, LinkedIn, Xbox and the Copilot assistant, and is a key partner of OpenAI.
msft-token: Microsoft • Robinhood Token is a tokenized version of Microsoft shares issued by Robinhood for its customers in the European Union. It follows the price of the US-listed stock and can be traded around the clock on a blockchain.
msi: Motorola Solutions is a US company based in Chicago that makes communication and security technology for police, firefighters, governments and businesses: two-way radios, emergency call-center software and video security systems. It is the successor of the original Motorola.
mstr: Strategy, formerly MicroStrategy, is an American company based in Tysons Corner, Virginia, founded in 1989 by Michael Saylor. It started in business-intelligence software and still sells analytics tools, but since 2020 it has turned into a bitcoin treasury company and is the largest corporate holder of bitcoin; it was renamed Strategy in 2025.
mstr-token: This is a Robinhood stock token that tracks the share price of Strategy Inc. (formerly MicroStrategy), the US software company that became the largest corporate holder of bitcoin under Michael Saylor. The token lets Robinhood customers in eligible regions get exposure on-chain; it is not the share itself.
mtb: M&T Bank is an American regional bank from Buffalo, New York, founded in 1856. It serves people and businesses in the Northeast and Mid-Atlantic; for decades it was led by the noted banker Robert Wilmers, and Berkshire Hathaway was long a shareholder.
mtd: Mettler-Toledo is a Swiss-American maker of precision scales and laboratory instruments with roots going back to 1945. Its balances, analyzers and product inspection systems are used by labs, drug makers, food factories and retailers.
mtl: Metal DAO (MTL) is a token that governs the Metal Dollar (XMD) stablecoin and gives holders fee discounts in the Metal Pay app for cash and crypto. The project grew out of Metal, a payments service founded in the US in 2016.
mtsi: MACOM Technology Solutions is a US semiconductor company from Lowell, Massachusetts, with roots going back to 1950. It designs analog, RF, microwave and optical chips used in data centers, telecom networks, defense and industrial systems.
mtx: MTU Aero Engines is a German aircraft engine maker based in Munich. It develops and builds key engine modules for passenger and military aircraft, including the Pratt & Whitney GTF engine for the Airbus A320neo, and is one of the largest providers of engine maintenance.
mu: Micron Technology is a US memory maker from Boise, Idaho, founded in 1978. It produces DRAM, NAND flash, SSDs and high-bandwidth HBM memory for AI accelerators, and also sells products under the Crucial brand.
mu-token: This is a tokenized share that tracks Micron Technology, issued through Backpack Securities so it can be traded on crypto rails. Micron, based in Boise, Idaho and founded in 1978, is one of the world's largest makers of memory chips — DRAM, including high-bandwidth memory for AI, and NAND flash.
mubarak: Mubarak is a BNB Chain meme token with an Arabic name meaning "blessed". It became popular in 2025 after Binance founder Changpeng Zhao (CZ) mentioned it and bought some.
murata: Murata Manufacturing is a Japanese electronic components maker based in Kyoto, founded in 1944. It is the world leader in multilayer ceramic capacitors and also makes RF modules, sensors and batteries for smartphones, cars and electronics.
muv2: Munich Re is one of the world's largest reinsurers, based in Munich, Germany, and founded in 1880. It insures insurance companies against big risks such as earthquakes, hurricanes and pandemics, and through its subsidiary ERGO it sells insurance directly to people and businesses.
mvc: MileVerse (MVC) is a blockchain-based mileage payment platform. It lets customers exchange unused or expiring loyalty miles and points from different companies into its own MileVerse Point (MVP) and spend them at affiliated stores.
mvl: MVL is a blockchain ecosystem for mobility that collects data about a car over its whole life from dealers, repair shops and rental companies. The Singapore-based project also launched the TADA ride-hailing service in Southeast Asia; MVL is the token for rewards and payments.
mwxt: MWX Token (MWXT) powers MWX, a decentralized marketplace of ready-to-use AI agent solutions for businesses. Paying marketplace fees in MWXT gives discounts, 20% of every commission is burned automatically and quarterly buy-backs from profits further reduce the supply.
mx: MX is the native token of the crypto exchange MEXC (formerly MXC), founded in 2018. MX holders get trading fee discounts, access to new token distributions and a vote on which coins get listed on the exchange.
mxnb: MXNB is a stablecoin backed by and pegged 1:1 to the Mexican peso. It lets businesses and individuals hold and move pesos on blockchain networks, for example for fast cross-border payments, trade settlement and exposure to the Mexican currency.
my: Metya (MY) is an AI-powered SocialFi dating platform built around "DatingFi", a mix of online dating and crypto economics. The MY token serves as the in-app currency and as rewards for users.
myro: MYRO is a meme coin on Solana named after Myro, the dog of Solana co-founder Raj Gokal. It is a community-driven token with no utility beyond its meme and community.
myst: Mysterium Network is a decentralized VPN started in 2017: people around the world rent out their internet connection as nodes, and users connect through them for private browsing. MYST is the token used to pay node operators.
myx: MYX Finance is a decentralized exchange for perpetual futures that runs on several blockchains. It uses a matching pool that pairs traders' orders with liquidity, letting them trade with leverage without an intermediary; MYX is its governance token.
nab: National Australia Bank (NAB) is one of Australia's four biggest banks, headquartered in Melbourne. It is especially strong in business lending and in New Zealand operates through its subsidiary Bank of New Zealand (BNZ).
naka: Nakamoto Games (NAKA) is a Web3 gaming platform on Polygon with a catalog of casual play-to-earn games, tournaments and a hub for game developers. The NAKA token is used to play, enter tournaments and receive rewards across its games.
naoris: Naoris Protocol is a decentralized cybersecurity network in which devices verify each other's trustworthiness, with a focus on post-quantum protection. The NAORIS token is used for rewards and staking in the network.
nat: DMT-NAT (NAT) is a token created from Bitcoin block data under the Digital Matter Theory standard, launched by a fair mint with no premine. Bitcoin miners earn NAT as an extra reward on top of the normal block subsidy.
natgas: Natural gas (US Henry Hub) is a fuel for heating and power plants and a raw material for the chemical industry. Its price is highly seasonal and depends on the weather and LNG exports.
natix: NATIX Network is a Munich-based DePIN project that crowdsources street-level camera data from drivers' smartphones and car cameras to build up-to-date maps and AI training data. Contributors earn NATIX tokens.
naver: NAVER is South Korea's largest internet company, based in Seongnam and founded in 1999. It runs Naver, the country's leading search portal, plus online shopping, the Naver Pay payment service, the Webtoon comics platform and cloud services.
navx: NAVI Protocol (NAVX) is one of the main lending and borrowing platforms on the Sui blockchain. Users deposit crypto to earn interest or borrow against it, and the protocol also offers liquid staking and a swap aggregator; NAVX is its governance token.
nbis: Nebius Group is a technology company headquartered in Amsterdam, created after Yandex sold its Russian business in 2024. It builds AI cloud infrastructure with large NVIDIA GPU clusters and also owns the TripleTen education platform and the self-driving developer Avride.
nbix: Neurocrine Biosciences is a US biopharmaceutical company from San Diego, founded in 1992, focused on neurological, psychiatric and endocrine disorders. Its main medicine is Ingrezza for tardive dyskinesia and Huntington's chorea; it also sells Crenessity for a rare adrenal disorder.
nct: PolySwarm (NCT) is a decentralized cybersecurity marketplace where antivirus experts and engines compete to detect malicious files and links. The Nectar token (NCT) pays for scans and rewards accurate verdicts.
ncx: NovaChargeX Coin (NCX) is an ERC-20 token on Ethereum linked to NovaChargeX LLC, a clean-energy company developing hybrid regenerative power systems meant to supply round-the-clock, off-grid electricity to AI data centers and industrial sites.
ndaq: Nasdaq is a US exchange and technology company based in New York that runs the Nasdaq stock market, which in 1971 became the world's first electronic exchange. Many tech giants trade there, and the company also sells software for banks and for fighting financial crime.
ndsn: Nordson is a US maker of industrial equipment based in Westlake, Ohio, founded in 1954. It builds precision systems that dispense and apply adhesives, coatings, sealants and other fluids, plus components for medical devices and inspection equipment for electronics.
near: NEAR Protocol is a layer-1 blockchain for smart contracts and apps that is increasingly focused on AI agents. Its co-founder, Ukrainian-born Illia Polosukhin, is one of the authors of the famous Transformer paper behind modern AI.
nect: Nectar (NECT) is an over-collateralized dollar stablecoin native to Berachain, issued by the Beraborrow lending protocol. Users lock approved Berachain assets in a vault called a Den to borrow NECT, which can be redeemed for collateral at face value.
nee: NextEra Energy is one of the largest US energy companies, headquartered in Florida. Its subsidiary Florida Power & Light supplies electricity to millions of customers, while NextEra Energy Resources is one of the world's biggest producers of wind and solar power.
neet: NEET is a memecoin named after the acronym for people "Not in Employment, Education, or Training". It turns the internet joke about stay-at-home life into a community token and has no function beyond trading and memes.
neiro: Neiro is a meme coin named after Neiro, the Shiba Inu adopted in 2024 by the owner of Kabosu, the dog behind the Doge meme. The token runs on its community and the popularity of dog memes and has no technical function of its own.
nem: Newmont is the world's largest gold miner, headquartered in Denver, USA, and founded in 1921. It runs mines in North and South America, Australia, Africa and Papua New Guinea, and also produces copper, silver and zinc.
neo: NEO is a Chinese smart-contract blockchain founded in 2014 as Antshares by Da Hongfei and Erik Zhang. It is often called the «Chinese Ethereum»; NEO holders receive the network's second token, GAS, which is used to pay fees.
nes: Nesa (NES) is a privacy-focused layer-1 blockchain for decentralized artificial intelligence. Its encrypted inference technology lets AI models run on confidential data without exposing it; NES pays for fees, model queries and running network nodes.
nesn: Nestlé is a Swiss company based in Vevey, the world's largest food maker, founded in 1866 by Henri Nestlé. It is known for the brands Nescafé, Nespresso, KitKat and Maggi, Purina pet food and baby food.
nest: NEST is the token of nest, a MetaDEX (vote-based decentralized exchange) in the Hyperliquid ecosystem. Like other MetaDEXs, it gives all trading fees to token voters, and its HYPE Engine system channels value into extra exposure to Hyperliquid's HYPE token.
nestleind: Nestlé India is the Indian subsidiary of Switzerland's Nestlé, headquartered in Gurugram. It makes Maggi noodles, Nescafé coffee, KitKat and Munch chocolates, baby food and dairy products for the Indian market.
netease: NetEase is a Chinese internet company based in Hangzhou, founded in 1997 by Ding Lei. It is one of the world's largest video game developers, with hits such as Fantasy Westward Journey and Eggy Party, and also runs the NetEase Cloud Music service and Youdao education.
netx: NetX is a Layer 1 blockchain ecosystem that combines AI tools with tokenized real-world assets, so apps on the network can use regulated stablecoins, tokenized financial instruments and other asset-backed tokens for payments and settlement.
newt: Newton Protocol (NEWT) is infrastructure for verifiable on-chain automation. Users, protocols and DAOs authorize AI agents to act for them under programmable permissions, and trusted execution environments plus zero-knowledge proofs show that each action followed the rules, without centralized bots.
nex: Nexus (NEX) is a layer-1 blockchain project for verifiable finance, designed to run decentralized exchanges. It uses zero-knowledge (ZK) technology to prove computations, and the NEX token is meant to power the network.
nexa: Nexa (NEXA) is a proof-of-work Layer 1 blockchain with native tokens and smart contracts, built by the Bitcoin Unlimited team. It is designed to scale on-chain for global peer-to-peer use, using techniques such as Graphene block compression and instant transactions.
nexo: Nexo is a crypto platform founded in 2018 that offers loans backed by crypto collateral, interest on deposits, exchange and a payment card. Holding the NEXO token gives users better rates, cheaper loans and cashback.
nflx: Netflix is the world's largest streaming service for films and series, based in Los Gatos, California, and founded in 1997 by Reed Hastings and Marc Randolph. It began by renting DVDs by mail and now produces its own hits such as Stranger Things and Squid Game.
nft: AINFT (formerly APENFT) is a project in the TRON ecosystem that combines NFTs with artificial intelligence. The NFT token serves as its governance token: holders take part in votes on how the platform develops.
ni: NiSource is a US energy company from Indiana. Under the Columbia Gas brand it delivers natural gas to millions of customers in several states, and through NIPSCO it sells electricity and gas in northern Indiana.
night: Midnight is a privacy-focused blockchain built by Input Output, the developer of Cardano, as a partner chain. Zero-knowledge proofs let applications verify data without revealing it; NIGHT is the network's native token.
nil: Nillion (NIL) is a decentralized network for working with encrypted data, letting computations run on it without revealing the contents. It is used for private AI apps and protected markets, and the NIL token pays for the service and is staked.
nila: MindWaveDAO (NILA) is a Web3 project that describes itself as building on Bitcoin-based yield infrastructure and its own Layer 2 network. It combines four areas — advertising tech, insurance tech, AI governance and climate tech — into one ecosystem.
nim: Nimiq is a payment-focused cryptocurrency with its own blockchain, designed to work directly in a web browser without extra software, so anyone can send and receive NIM from a simple web wallet. Launched in 2018, the network switched from mining to proof of stake in 2024.
nintendo: Nintendo is a Japanese maker of game consoles and video games based in Kyoto, founded in 1889 as a playing-card company. It creates the Switch consoles and the Mario, Zelda and Pokémon game series (the latter with partners).
nke: Nike is a US maker of sports shoes and apparel from Beaverton, Oregon, founded in 1964 by Phil Knight and Bill Bowerman. It is the world's largest sportswear brand, known for Air Jordan and Air Max sneakers and also owning the Jordan and Converse brands.
nkn: NKN (New Kind of Network) is a decentralized networking project launched in 2018, where people run nodes that relay internet data and earn NKN tokens. It aims to make data transfer cheaper, more private and harder to censor.
nkyc: NKYC is the token of NonKYC.io, a crypto exchange founded in 2023 that lists many small and mid-cap coins and lets users trade without identity verification. Paying trading fees in NKYC gives a 25% discount.
nls: Nolus (NLS) is a Cosmos-based blockchain for DeFi whose main product, DeFi Lease, lets users open a larger crypto position while paying only part of it upfront, with the rest financed by the protocol. NLS is used for fees, staking and governance.
nmr: Numeraire (NMR) is the token of Numerai, a San Francisco hedge fund founded in 2015 by Richard Craib. The fund runs a tournament where data scientists submit stock-market prediction models and stake NMR on their quality: accurate models are rewarded, poor ones lose their stake.
nn: NN Group is a Dutch insurer from The Hague that grew out of ING's former insurance business. It sells life insurance, pensions and property and casualty insurance in the Netherlands, elsewhere in Europe and in Japan.
noc: Northrop Grumman is a US defense and aerospace company based in Falls Church, Virginia. It builds the B-21 Raider stealth bomber, military drones, missile systems and space hardware, including parts of the James Webb Space Telescope.
nock: Nockchain (NOCK) is a layer-1 blockchain where nodes «mine» zero-knowledge proofs (ZK Proof of Work) instead of ordinary hashes. The project is connected to the Urbit community and the Nock programming language.
nom: NOM is the main network token of Nomina, a unified trading platform for running complex trading strategies across several decentralized exchanges from one interface.
not: Notcoin (NOT) is a token on the TON network that grew out of a viral 2024 tap-to-earn game in Telegram, where millions of users tapped a coin on screen. The project became one of the biggest gateways for newcomers into crypto through Telegram.
novn: Novartis is a Swiss pharmaceutical company based in Basel, formed in 1996 by the merger of Ciba-Geigy and Sandoz. It develops innovative medicines for cancer, heart disease and immunology, including Entresto, Kisqali and Cosentyx.
now: ServiceNow is a US cloud software company from Santa Clara, California, founded in 2004. Its platform automates workflows in IT, HR, customer service and security for large companies, increasingly with AI agents.
now-token: NOW is the token of ChangeNOW, an instant non-custodial crypto exchange service that swaps hundreds of coins without requiring an account. Holding or staking NOW gives users cashback and discounts on the platform.
noxo: NOXO is the utility and governance token of NOXCAT, a self-custodial Web3 wallet. Besides storing and sending crypto, the app offers on-chain escrow, collateralized loans and social messaging; NOXO holders can vote and unlock selected features.
npc: Non-Playable Coin (NPC) is an Ethereum meme coin inspired by the "non-playable character" meme. Its supply equals Earth's population as of 26 July 2023, and each token can be turned into an NFT and back.
nrg: NRG Energy is a US energy company based in Houston. It owns power plants and sells electricity and natural gas to millions of homes and businesses under brands such as Reliant, Direct Energy and Green Mountain, plus Vivint smart-home security.
ns: SuiNS (NS) is the token of the Sui Name Service, which gives readable names ending in .sui to wallet addresses and apps on the Sui blockchain. NS is used to pay for names at a discount and for governance.
nsc: Norfolk Southern is a US freight railroad based in Atlanta that runs a rail network across the eastern United States. It carries raw materials, industrial goods, cars and containers between ports, factories and cities in more than 20 states.
nst: Northern Star Resources is an Australian gold miner based in Perth, founded in 2000. It runs large mines in Western Australia, including the famous Super Pit at Kalgoorlie, as well as the Pogo mine in Alaska.
nst-token: Ninja Squad Token (NST) is the native token of Ninja Traders, an ecosystem of trading tools and products for both beginner and advanced crypto traders. Holding NST gives access to the ecosystem's products and community features.
ntap: NetApp is an American company from San Jose, founded in 1992, that makes data storage systems and software to manage data. Its products run both in customers' own data centers and in the AWS, Microsoft Azure and Google Cloud clouds.
ntgy: Naturgy is a Spanish energy company from Madrid, formerly known as Gas Natural Fenosa. It distributes gas and electricity in Spain and Latin America, supplies LNG and generates power at gas-fired and renewable plants.
ntpc: NTPC is India's largest power generation company, based in New Delhi, controlled by the state and founded in 1975. It produces electricity mainly at coal and gas plants and is rapidly expanding solar and wind capacity.
ntr: Nutrien is a Canadian fertilizer maker from Saskatoon, formed in 2018 by the merger of Potash Corp and Agrium. It is the world's largest producer of potash fertilizer and also runs a large network of farm retail stores.
ntrs: Northern Trust is an American bank from Chicago, founded in 1889. It serves wealthy individuals and families and provides custody and accounting of assets for pension funds, sovereign wealth funds and investment firms worldwide.
ntt: NTT (formerly Nippon Telegraph and Telephone) is Japan's largest telecom group, based in Tokyo, created as a state monopoly and privatized in 1985. It owns NTT Docomo, Japan's biggest mobile operator, regional fixed-line companies and NTT Data's global IT services and data centers.
nu: Nu Holdings is a Brazilian digital bank based in São Paulo, founded in 2013 by David Vélez. Known for the purple Nubank card, it offers accounts, credit cards, loans and investments through its app in Brazil, Mexico and Colombia.
nue: Nucor is the largest steelmaker in the United States, headquartered in Charlotte, North Carolina. It makes steel in electric arc furnaces mostly from scrap metal and is also North America's largest scrap recycler.
num: Numbers Protocol (NUM) is the token of Numbers Protocol, a decentralized network for verifying where digital photos, videos and other media come from. Creators register content with its Capture app so its origin and edits can be traced; NUM pays for these records.
numi: Numine is a blockchain gaming platform that helps studios develop, publish and run blockchain-based games and gives players one place to play them. NUMI is the platform's token, used for rewards and in-game economies.
nuts: Thetanuts Finance is an on-chain options protocol where users can buy and sell crypto options or deposit into vaults that run options strategies to earn yield. NUTS is the protocol's governance token.
nvda: Nvidia is a US chipmaker based in Santa Clara, California, founded in 1993 by Jensen Huang. Known for GeForce graphics cards, its main business today is GPUs and systems for data centres that train and run artificial intelligence.
nvda-token: This is a Robinhood stock token that tracks NVIDIA shares, the US maker of graphics and AI chips. Robinhood launched such tokens in 2025 for customers in the European Union, letting them trade US stock exposure on-chain, around the clock.
nvt: nVent Electric is an electrical equipment company incorporated in Ireland and run from Minneapolis, spun off from Pentair in 2018. It makes enclosures, cable management, grounding and liquid-cooling systems that protect electrical equipment and data centers.
nws: News Corp is a US media company from New York, created in 2013 when Rupert Murdoch's media empire was split. It publishes The Wall Street Journal, Dow Jones, The Times, The Sun and The Australian, owns HarperCollins books and a large stake in REA Group. Class B shares carry voting rights.
nxpc: Nexpace (NXPC) is the token of MapleStory Universe, a blockchain ecosystem built by South Korean game giant Nexon around its cult game MapleStory. It is used to create and trade in-game NFT items and in the economy of the games in this universe.
nxpi: NXP Semiconductors is a Dutch chipmaker based in Eindhoven, spun off from Philips in 2006. It makes chips for cars, industry and the Internet of Things and is a leader in NFC contactless payment technology.
nxt: NEXST is a Web3 platform for the entertainment industry that tokenizes the fan experience. Going to concerts, buying merchandise and interacting with AI create digital rights that build up over time and unlock new perks for fans.
nym: Nym is a privacy network that protects internet traffic metadata using a mixnet and the NymVPN service. It hides who talks to whom, when and how often; NYM is used for payments and rewards for node operators.
o: Realty Income is a US real estate investment trust (REIT) from San Diego, founded in 1969. It leases thousands of stores, warehouses and other properties on long-term contracts and calls itself «The Monthly Dividend Company» because it pays dividends every month.
o-token: o1.exchange (O) is the token of o1.exchange, a decentralized trading terminal where users buy and sell crypto tokens straight from their own wallets, with charts and fast order tools in one interface.
oats: Oats are a grain used for cereal flakes, porridge and animal feed. The futures market is small, so prices can swing sharply on the weather in Canada and the US.
obsr: Observer is a South Korean blockchain project that builds a decentralized weather-data network: it gathers weather information from smartphone sensors and weather stations, pools it on-chain and offers it to businesses. Users who contribute data are rewarded with the OBSR token.
obt: Orbiter Finance (OBT) is the token of Orbiter Finance, a cross-rollup bridge for moving ETH, stablecoins and other assets quickly and cheaply between Ethereum and its layer-2 networks.
ocean: Ocean Protocol is a blockchain ecosystem for sharing data and related services, founded in Singapore in 2017. It lets people sell and buy access to datasets and AI computing without handing over the data itself; in 2024 it joined the ASI Alliance with Fetch.ai and SingularityNET.
oct: Octra (OCT) is the token of a blockchain network built around fully homomorphic encryption (FHE), which lets data be processed while it stays encrypted, and isolated execution environments. Most of its code is written in OCaml, Rust and C++.
odfl: Old Dominion Freight Line is an American trucking company from Thomasville, North Carolina, founded in 1934. It specializes in less-than-truckload (LTL) freight and is known for on-time delivery and very low damage rates.
og: OG Fan Token is the fan token of OG, the esports organisation that became the first team to win Dota 2's The International twice. Issued on Chiliz's Socios.com platform, it lets fans vote in team polls and get rewards and experiences.
ogn: Origin Protocol (OGN) is a DeFi project founded in 2017 by Josh Fraser and Matthew Liu. It issues the yield-bearing tokens Origin Ether (OETH) and Origin Dollar (OUSD); OGN is used to govern the protocol.
ogy: ORIGYN (OGY) is the token of the Swiss-based ORIGYN Foundation, which issues digital certificates on the Internet Computer blockchain to prove the authenticity and ownership of luxury goods such as watches and art. OGY is used for fees and governance.
ohm: Olympus is a DeFi protocol launched on Ethereum in 2021 around OHM, a token backed by an on-chain treasury of crypto assets. The protocol manages that treasury and its own liquidity to keep OHM a stable, decentralised reserve currency.
ojuice: Frozen concentrated orange juice is a small futures market. Prices depend on orange harvests in Florida and Brazil, hurricanes and citrus diseases.
okb: OKB is the token of the OKX crypto exchange (formerly OKEx), launched in 2018. It gives discounts on trading fees and access to new token launches, and pays fees on X Layer, OKX's layer-2 network.
oke: ONEOK is a US energy infrastructure company from Tulsa, Oklahoma. It owns thousands of miles of pipelines, gas processing plants and storage facilities that move natural gas, natural gas liquids and refined products.
okta: Okta is an American company from San Francisco, founded in 2009, and a leader in digital identity management. Its cloud service gives employees and customers one secure login to thousands of apps, with multi-factor authentication.
ol: Open Loot is a Web3 gaming platform built by the team behind the game Big Time, where players buy, sell and trade in-game items and developers publish and market their games. The OL token is used for rewards and activity across the Open Loot ecosystem.
olas: Olas (formerly Autonolas) is a network for building and running autonomous AI agents and off-chain services that are co-owned by the community. Developers and operators are rewarded in OLAS for creating useful agents and running them.
omc: Omnicom Group is one of the world's largest advertising holding companies, headquartered in New York. It brings together agencies such as BBDO, DDB and TBWA plus media and PR networks, and grew further by buying Interpublic Group.
omg: OMG Network is an Ethereum scaling network for fast, cheap transfers of ETH and ERC-20 tokens, created by the OmiseGO team from Thailand. It was one of the first solutions built on Plasma technology.
omi: ECOMI (OMI) is the token behind VeVe, a mobile platform for licensed digital collectibles in the form of NFTs. Collections from major brands such as Marvel, DC and Disney are released on VeVe; OMI is used in the loyalty program and for purchases.
on: onsemi (ON Semiconductor) is a US chipmaker from Scottsdale, Arizona, spun off from Motorola in 1999. It specialises in silicon carbide power chips and image sensors used in electric cars, factories and energy systems.
on-token: Orochi Network is verifiable data infrastructure based on zero-knowledge proofs: zkDatabase, the Orand random number generator and the Orocle oracle. The ON token pays for services and incentives in the network.
ondo: Ondo is a real-world asset tokenization project that brings US Treasuries, funds and stocks onto the blockchain, making them accessible to crypto investors. The Ondo Foundation was set up in 2022, and ONDO is the ecosystem's governance token.
one: ONEchain (ONE), formerly CROSS, is a Layer 1 blockchain for games developed by South Korea's NEXUS. It lets studios turn in-game currencies and items into tokens and NFTs that go to the player's wallet; ONE is the network's native token.
ong: Ontology Gas (ONG) is the token used to pay transaction fees on the Ontology blockchain. It is gradually released to ONT holders and stakers, because the network uses a two-token model: ONT for staking and governance, ONG as the "gas".
ongc: ONGC (Oil and Natural Gas Corporation) is India's largest oil and gas producer, based in New Delhi, state-controlled and founded in 1956. It produces oil and gas in India and abroad (through ONGC Videsh) and also has stakes in refining.
ont: Ontology (ONT) is a public blockchain founded in 2017 by the Chinese team Onchain, focused on digital identity and trusted data. ONT is used for staking and governance and generates the network's second token, ONG, which pays transaction fees.
oob: Oobit is a crypto payments app that lets people pay in shops worldwide straight from their crypto wallet with tap-to-pay, wherever contactless Visa cards are accepted; the merchant receives regular money. The OOB token gives users rewards and extra benefits in the app.
oort: OORT is the token of OORT, a decentralized cloud for AI that offers data collection and labeling, storage and computing through a network of community-run nodes. OORT pays for services and rewards node operators and contributors.
op: Optimism is a Layer 2 network for Ethereum built on optimistic rollup technology, making transactions cheaper and faster. Its open-source OP Stack powers the Superchain of connected networks, including Coinbase's Base; OP is the governance token.
opal: Opal (OPAL) is a decentralized exchange for perpetual futures on Ethereum that hides orders until they are settled to protect traders from front-running bots. The project says all platform revenue is shared with OPAL holders in ETH.
open: OpenLedger (OPEN) is a blockchain for artificial intelligence where data, models, apps and agents can be monetized. It tracks how much each data provider contributes to a model's work and shares out rewards accordingly; OPEN is used for fees and incentives.
openai: OpenAI PreStocks (OPENAI) is a token on Solana issued by PreStocks that tracks the value of OpenAI's private, pre-IPO shares. It is not issued or endorsed by OpenAI and gives no shareholder rights.
opg: OpenGradient (OPG) is a decentralized network for hosting, running and verifying AI models. Model outputs are proven cryptographically, so smart contracts and apps can trust AI results; the OPG token pays for the service and rewards participants.
opn: Opinion is a prediction-market platform on BNB Chain where users bet on the outcomes of events in macroeconomics, crypto and sport. OPN is the ecosystem's utility token, used for access to services and governance.
or: L'Oréal is the world's largest cosmetics company, headquartered near Paris and founded in 1909 by chemist Eugène Schueller. It owns L'Oréal Paris, Garnier, Maybelline, Lancôme, Yves Saint Laurent Beauté, La Roche-Posay and CeraVe, selling skin, hair and makeup products.
ora: Orange is France's largest telecom operator, formerly France Télécom, headquartered in Paris. It provides mobile, home internet and TV in France, Spain, Poland, Belgium and many African countries, plus IT services for businesses through Orange Business.
orai: Oraichain is a layer-1 blockchain built with the Cosmos SDK that focuses on connecting AI with blockchains, starting as an AI-powered oracle that feeds verified data to smart contracts. ORAI pays fees, is staked to secure the network and is used for governance.
orbio: Orbio (ORBIO) is a crypto token whose holders earn OpenRouter credits, a service that gives access to many AI models. Half of the token's trading fees are converted into these AI inference credits and paid out to holders in dollars.
orbs: Orbs (ORBS) is an Israeli blockchain project founded in 2017 that works as a supporting execution layer for other networks. DeFi tools such as dLIMIT and dTWAP for decentralized exchanges are built on it; ORBS is used for staking.
orca: Orca (ORCA) is one of the first decentralized exchanges on Solana, known for its simple interface. Users swap tokens and provide liquidity in concentrated-liquidity pools called Whirlpools to earn a share of fees; ORCA is the governance token.
orcl: Oracle is an American technology company founded in 1977 by Larry Ellison. It is known for the Oracle Database, enterprise software and its Oracle Cloud Infrastructure, which builds data centers for AI; Oracle also owns Java.
order: Orderly is a layer-2 network on the OP Stack that provides a shared order book for decentralized trading across different blockchains via LayerZero. Third-party exchanges with spot and perpetual futures run on its liquidity; ORDER is the network token.
ordi: ORDI is the first token of the BRC-20 standard on the Bitcoin network, created in 2023 using the Ordinals protocol. It showed that tokens can be issued directly on Bitcoin's blockchain; it has no practical function and trades as a symbol of that trend.
ore: ORE is a digital currency on Solana that anyone can mine with an ordinary computer using proof-of-work, competing for rewards issued by the protocol. It launched in 2024 and aims to be a simple, fairly distributed store of value.
oriental-land: Oriental Land is the Japanese company that owns and operates Tokyo Disney Resort in Urayasu, Chiba, under a license from The Walt Disney Company. Founded in 1960, it runs Tokyo Disneyland and Tokyo DisneySea, the resort's hotels and the Ikspiari shopping complex, attracting tens of millions of visitors a year.
orly: O'Reilly Automotive is a US chain of auto parts stores based in Springfield, Missouri, founded in 1957. It sells parts, tools and accessories both to drivers who repair their own cars and to professional repair shops, with thousands of stores across the US, Canada and Mexico.
osak: Osaka Protocol (OSAK) is a community memecoin on Ethereum that launched by airdropping 30% of its supply to people who had sold their SHIB before Shiba Inu's big rally. Its first phase focuses on building a spread-out community.
osmo: Osmosis is the largest decentralized exchange in the Cosmos ecosystem, where dozens of independent blockchains are linked by the IBC protocol. It lets users swap tokens across chains and provide liquidity; OSMO is used for governance and staking.
otfy: Obligate Trade Finance Yield (oTFY) is a tokenized real-world asset that gives exposure to a revolving portfolio of investment-grade digital bonds. The bonds finance asset-backed physical commodity trades and are issued by a Luxembourg securitization vehicle, with Obligate as product sponsor.
otis: Otis Worldwide is the world's largest maker of elevators and escalators. The company was founded in 1853 by Elisha Otis, inventor of the safety elevator, and most of its revenue comes from servicing millions of elevators around the world.
ousd: Open USD (OUSD) is a crypto stablecoin meant to track the US dollar at a 1:1 value. It lets users keep dollar value on the blockchain and use it for transfers, trading and DeFi apps without the price swings of ordinary cryptocurrencies.
over: Overtime (OVER) is the token of Overtime, a decentralized on-chain sportsbook launched in 2021. Bets are priced and backed by its own automated market maker and liquidity pool, and results are settled through smart contracts and decentralized oracles.
ovr: OVR is the token of OVER, an augmented reality platform that divides the whole planet into hexagonal plots called OVRLands. Owners can place AR experiences on their land, and OVR is used to buy land and pay for services.
ovv: Ovintiv is a North American oil and natural gas producer headquartered in Denver, formerly the Canadian company Encana, renamed in 2020. It drills mainly in the Permian Basin, Oklahoma's Anadarko Basin and Canada's Montney region.
owb: OWB is the token of Clash of Coins, a blockchain strategy game on the Base network where players build bases, battle other players and earn in-game rewards.
oxt: Orchid is a decentralized VPN marketplace where users buy internet bandwidth from many independent providers to hide their traffic. Payments are made with the OXT token, which providers also stake to receive traffic.
oxy: Occidental Petroleum is a Houston-based oil and gas company. It produces oil and gas mainly in the US Permian Basin and the Middle East, owns the chemicals unit OxyChem and develops carbon capture technology; Berkshire Hathaway is a major shareholder.
ozo: Ozone Chain is a blockchain that presents itself as resistant to quantum-computer attacks thanks to built-in quantum cryptography technology. It lets developers build decentralized applications with low fees; OZO is the network's native coin.
p: Everpure (formerly Pure Storage) is an American company from Santa Clara that makes FlashArray and FlashBlade all-flash data storage systems running its Purity software. Its products are used in corporate data centers and AI infrastructure.
p911: Porsche AG is a German sports-car maker based in Stuttgart, founded by Ferdinand Porsche in 1931. It builds the iconic 911 as well as the Cayenne, Macan, Panamera and electric Taycan; it was listed on the stock market in 2022 and remains controlled by the Volkswagen Group and the Porsche-Piëch families.
paal: PAAL AI (PAAL) is the token of PAAL AI, a project that builds AI chatbots for crypto communities on Telegram and Discord — they answer questions, summarize news and help research tokens. PAAL runs on Ethereum and gives access to the bots and staking.
pack: HashPack is a popular crypto wallet for the Hedera network, available as a browser extension and mobile app for holding HBAR and tokens, staking and connecting to apps. PACK is the token of the HashPack ecosystem.
pact: PACT builds stablecoin infrastructure for payroll and fintech platforms: credit lines, instant stablecoin settlement that runs seven days a week, and cards that let workers spend their balance anywhere Visa is accepted. It started with early access to earned wages.
palladium: Palladium is a rare platinum-group metal that goes almost entirely into catalytic converters for petrol engines. The main producers are Russia and South Africa.
panw: Palo Alto Networks is a US cybersecurity company based in Santa Clara, California, founded in 2005. It sells next-generation firewalls, cloud security and AI-powered platforms for detecting attacks, including Prisma and Cortex.
parti: Particle Network is a layer-1 blockchain for 'chain abstraction' that unifies users and liquidity across different blockchains. Its main idea is Universal Accounts: one account and balance for all networks; PARTI is the network's token.
paxg: PAX Gold (PAXG) is a token issued by Paxos in which each coin is backed by one troy ounce of London Good Delivery gold held in professional vaults in London. Launched in 2019 and overseen by the New York regulator, it lets people own gold on Ethereum and redeem it for bars.
payai: PayAI Network (PAYAI) is a payments project on Solana for AI agents and online services. It acts as a facilitator for the x402 protocol, letting agents and apps pay each other instantly in stablecoins over the web, and PAYAI is its native token.
payx: Paychex is an American provider of payroll and HR services for small and mid-sized businesses, based in Rochester, New York, and founded in 1971 by Tom Golisano. It handles payroll and tax filing, employee benefits, retirement plans, insurance and HR software for hundreds of thousands of employers; it bought rival Paycor in 2025.
pcar: PACCAR is a US truck maker from Bellevue, Washington. It builds heavy trucks under the Kenworth and Peterbilt brands in North America and DAF in Europe, and also sells parts and provides financing.
pcg: PG&E is California's largest utility, headquartered in Oakland. It supplies electricity and natural gas to millions of customers in northern and central California and maintains a huge network of power lines.
pci: Paycoin (PCI) is a South Korean payment cryptocurrency from Danal Fintech, part of the Danal mobile payments group. Its app lets users pay with crypto at shops, restaurants and online stores across Korea.
pcock: PulseChain Peacock (PCOCK) is a meme token on PulseChain, the blockchain founded by Richard Heart. It was launched on the Pump.tires platform, inspired by community posts about a peacock, and is promoted as an unofficial mascot of the network.
pdd: PDD Holdings is a Chinese e-commerce company founded in 2015 by Colin Huang. It owns Pinduoduo, a Chinese marketplace known for group-buying discounts, and Temu, an international marketplace for low-cost goods.
peaq: peaq (PEAQ) is a blockchain for the «machine economy» that gives robots, vehicles, devices, sensors and AI agents digital identities, wallets and the ability to pay each other. DePIN projects run on it, letting people earn from their devices' data and services.
pearl: Pearl is a layer-1 blockchain built on Proof of Useful Work: mining happens as a by-product of useful AI computation on graphics cards. The same GPUs train or run AI models while also securing the network; PEARL is its native coin.
peas: Peapods Finance is a DeFi protocol where users wrap tokens into 'pods' — index-like baskets that earn fees when their price moves, an approach the team calls volatility farming. PEAS is the protocol's main token and earns a share of these fees.
peg: Public Service Enterprise Group (PSEG) is an American energy company based in Newark, New Jersey. Its utility PSE&G is New Jersey's largest supplier of electricity and natural gas to millions of homes and businesses, and the group also owns nuclear power plants at Salem and Hope Creek.
pendle: Pendle is a DeFi protocol that splits yield-bearing assets into two parts — the principal and the future yield — which can be traded separately. This lets users lock in a fixed yield or speculate on how it changes; PENDLE is the governance and rewards token.
pengu: PENGU is the official token of Pudgy Penguins, one of the best-known NFT collections of cartoon penguins. The brand has grown beyond crypto, with Pudgy Penguins toys sold in major retail stores; the token launched on Solana in late 2024.
peo: Bank Pekao is one of Poland's largest banks, headquartered in Warsaw and founded in 1929. It provides retail, business and corporate banking, asset management and brokerage across Poland; the state-controlled PZU group is a key shareholder.
people: ConstitutionDAO (PEOPLE) is the token of an online community that in November 2021 raised over $40 million in crypto to bid at Sotheby's for an original copy of the US Constitution. The auction was lost, but the token remained a symbol of the movement.
pep: PepsiCo is an American food and beverage giant based in Purchase, New York. Besides Pepsi it owns Lay's, Doritos, Cheetos, Gatorade, Quaker and 7UP (outside the US); it was formed in 1965 by the merger of Pepsi-Cola and Frito-Lay.
pep-token: Pepecoin (PEP) is a community-focused Layer 1 cryptocurrency created by one of the original 2013 Dogecoin community members to recreate that fun spirit. It uses the Scrypt algorithm, can be merge-mined with Litecoin and Dogecoin and was fairly launched with no premine or ICO.
pepe: Pepe is a meme coin on Ethereum dedicated to the famous Pepe the Frog internet meme, launched in 2023. The token has no hidden functions or transaction taxes and relies on the meme's popularity and community activity.
pepecat: PEPECAT is a community memecoin that mixes the Pepe the Frog meme with cat culture. Like most memecoins, it has no business or assets behind it, and its price depends mainly on community attention and trading.
pepecoin: PepeCoin (PEPECOIN) is a meme coin. Like most meme coins, it is not backed by a business or assets, and its price is driven mainly by community attention and trading.
pepper: PEPPER is a community meme token on the Chiliz Chain, made to reward the Chiliz community and CHZ holders. It had a fair launch with no pre-mint or ICO and a large supply distributed through airdrops and farming.
perp: Perpetual Protocol is a decentralized exchange for perpetual futures, launched in 2020, that lets users trade crypto with leverage directly from their wallets without an order book, using a virtual automated market maker. It runs mainly on the Ethereum layer-2 network Optimism; PERP is used for governance and staking.
petr4: Petrobras is Brazil's state-controlled oil company, based in Rio de Janeiro and founded in 1953. It produces oil and gas, mainly from deep-water pre-salt fields off the coast, and refines crude and sells fuel.
petrochina: PetroChina is China's largest oil and gas company, based in Beijing and created in 1999 as a subsidiary of state-owned CNPC. It produces oil and gas, refines them, owns trunk pipelines and runs a network of filling stations across the country.
pfe: Pfizer is one of the world's largest pharmaceutical companies, founded in 1849 in New York. It develops medicines and vaccines for cancer, infections and heart disease, and is known for the COVID-19 vaccine made with BioNTech and for drugs such as Viagra and Lipitor.
pfg: Principal Financial Group is a US financial company from Des Moines, Iowa, founded in 1879. It manages retirement plans and investment funds and sells life and disability insurance to individuals and employers.
pfgc: Performance Food Group is a US foodservice distributor from Richmond, Virginia. It delivers food, drinks and supplies to restaurants, schools, hospitals and convenience stores, and owns the Core-Mark convenience distribution business.
pg: Procter & Gamble is an American consumer goods maker based in Cincinnati, founded in 1837. It owns brands such as Gillette, Pampers, Tide, Ariel, Head & Shoulders, Oral-B and Fairy, and is known for decades of uninterrupted dividend increases.
pghn: Partners Group is a Swiss investment firm based in Baar near Zug, founded in 1996. It manages money for pension funds and other investors in private markets, buying stakes in companies, real estate and infrastructure outside the stock exchange.
pgr: Progressive is one of the largest car insurers in the US, headquartered in Mayfield Village, Ohio. It sells auto, motorcycle, home and business insurance online and through agents, and is known for its TV ads featuring the character Flo.
ph: Parker Hannifin is a US industrial manufacturer from Cleveland, Ohio, founded in 1917. It is a world leader in motion and control technologies: hydraulics, pneumatics, filtration, seals and components for aerospace and industry.
pha: Phala Network (PHA) is a decentralized cloud for confidential computing that uses secure processor enclaves (TEE). It lets AI agents work safely with blockchains; the PHA token is used for payments and staking.
phia: Philips is a Dutch health technology company from Amsterdam, founded in 1891 in Eindhoven as a light bulb maker. Today it makes medical imaging and patient monitoring equipment, plus electric shavers, Sonicare toothbrushes and personal care appliances.
phm: PulteGroup is one of the largest homebuilders in the US, headquartered in Atlanta and founded in 1950 by Bill Pulte. It builds houses under brands such as Pulte Homes, Centex and Del Webb, which focuses on buyers aged 55 and over.
phnix: PHNIX is a meme coin on the XRP Ledger, launched on December 3, built around the phoenix — the rising-from-the-ashes mascot used by the XRP community. It trades on the FirstLedger DEX with no transaction tax, and its liquidity pool was burned.
pi: Pi Network is a social cryptocurrency launched in 2019 by Stanford graduates. Users "mine" Pi in a mobile app with a single tap and no energy cost, and the network's open mainnet went live in February 2025.
pieverse: Pieverse is compliance-focused payment infrastructure for Web3. The protocol records transactions on-chain as verifiable receipts and timestamps (including on the x402 standard), so businesses and AI agents can settle payments transparently; it runs on BNB Chain.
pin: PinLink (PIN) is a marketplace for tokenized DePIN assets on Ethereum: it turns physical computing hardware such as GPU servers into tokens, so people can buy fractional ownership and earn a share of the rental income.
ping-an: Ping An Insurance (A shares) are shares of the Shenzhen-based Chinese financial group Ping An listed on the Shanghai exchange. Founded in 1988, the group works in life and property insurance, banking and asset management, and develops online healthcare services.
ping-an-bank: Ping An Bank is a Chinese commercial bank from Shenzhen and part of the Ping An financial group. Its predecessor, Shenzhen Development Bank, became China's first bank with publicly traded shares in 1987; today it focuses on retail and digital banking.
ping-an-insurance: Ping An is a Chinese financial group from Shenzhen, founded in 1988 by Ma Mingzhe. It is one of the world's largest insurers, covering life and property insurance, Ping An Bank, asset management, and healthcare and fintech services.
pipi: PIPI is a memecoin on Ethereum featuring Pipi, a laid-back cartoon toad in a pink Hawaiian shirt, gold chain and aviator sunglasses. It is a community token built around a relaxed, synthwave-style image.
pippin: Pippin is a meme token on Solana linked to an autonomous AI agent of the same name on X. The character, an SVG unicorn drawn with ChatGPT-4o, was created by investor and developer Yohei Nakajima, the author of the well-known BabyAGI experiment.
pit: Pitbull (PIT) is a community meme token on BNB Smart Chain, launched in 2021 during the wave of dog-themed coins. It is driven by its community and has no significant built-in utility.
pivx: PIVX is a privacy-focused cryptocurrency launched in 2016 as a fork of Dash. It runs on proof of stake, uses masternodes and a community treasury that funds development, and offers optional private transactions through its zk-SNARK-based SHIELD feature.
pixel: Pixels is a pixel-art online game about farming and exploration that runs on the Ronin network. Players grow crops, build skills and complete quests, and PIXEL is the in-game token used for purchases and governance.
pkg: Packaging Corporation of America is a US maker of containerboard and paper based in Lake Forest, Illinois. It produces linerboard and corrugated boxes for the food, industrial and logistics sectors, as well as office paper.
pkn: Orlen is Poland's largest company, a state-controlled energy group based in Płock. It runs oil refineries and petrochemical plants, a network of thousands of fuel stations in Poland, Germany, Czechia, Slovakia and Lithuania, gas production and trading after merging with PGNiG and Lotos in 2022, and power generation.
pko: PKO Bank Polski is Poland's largest bank, based in Warsaw, founded in 1919 and controlled by the state. It serves millions of individuals and businesses with accounts, cards, mortgages, loans, investment and insurance products, and is known for its popular IKO mobile banking app.
pkoin: Pocketcoin (PKOIN) is the coin of Bastyon, formerly Pocketnet, a decentralized and censorship-resistant social network that runs on its own blockchain. PKOIN is used for tips to authors, paid content, advertising and staking.
platinum: Platinum is a rare precious metal mined mostly in South Africa. Its main uses are catalytic converters for cars, jewellery and hydrogen technologies.
play: PlaysOut (PLAY) is the token of PlaysOut, a publishing platform for mini-games inside big apps and super apps. Developers integrate once to launch many small games, and host apps use them to keep users engaged and earn money.
pld: Prologis is the world's largest owner of logistics real estate, a REIT based in San Francisco. It builds and leases warehouses and distribution centers near major cities to online retailers, store chains and logistics companies.
pltr: Palantir is an American data analytics company headquartered in Denver, founded in 2003 by Peter Thiel, Alex Karp and others. Its Gotham, Foundry and AIP platforms help governments, armed forces and corporations analyze large datasets and put artificial intelligence to work.
pltr-token: Palantir Technologies • Robinhood Token is a tokenized version of Palantir shares issued by Robinhood for its customers in the European Union. It follows the price of the US-listed stock and can be traded around the clock on a blockchain.
plume: Plume (PLUME) is an Ethereum-compatible layer-1 blockchain built for tokenized real-world assets (RWA). It lets assets such as loans, bonds or commodities be issued on-chain and used in DeFi for lending and earning yield.
pm: Philip Morris International is a tobacco company based in Stamford, Connecticut, that sells Marlboro outside the United States. It is pushing smoke-free products: IQOS heated-tobacco devices and ZYN nicotine pouches.
pmt: Public Masterpiece (PMT) is a platform that links physical art with blockchain: digital certificates confirm a painting's authenticity from creation to sale. It offers collectors NFTs and tokenized artworks as real-world assets (RWA).
pnc: PNC Financial Services is one of the largest US banks, headquartered in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, with roots going back to 1845. It serves consumers and businesses with checking and savings accounts, loans, mortgages, corporate banking and asset management.
png: Pangolin (PNG) is the token of Pangolin, a decentralized exchange launched in 2021 on the Avalanche network. Users swap tokens and provide liquidity through an automated market maker, and PNG is used for governance and liquidity rewards.
pnic: Phoenic (PNIC) is a payments token on Arbitrum linked to the Miracle Chain project. It is designed for fast, low-cost digital transactions and is used across the apps of its ecosystem.
pnkstr: PunkStrategy (PNKSTR) is a token from TokenWorks whose trading fees are used to buy CryptoPunks, the famous 2017 NFT collection. The bought Punks are relisted at a higher price, and the proceeds are used to buy back and burn PNKSTR.
pnt: Pheasant Network (PNT) is a cross-chain bridge from a Japanese team that moves ETH and tokens quickly and cheaply between Ethereum layer 2 networks such as Arbitrum, Optimism and Base. PNT is the network's token.
pnut: Peanut the Squirrel (PNUT) is a meme token on Solana named after Peanut, a squirrel popular on Instagram that New York state authorities seized and euthanized in November 2024. The story went viral, and the token became a symbol of community protest.
pod: Dolphin (POD) is linked to Dolphin Network, a decentralized AI inference network where gamers and other GPU owners rent out idle graphics cards to run AI models and earn tokens. Work is checked with encryption, random validation and staked bonds.
pokt: Pocket Network is decentralized RPC infrastructure: thousands of independent nodes give apps access to data from dozens of blockchains instead of centralized providers. POKT is used to pay for requests and to stake nodes.
pol: POL is the native token of the Polygon network, which replaced MATIC in 2024. Polygon is a family of Ethereum scaling solutions popular for payments and tokenization; POL pays network fees and is staked to secure Polygon chains.
polis: Star Atlas DAO (POLIS) is the governance token of Star Atlas, a space-exploration strategy game built on Solana. POLIS holders vote on the game's direction, while ATLAS is the separate in-game currency.
pols: Polkastarter (POLS) is the token of Polkastarter, a launchpad founded in 2020 where new crypto projects run token sales (IDOs) for the public. Holding or staking POLS helps users qualify for allocations in these sales.
polyx: Polymesh (POLYX) is a layer-1 blockchain for regulated assets such as tokenized stocks and bonds, built by the Polymath team. It has built-in identity checks and compliance rules; POLYX is used for fees and staking.
pond: Marlin is a network for verifiable off-chain computing that lets apps run tasks in secure hardware enclaves (TEEs) and ZK coprocessors and prove the results on-chain. POND is staked by node operators and used to secure and pay for the network.
ponke: PONKE is a memecoin on Solana built around a cartoon monkey character known as a reckless, degenerate gambler. It has no function beyond its community, memes and trading.
pons: Pons (PONS) is the token of Pons, a launchpad for new tokens on Robinhood Chain, the blockchain network launched by the brokerage Robinhood. Projects use the platform to issue and list their tokens.
popcat: Popcat (POPCAT) is a Solana meme token inspired by the viral meme of a cat named Oatmeal that "pops" its mouth open in an O shape. It is driven purely by meme culture.
portal: Portal is a cross-chain Web3 gaming platform that aims to bring mainstream gamers into crypto. It works as a launcher and hub where players discover blockchain games across different networks; PORTAL is the ecosystem token.
porto: FC Porto Fan Token is the official fan token of FC Porto, the football club from Portugal, issued on Binance's Fan Token platform. Holders vote in club polls and get access to rewards and fan experiences.
power: Power Protocol is a rewards layer for Web3 games: players earn and spend the POWER token across partner games, and studios use it to reward their communities. The token runs on BNB Chain, Ethereum and Ronin.
powergrid: Power Grid Corporation of India is a state-owned company from Gurugram that runs most of India's inter-state power transmission lines. It builds and maintains high-voltage lines and substations and also offers telecom services over its fibre network.
powr: Powerledger is an Australian tech company founded in Perth in 2016 that builds blockchain software for decentralized energy markets. Its platform tracks and trades electricity, including solar power between neighbours, and environmental certificates; POWR is the platform access token.
ppc-token: Peercoin (PPC), launched in 2012 by the pseudonymous developer Sunny King, is one of the oldest cryptocurrencies and the first to use proof-of-stake, which secures the network with far less energy than Bitcoin-style mining. It combines proof-of-stake with proof-of-work.
ppg: PPG Industries is a US paint and coatings maker from Pittsburgh, founded in 1883. It produces coatings for cars, aircraft, industry and buildings; its brands include PPG, Glidden and Comex.
ppl: PPL Corporation is a US energy company from Allentown, Pennsylvania. Through regulated subsidiaries it delivers electricity and natural gas to millions of customers in Pennsylvania, Kentucky and Rhode Island.
pr: Permian Resources is an independent US oil and gas producer based in Midland, Texas. Formerly Centennial Resource Development, it took its current name in 2022 after merging with Colgate Energy, and drills mainly in the Delaware Basin of West Texas and New Mexico.
prcl: Parcl (PRCL) is the token of Parcl, a Solana-based platform for trading real-estate price indexes of cities such as New York or Miami. Users can bet on home prices rising or falling without buying property.
preopai: This token from the investment platform Republic tracks the value of pre-IPO shares of OpenAI, the US company behind ChatGPT. It gives economic exposure to a private company before any listing, but it is not issued by OpenAI and carries no shareholder rights.
prespcx: This token from the investment platform Republic tracks the value of pre-IPO shares of SpaceX, Elon Musk's rocket and Starlink satellite internet company. It offers economic exposure to the private company, but it is not issued by SpaceX and carries no shareholder rights.
prime: PRIME is the token of the Echelon Prime Foundation and the main currency of the Parallel ecosystem, a sci-fi trading card game on Ethereum and Base. Players use PRIME to buy and craft cards, and it powers AI-driven games built in the ecosystem.
priors: Priors Agents is an on-chain credit pool on Robinhood Chain that lends the USDG stablecoin to AI agents with ERC-8004 identities. Every loan, repayment and default is recorded on-chain and builds a public credit score from 0 to 1,000 for each agent.
prize: Prize Protocol (PRIZE) is a watch-to-earn project on Solana: users collect Gems by engaging with sponsored content and convert them into PRIZE, which is used to join giveaways. A Recycle feature also lets people swap dead tokens for PRIZE.
prl: Perle Labs is a Web3 AI platform on Solana that connects verified experts with companies and research teams to train and improve AI models. Specialists are rewarded for labeling and evaluating data, and PRL is the ecosystem token.
pro: Propy is an American blockchain platform for real-estate deals that automates buying a home, from signing the contract to recording the title. In 2017 it handled one of the first property sales recorded on a blockchain; the PRO token is used in its ecosystem.
prom: Prom (PROM) is a modular Layer 2 network built on zkEVM technology that connects different blockchains, both Ethereum-compatible and not. The project grew out of the Prometeus platform; PROM is used to pay fees and for staking.
prompt: Wayfinder is a non-custodial AI agent for crypto trading: from a single chat you can trade spot on EVM chains and Solana, futures on Hyperliquid and Polymarket markets. The PROMPT token powers the ecosystem.
propc: Propchain is a Swiss-based blockchain platform for real estate that tokenizes property, letting investors buy fractional digital shares of buildings and helping owners and funds manage and raise capital on-chain. The PROPC token is used for access, fees and rewards on the platform.
props: Propbase (PROPS) is the token of Propbase, a real estate tokenization marketplace on the Aptos blockchain. It lets people buy fractions of rental properties with small amounts and receive their share of rental income.
pros: Pharos (PROS) is an Ethereum-compatible layer-1 blockchain built for payments and tokenized real-world assets. The network is designed for very high throughput, and PROS is its native token.
prove: Succinct (PROVE) is a decentralized network of provers that generates zero-knowledge proofs for blockchains and apps. The team built the SP1 zkVM, and the PROVE token is used to pay for proofs and for staking.
pru: Prudential Financial is one of the largest US life insurers, based in Newark, New Jersey, and founded in 1875; its Rock of Gibraltar logo is widely known. It sells life insurance, annuities and retirement plans and runs the investment manager PGIM; it is a separate company from the UK's Prudential plc.
prx: Prosus is a Dutch internet investment group based in Amsterdam, spun off from South Africa's Naspers in 2019. It owns a large stake in China's Tencent and runs online businesses such as OLX classifieds, iFood food delivery and PayU payments.
pry: Prysmian is an Italian cable maker from Milan and the largest in the world in its industry. It produces power cables, including high-voltage subsea cables for offshore wind farms, plus telecom and fiber-optic cables under the Prysmian, Draka and General Cable brands.
psa: Public Storage is the largest self-storage operator in the US, a REIT based in Glendale, California, and founded in 1972. It rents storage units and lockers to individuals and businesses at thousands of locations.
psg: Paris Saint-Germain Fan Token (PSG) is the fan token of French football club PSG on the Socios.com platform on the Chiliz network. It lets supporters vote in club polls and take part in giveaways and fan promotions.
pst: Poste Italiane is Italy's national postal operator, based in Rome and controlled by the state, with roots going back to 1862. Besides letters and parcels it is one of the country's largest financial groups, offering BancoPosta savings and payments, PostePay cards and life insurance through Poste Vita in thousands of post offices.
psx: Phillips 66 is a US energy company from Houston, spun off from ConocoPhillips in 2012. It refines crude oil, runs pipelines, makes chemicals through the Chevron Phillips joint venture and sells fuel at Phillips 66, 76 and Conoco stations.
ptc: PTC is an American software company based in Boston, founded in 1985 as Parametric Technology. It makes software for engineers and manufacturers: Creo and Onshape for 3D design, Windchill for product lifecycle management, and ThingWorx for the industrial internet of things.
ptgc: The Grays Currency (PTGC) is a DAO token on PulseChain. Holders collect rewards simply by holding, stakers earn more with no lock-up, the top 100 stakers can create proposals and all stakers vote; the project focuses on buying and burning liquidity tokens.
ptt: PTT is Thailand's state-owned oil and gas company from Bangkok, founded in 1978. It runs gas pipelines and gas processing, exploration and production (through PTTEP), refining and petrochemicals; PTT gas stations belong to its unit PTT Oil and Retail.
pttep: PTT Exploration and Production (PTTEP) is Thailand's national oil and gas exploration and production company, based in Bangkok and founded in 1985 as a subsidiary of the state energy group PTT. It finds and produces oil and natural gas in Thailand, Southeast Asia and other regions.
puffer: Puffer is a decentralized Ethereum platform that combines restaking with rollup-based solutions. Users receive the liquid token pufETH in place of staked ETH, while PUFFER is used for voting in the protocol.
pump: PUMP is the token of Pump.fun, a Solana platform that since 2024 lets anyone launch their own meme coin in about a minute. Pump.fun became one of the main venues of the meme coin boom, and part of its revenue goes to buying back PUMP.
pumpcade: PUMPCADE is the token of Pumpcade, a platform for fast, real-time prediction markets embedded in livestreams. Streamers can show markets as an overlay, viewers predict right from the stream chat, and markets settle automatically.
pundix: Pundi X is a project from Indonesia that built crypto point-of-sale terminals for paying in shops. Today it is developing the Pundi AI blockchain ecosystem for data and AI; PUNDIX is the project's token.
puppies: I love puppies (PUPPIES) is a meme coin. Like most meme coins, it is not backed by a business or assets, and its price is driven mainly by community attention and trading.
pups: PUPS (Pups) is a memecoin on the Bitcoin blockchain, issued with the Runes protocol that lets tokens live directly on Bitcoin. It grew from a dog-themed community and has no business behind it.
purpe: Purple Pepe (PURPE) is a memecoin built around a purple version of the Pepe the Frog meme. Like most memecoins, it has no business or assets behind it, and its price depends mainly on community attention and trading.
purr: Purr (PURR) is a cat-themed memecoin, the first spot token on the Hyperliquid network, launched without a sale. Half of the supply was distributed to Hyperliquid users; the token has no planned utility and exists as a community symbol.
pwr: Quanta Services is a US infrastructure contractor based in Houston. It designs, builds and maintains power lines, substations, renewable energy connections, gas pipelines and communications networks for utilities and other industries across North America and abroad.
px: Not Pixel (PX) is the token of Not Pixel, a Telegram mini-app game from the team behind Notcoin in which players paint a huge shared pixel canvas together. The PX token was issued on The Open Network (TON).
pybobo: Capybobo is a Web3 art toy project built around a capybara character. Its ecosystem combines a GameFi game, NFTs linked to blind boxes and physical collectible figures, and the PYBOBO token is used in games and rewards.
pypl: PayPal is a US online payments company from San Jose, California, founded in 1998; its founders include Peter Thiel and Elon Musk. It owns the PayPal wallet, the Venmo app and the Braintree payment platform.
pyth: Pyth Network is a decentralized oracle network that delivers real-time prices of stocks, crypto, currencies and commodities to blockchains. The data comes directly from exchanges and trading firms; PYTH is the network's governance token.
pyusd: PayPal USD (PYUSD) is a dollar-pegged stablecoin launched by PayPal in August 2023 and issued by Paxos. It is backed by dollar deposits and short-term US Treasuries, runs on Ethereum and Solana, and can be bought, sent and used for payments inside PayPal and Venmo in the US.
pzu: PZU (Powszechny Zakład Ubezpieczeń) is Poland's largest insurer, based in Warsaw, with roots going back to 1803. Controlled by the state, it sells life and non-life insurance and pensions in Poland and the Baltics and owns large stakes in Bank Pekao and Alior Bank.
q: Qnity Electronics is a US company spun off from DuPont in 2025. It makes materials for producing semiconductors and electronics, such as wafer-polishing chemicals, photoresists and materials for circuit boards and chip packaging.
q-token: Quack AI (Q) is a project building a governance layer for the AI agent economy, where agents, users and apps interact under verifiable rules. It supports sign-to-pay, gasless payments across blockchains based on the x402 standard; Q is the ecosystem token.
qait: QAIT is the token of the SEALCOIN ecosystem, issued and governed by the QAIT Association, a Swiss non-profit. It serves as a settlement mechanism for machine-to-machine and AI agent transactions, letting connected devices, robots and autonomous agents exchange data and pay each other without intermediaries.
qanx: QANplatform is a hybrid blockchain designed to resist attacks from quantum computers. It lets developers write smart contracts in any programming language and deploy both public and private networks; QANX is the native token.
qbe: QBE Insurance is an Australian insurer from Sydney, founded in 1886. It insures businesses and individuals, covering property, liability and agriculture, in Australia, North America and Europe.
qcad: QCAD is a stablecoin pegged 1:1 to the Canadian dollar, issued by Stablecorp, a Toronto-based company. Each token is backed by Canadian dollar reserves, and it is used for payments and trading on blockchains such as Ethereum.
qcom: Qualcomm is a US chip designer from San Diego, founded in 1985. It makes Snapdragon processors and modems for smartphones, cars and PCs, and earns licensing fees on its patents for 3G, 4G and 5G wireless technology.
qi: BENQI is a DeFi protocol on Avalanche for lending and borrowing crypto, and it also offers sAVAX liquid staking for AVAX. Depositors earn interest from borrowers; QI is the governance token.
qie: QIE Blockchain is an Ethereum-compatible layer-1 blockchain that positions itself as a digital identity layer for Web3. The network offers fast, cheap transactions, its own wallet and a decentralized exchange; QIE pays fees and validator staking.
qka: Qkacoin (QKA) is a meme coin dedicated to the quokka, the small smiling marsupial from islands off Western Australia such as Rottnest Island. The project rests on its community and the image of "the happiest animal in the world".
qkc: QuarkChain is a scalable sharded blockchain launched in 2018 by a team led by Qi Zhou. The network is split into many parallel shard chains for high throughput; QKC is its native coin.
qnt: Quant is a London-based company founded by Gilbert Verdian whose Overledger technology connects different blockchains with each other and with banking systems. The QNT token is needed to access the platform and pay for licences for developers and businesses.
qqq: Invesco QQQ is an ETF that tracks the Nasdaq-100, the 100 largest non-financial companies listed on Nasdaq. Tech giants such as Apple, Microsoft, Nvidia and Amazon dominate it.
qqq-token: This is a Robinhood stock token that tracks Invesco QQQ, the ETF that follows the Nasdaq-100 index of the largest non-financial companies on Nasdaq. Robinhood launched such tokens in 2025 for customers in the European Union, letting them get US stock exposure on-chain around the clock.
qqqm: Invesco Nasdaq 100 (QQQM) tracks the same Nasdaq-100 index as QQQ but with a lower annual fee, aimed at long-term investors.
qrl: Quantum Resistant Ledger (QRL) is a blockchain launched in 2018 and secured by XMSS signatures that resist attacks from future quantum computers. Its core idea is to keep funds safe even once quantum machines can break today's usual cryptography.
qtc: Quantus (QTC) is the coin of Quantus Network, a proof-of-work Layer 1 blockchain built on Substrate and designed to resist attacks from future quantum computers. It uses NIST-approved post-quantum cryptography such as ML-DSA (Dilithium) signatures.
qtum: Qtum (QTUM) is a Singapore-based blockchain launched in 2017 that combines Bitcoin's UTXO transaction model with Ethereum-style smart contracts. It runs on proof of stake, so QTUM holders earn rewards for helping secure the network.
quai: Quai Network is a proof-of-work blockchain made of many connected chains (shards) that are merge-mined together, so it can scale to high transaction speeds. It uses a consensus called Proof-of-Entropy-Minima and has two tokens: QUAI and the Qi payment token.
quanta-computer: Quanta Computer is a Taiwanese company from Taoyuan, founded in 1988 by Barry Lam. It is one of the world's largest contract manufacturers of laptops for major brands and also builds servers for cloud and AI data centers.
qubic: Qubic (QUBIC) is a layer-1 blockchain founded by Sergey Ivancheglo, a co-founder of IOTA. It offers fee-free transactions and «useful» mining, where miners' computing power goes toward training artificial intelligence.
quid: Squid is a cross-chain protocol that lets users swap and move tokens between more than a hundred blockchains in one click, without manual bridges. It aggregates liquidity from many DEXs and is built on the Axelar network; QUID is the project's token.
raca: Radio Caca (RACA) started as a community memecoin and grew into a metaverse project known for the Metamon NFT game and the USM virtual world. RACA is used to buy NFTs, items and land within its ecosystem on BNB Chain and Ethereum.
race: Ferrari is the legendary Italian sports-car maker from Maranello, founded by Enzo Ferrari in 1947. It builds a limited number of expensive supercars and runs Scuderia Ferrari, the most successful team in Formula 1 history.
