umia: Umia is an on-chain venture protocol: founders launch a token and raise money in an open auction, the funds sit in an on-chain treasury the team cannot spend alone, and token holders steer the treasury through decision markets.
umxm: Manadia (UMXM) is a Web3 infrastructure project that combines AI collaboration with privacy-preserving computation. It aims to provide verifiable data settlement and private value transfer between on-chain and off-chain systems, for uses such as finance and asset digitization.
unh: UnitedHealth Group is the largest health insurance company in the United States, based in Minnetonka, Minnesota. It has two parts: UnitedHealthcare sells health insurance, while Optum runs clinics, pharmacy benefits, health data and software for hospitals.
uni: UNI is the governance token of Uniswap, the largest decentralised exchange (DEX) on Ethereum, launched in 2018 by Hayden Adams. Uniswap lets people swap tokens straight from their wallet via liquidity pools, and UNI holders vote on protocol changes.
unp: Union Pacific is the largest US railroad by track length, headquartered in Omaha, Nebraska, and founded in 1862. It hauls coal, grain, chemicals, cars and containers across a network of tens of thousands of kilometres of track in the western United States.
unp-token: Unipoly (UNP) is a GameFi project launched in October 2023 that is building a decentralized entertainment platform mixing games with real-estate-themed elements. The UNP token serves as the currency of its ecosystem.
up: Unitas (UP) is a yield-bearing stablecoin protocol from Unipay: its dollar token earns income through delta-neutral arbitrage strategies, including ones built on JLP on Solana. The UP token is tied to the protocol's governance and incentives.
upc: UPCX is an open-source payment system running on its own fast blockchain built for payments and financial services. It offers a wallet app for transfers and settlements, and UPC is the network's native coin.
ups: United Parcel Service (UPS) is a US package delivery and logistics giant based in Atlanta, founded in 1907 in Seattle. Its brown trucks and own airline deliver parcels in more than 200 countries, and it also offers freight, supply-chain and healthcare logistics.
uqc: Uquid Coin (UQC) is an Ethereum token linked to the Uquid online store, where shoppers can buy goods, gift cards and mobile top-ups with cryptocurrency. UQC gives discounts and is used within that ecosystem.
ura: Global X Uranium (URA) invests in uranium miners and companies in the nuclear power supply chain.
uri: United Rentals is the world's largest equipment rental company, founded in 1997 in Stamford, Connecticut. It rents out excavators, aerial lifts, generators, tools and other equipment to builders, factories and utilities in the US and Canada.
us: Talus is an AI infrastructure network that gives autonomous AI agents an on-chain layer to run on. Its Nexus protocol lets agents carry out verifiable tasks and workflows on the blockchain, and the US token powers the network.
usb: U.S. Bancorp is the parent of U.S. Bank, one of the largest banks in the United States, headquartered in Minneapolis. It offers checking and savings accounts, mortgages, credit cards, business loans, payment processing and wealth management.
usd0: Usual USD (USD0) is a dollar stablecoin from Usual, a Paris-founded DeFi protocol launched in 2024. It is backed one-to-one by tokenized short-term US Treasury bills, and the protocol's USUAL token gives holders a share of its revenue and governance.
usd1: USD1 is a dollar-pegged stablecoin launched in 2025 by World Liberty Financial, a crypto project linked to the Trump family. Its reserves are held in short-term US Treasuries, dollar deposits and cash equivalents, with custody by BitGo, and it runs on Ethereum and BNB Chain.
usdc: USDC is a dollar-pegged stablecoin issued by Circle, a US fintech company, launched in 2018 together with Coinbase. Each token is backed by cash and short-term US Treasuries held at regulated institutions, and it is used for payments, trading and DeFi on Ethereum, Solana and other networks.
usdd: USDD is a dollar-pegged stablecoin of the Tron ecosystem, launched in 2022 and associated with Tron founder Justin Sun. It is over-collateralized with crypto reserves such as TRX and other stablecoins, runs mainly on the TRON network and is used in its DeFi apps.
usde: Ethena USDe (USDE) is a synthetic dollar from Ethena Labs, launched in 2024. Instead of bank deposits it holds crypto such as ETH and BTC and offsets their price moves with short futures positions; staked USDe (sUSDe) earns the funding and staking income.
usdf: Falcon USD (USDF) is a synthetic dollar from Falcon Finance, a project backed by DWF Labs. Users mint it by depositing stablecoins, bitcoin, ether and other assets worth more than the USDF they receive; staking it as sUSDf earns yield from market-neutral trading strategies.
usdg: Global Dollar (USDG) is a dollar-pegged stablecoin issued by Paxos from Singapore under the city's stablecoin rules, launched in 2024. It belongs to the Global Dollar Network, whose members such as Robinhood and Kraken share the reserve income, and it runs on Ethereum and Solana.
usdgo: USDGO is a stablecoin designed to keep a 1:1 value with the US dollar. Like other dollar stablecoins, it is used to hold dollar value on the blockchain, move money between exchanges and wallets, and pay or trade without converting back to a bank account.
usds: USDS is the dollar-pegged stablecoin of Sky, the protocol formerly known as MakerDAO, launched in 2024 as the upgraded successor to DAI. DAI can be swapped for USDS one-to-one, and holders can deposit it to earn the Sky Savings Rate.
usdt: Tether (USDT) is the largest stablecoin, a token designed to stay equal to one US dollar. Issued by Tether since 2014 and backed mainly by cash and US Treasury bills, it runs on Tron, Ethereum and many other networks and is widely used for trading and transfers.
useless: Useless Coin (USELESS) is a Solana memecoin launched in 2025 that openly presents itself as a "useless" token with no function at all. The whole idea is irony about crypto speculation, and its price depends only on community demand.
usg: USG is an over-collateralized dollar stablecoin issued by Tangent Finance on Ethereum. Users borrow USG against yield-bearing collateral such as boosted Curve LP tokens and keep most of the underlying yield, while sUSG shares protocol revenue with savers.
uso: United States Oil Fund • Robinhood Token is a tokenized version of United States Oil Fund (USO) shares issued by Robinhood for its customers in the European Union. It follows the price of the US-listed stock and can be traded around the clock on a blockchain.
usual: Usual is a DeFi protocol that issues the USD0 stablecoin, backed by tokenized US Treasury bonds and other real-world assets. The USUAL token gives holders governance rights and a share of the protocol's revenue.
usualx: USUALx is the staked form of USUAL, the governance token of Usual, the protocol that issues the USD0 dollar stablecoin backed by tokenized US Treasury bills. Holders lock USUAL to receive USUALx and a share of the protocol's rewards.
utya: Utya is a memecoin on the TON blockchain inspired by the popular Utya duck stickers in Telegram. It has no function beyond its community and the fame of the yellow duck character among Telegram users.
v: Visa is a San Francisco-based US payments company that runs the world's largest card payment network. It does not issue cards or lend money itself: banks issue Visa cards, and Visa earns a fee for processing each transaction.
val-token: Validity (VAL) is a cryptocurrency that began life as Radium (RADS), one of the early proof-of-stake coins. The project rebranded to Validity and develops tools for running and checking decentralised apps and smart contracts.
vale3: Vale is a Brazilian mining company from Rio de Janeiro, founded in 1942 as a state company. It is one of the world's largest producers of iron ore and nickel, also mines copper and owns its own railways and ports.
vana: Vana is a blockchain network where users can own their data and pool it into 'DataDAOs' to train AI models and earn rewards. VANA is used for transaction fees, staking and data access.
vanry: Vanar (VANRY) is the coin of Vanar Chain, a layer-1 blockchain aimed at entertainment, gaming, brands and AI applications. It grew out of the Virtua project, whose TVK token was swapped into VANRY.
vanta: Vanta Network (VANTA) is Subnet 8 on Bittensor, a decentralized network where quantitative and machine-learning models compete to produce trading signals for forex, stocks and crypto. Contributors are scored and rewarded on risk-adjusted performance.
var: Variational (VAR) is the token of Variational, a peer-to-peer protocol for trading crypto derivatives on Arbitrum. Its app Omni offers perpetual futures on many coins without trading fees for users.
vara: Vara Network is a layer-1 blockchain built on Gear Protocol, a framework based on Polkadot's Substrate technology. It runs WebAssembly smart contracts that communicate through messages, aiming at fast, parallel apps such as games and DeFi; VARA pays for fees and staking.
vatreni: Vatreni is the fan token of the Croatian Football Federation, named after the nickname of Croatia's national team, "Vatreni" ("the Blazers"). Holders vote in fan polls and get access to exclusive rewards.
vcb: Vietcombank (Joint Stock Commercial Bank for Foreign Trade of Vietnam) is one of Vietnam's largest banks, based in Hanoi and founded in 1963. Majority-owned by the state, it is a leader in foreign trade finance, payments and retail banking.
vchf: VNX Swiss Franc (VCHF) is a stablecoin pegged 1:1 to the Swiss franc, issued by VNX, a tokenization company based in Liechtenstein. It lets users hold and transfer francs on blockchains such as Ethereum.
vea: Vanguard FTSE Developed Markets (VEA) invests in companies from developed countries outside the US, mainly Europe, Japan, Canada and Australia.
veev: Veeva Systems is a California company founded in 2007. It builds cloud software for pharmaceutical and biotech companies: CRM for working with doctors and systems for clinical trials, quality and drug registration.
velo: Velo (VELO) is the token of Velo Labs, a protocol for cross-border money transfers and settlement focused on Southeast Asia. It runs on the Stellar and BNB Chain blockchains and uses VELO as collateral to issue digital credit between partners in its network.
velvet: Velvet Capital (VELVET) is a non-custodial terminal for social crypto trading: spot, perpetual futures and yield strategies on Solana, Base, BNB Chain, Ethereum, Hyperliquid and other networks. Users can copy other traders' trades, and VELVET is the platform token.
verem: Verified Emeralds (VEREM) is a real-world asset project in which each token is backed by GIA-certified emeralds held in audited storage. It operates under ADGM regulatory rules in Abu Dhabi and links the gemstone market with DeFi.
verona: Verona is the new name of XION, a layer-1 blockchain from Burnt Labs built on Cosmos technology. It positions itself as an intelligence and verification layer for AI, letting AI agents act on verified real-world information; VERONA is the network's token.
verse: Verse World (VERSE) is the token of a virtual-reality company that is building an open digital world, playable on PC through the Epic Games Store or in VR. VERSE is the currency of the in-game economy.
vet: VeChain is a business-focused, Ethereum-compatible blockchain for supply-chain tracking, proving where goods come from and sustainability reporting. It uses two tokens: VET stores value, while the VTHO gas it generates pays for transactions.
vfy: zkVerify (VFY) is the token of zkVerify, a blockchain built by Horizen Labs specifically to verify zero-knowledge proofs quickly and cheaply for other chains and apps. VFY pays verification fees and is staked to secure the network.
vgt: Vanguard Information Technology (VGT) is an ETF covering the US tech sector: software, chips and hardware companies of all sizes.
vic: Vingroup is Vietnam's largest private conglomerate, founded by Pham Nhat Vuong. It grew out of a business in Kharkiv, Ukraine, where Mivina instant noodles were first made in 1993; today it owns Vinhomes, carmaker VinFast, Vinpearl resorts and Vinmec hospitals.
vici: VICI Properties is a US real estate investment trust (REIT) spun off from Caesars Entertainment in 2017. It owns casinos and resorts, including Caesars Palace and the Venetian in Las Vegas, plus entertainment venues, which it rents out on long-term leases.
vie: Veolia is a French company from Paris and a world leader in water, waste and energy services. It supplies drinking water, treats wastewater, and collects and recycles waste, including hazardous waste, for cities and industry around the world.
vig: Vanguard Dividend Appreciation (VIG) invests in US companies that have raised their dividends for at least 10 years in a row.
vin: VulgarTycoon (VIN) is a BEP-20 DeFi token on BNB Chain linked to the YFSX token across several liquidity pools. The community-governed project pays dividends on transactions and burns part of each trade.
vine: Vine is a meme coin on Solana launched in 2025 by Rus Yusupov, co-founder of the Vine video app. It pays tribute to the legendary six-second video platform that Twitter shut down and trades as a meme token.
virtual: Virtuals Protocol is a platform launched on Base in 2024 where users create, tokenize and monetize AI agents, including virtual characters and game bots. VIRTUAL is the base token that individual agent tokens are paired and traded against.
vivt3: Telefônica Brasil, known by its Vivo brand, is Brazil's largest telecom operator, based in São Paulo and part of Spain's Telefónica group. It provides mobile service, fiber broadband, pay TV and digital services to homes and businesses.
vlo: Valero Energy is the largest independent oil refiner in the US, based in San Antonio, Texas. It turns crude into gasoline, diesel and jet fuel at refineries in the US, Canada and the UK, and also makes ethanol and renewable diesel.
vlto: Veralto is a US company spun off from Danaher in 2023. It makes equipment to test and treat water, under brands such as Hach and Trojan, and marking, coding and packaging-design solutions such as Videojet used by utilities and manufacturers.
vmc: Vulcan Materials, based in Birmingham, Alabama, is the largest US producer of construction aggregates — crushed stone, sand and gravel. It also supplies asphalt and ready-mixed concrete for roads, bridges and buildings from hundreds of quarries.
vmrk: Vivmark Residential is a Chicago-based US real estate investment trust (REIT) that builds, buys and manages high-quality rental apartment communities in major US metro areas. It earns its income mainly from residents' rent.
vnq: Vanguard Real Estate (VNQ) invests in US REITs — companies that own property such as offices, warehouses and apartments and pay out most of the rental income.
vnxau: VNX Gold (VNXAU) is a gold-backed token issued by VNX, a tokenization company from Liechtenstein. Each token is backed by physical gold stored in a vault in Liechtenstein, so its price follows the price of gold.
voo: Vanguard S&P 500 (VOO) tracks the S&P 500 index of 500 large US companies with one of the lowest fees available. It is a popular choice for regular long-term investing.
vooi: VOOI is a non-custodial perpetual DEX aggregator: one app that connects to several decentralized exchanges for perpetual futures across different blockchains and routes each trade to the best venue. VOOI is the project's token; users keep control of their own wallets.
vow: Vow is a crypto project that aims to decentralize the issuance of money: businesses and communities can create their own currency tokens backed by VOW for loyalty programs and payments. The VOW token is the base of this system.
vow3: Volkswagen is Europe's largest carmaker, based in Wolfsburg, Germany, and founded in 1937. Its group brands include Volkswagen, Audi, Porsche, Škoda, SEAT and Cupra, Lamborghini, Bentley and Ducati motorcycles, and its Traton unit makes Scania and MAN trucks; this listing is the preferred share.
vr: Victoria VR (VR) is an open-source platform that turns text prompts into 3D content and virtual worlds using AI. The project started as a VR metaverse, and the VR token is used across its ecosystem.
vra: Verasity (VRA) is the token of Verasity, a video technology company whose Proof of View system detects fake views and ad fraud in online video. VRA is used in its ad tech, video rewards and esports products.
vrsk: Verisk Analytics is a US data analytics company from Jersey City, founded in 1971 as an insurers' organisation. It sells insurance companies databases, catastrophe risk models and software for pricing policies and assessing claims.
vrsn: Verisign is a US internet company from Virginia, founded in 1995. It runs the registries for the .com and .net domains and two of the thirteen DNS root servers, keeping the addresses of millions of websites working.
vrt: Vertiv is a US maker of data-centre infrastructure based in Ohio and a former unit of Emerson Electric. It supplies uninterruptible power systems, cooling (including liquid cooling for AI servers), racks and monitoring software for data centres and telecom networks.
vrtx: Vertex Pharmaceuticals is a US biotech company based in Boston, founded in 1989. It is best known for cystic fibrosis medicines such as Trikafta and also develops treatments for sickle cell disease, pain and kidney diseases, including the gene therapy Casgevy.
vsn: Vision (VSN) is the Web3 ecosystem token of Bitpanda, the European crypto and investing platform from Vienna. It powers the Bitpanda DeFi wallet, the Vision Chain layer-2 network and a launchpad; holders get fee discounts, staking rewards and voting rights.
vst: Vistra is one of the largest power companies in the United States, based in Irving, Texas. It generates electricity from nuclear plants such as Comanche Peak, natural gas, coal, solar and batteries, and sells power directly to millions of homes and businesses through retail brands like TXU Energy.
vstr: Vestra DAO (VSTR) is a decentralized autonomous organization in the SocialFi niche that mixes social engagement with DeFi: members vote on governance, stake VSTR and earn rewards for activity.
vt: Vanguard Total World Stock (VT) is a single fund for the whole world's stock market: thousands of companies from the US, Europe, Asia and emerging markets.
vtho: VeThor (VTHO) is the gas token of the VeChainThor blockchain, used to pay transaction fees. Holders of the main coin VET receive VTHO automatically, which keeps fees separate from VET's price; the network is used for supply-chain tracking and proving where goods come from.
vti: Vanguard Total Stock Market (VTI) holds the entire US stock market in one fund — thousands of companies from giants to small caps — at a very low fee.
vtr: Ventas is a US real estate investment trust (REIT) from Chicago. It owns senior housing, medical office buildings, hospitals and research campuses in the US, Canada and the UK and earns rental income from them.
vtrs: Viatris is a pharmaceutical company formed in 2020 by merging Mylan with Pfizer's Upjohn unit. It sells generic medicines and well-known branded drugs such as Lipitor and Viagra in more than 165 countries.
vug: Vanguard Growth (VUG) invests in large US growth companies — firms expected to grow faster than average, mostly in technology.
vvs: VVS Finance (VVS) is a decentralized exchange with an automated market maker on Cronos, the network linked to Crypto.com. Users swap tokens, provide liquidity and stake VVS to earn rewards.
vvv: VVV is the token of Venice, a private generative AI service founded by crypto entrepreneur Erik Voorhees. Venice gives access to open-source language models, image and code generation without storing user prompts; staking VVV unlocks API access for developers and AI agents.
vwo: Vanguard FTSE Emerging Markets (VWO) invests in companies from emerging markets such as China, India, Taiwan and Brazil.
vxus: Vanguard Total International Stock (VXUS) invests in companies outside the United States — Europe, Japan, China and other emerging markets — in one low-cost fund.
vylr: Vylor is a US seed and plant genetics company headquartered in Johnston, Iowa, with a history going back to 1802. It breeds seeds for farm crops and develops biotechnology and gene editing for farmers.
vym: Vanguard High Dividend Yield (VYM) invests in US companies whose dividend yield is above the market average.
vz: Verizon is one of the largest US telecom operators, headquartered in New York. It provides mobile service, Fios home internet and business services; the company was formed in 2000 from parts of the former Bell system.
w: Wormhole (W) is a cross-chain protocol for passing messages and tokens between dozens of blockchains, including Ethereum and Solana. The network is verified by a group of independent «Guardian» nodes; W is used for protocol governance.
wab: Wabtec (Westinghouse Air Brake Technologies) is a US rail equipment maker from Pittsburgh whose roots go back to 1869 and George Westinghouse's air brake. It makes locomotives, brakes, train control systems and parts for freight and passenger trains.
wai: World3 (WAI) is a Web3 platform for creating and running autonomous AI agents without writing code: agents can act on-chain, manage tasks and interact in games and apps. WAI is used for payments, staking and governance.
wal: Walrus (WAL) is a decentralized storage network for large files, created by Mysten Labs, the team behind the Sui blockchain. It stores video, images and AI data reliably and cheaply; WAL pays for storage and is staked by node operators.
wallet: Ambire Wallet is a self-custody smart-account crypto wallet for Ethereum and other EVM networks. It offers features such as paying gas fees in stablecoins, batching transactions and account recovery, and WALLET is its governance and rewards token.
walmex: Walmart de México (Walmex) is Mexico's largest retailer and is controlled by the US company Walmart. It runs Walmart hypermarkets, Bodega Aurrerá discount stores and Sam's Club warehouse stores in Mexico and Central America.
wan: Wanchain (WAN) is a blockchain launched in 2018 that focuses on interoperability: its decentralized bridges move tokens between networks such as Bitcoin, Ethereum and many others. WAN pays fees and is staked to secure the network.
wanhua-chemical: Wanhua Chemical is a Chinese chemical company from Yantai, Shandong province, and one of the world's largest producers of MDI, the raw material for polyurethanes used in insulation, furniture foam and footwear. In 2011 it bought Hungary's BorsodChem.
wat: Waters Corporation is a US scientific instruments company based in Milford, Massachusetts. It makes liquid chromatography and mass spectrometry systems, software and lab supplies used by pharmaceutical, food and environmental labs, and thermal analysis instruments under the TA brand.
waves: Waves is a blockchain platform founded in 2016 by Alexander Ivanov for issuing tokens and building decentralized applications. It was one of the first networks where anyone could easily create their own token; WAVES is its native coin.
waxp: WAX (Worldwide Asset eXchange) is a blockchain for NFTs and games, founded in 2017 by OPSkins co-founder William Quigley. It hosts games such as Alien Worlds and Topps digital card collections; WAXP is used for staking and paying for network resources.
wbc: Westpac is Australia's oldest bank, founded in Sydney in 1817 as the Bank of New South Wales. It serves households and businesses in Australia and New Zealand and owns the St.George and BankSA brands.
wbrl: WBRL is a stablecoin designed to track the Brazilian real, so that one token equals one real. It lets people and companies hold and send Brazil's currency on a blockchain, for payments, trading and DeFi.
wbt: WhiteBIT Coin (WBT) is the native token of WhiteBIT, a crypto exchange founded in Ukraine in 2018. WBT gives trading-fee discounts, access to staking and other exchange services, and is used on its own WB Network blockchain.
wcn: Waste Connections is a North American waste management company with head offices in Ontario and Texas. It collects household and industrial waste and runs landfills and transfer and recycling stations, mainly in smaller cities and suburbs of the US and Canada.
wct: WalletConnect is an open protocol that connects crypto wallets to decentralized apps, usually by scanning a QR code. It is supported by hundreds of wallets and thousands of apps; WCT is used for staking, rewards and network governance.
wday: Workday is a US company from Pleasanton, California, founded in 2005 by David Duffield and Aneel Bhusri. It sells cloud software for managing the staff, payroll and finances of large companies.
wdc: Western Digital is a US data storage maker from California, founded in 1970. It produces hard disk drives, including high-capacity HDDs for cloud data centers; in 2025 it spun off its flash memory business as Sandisk.
wds: Woodside Energy is Australia's largest independent oil and gas company, based in Perth and founded in 1954. It is best known for liquefied natural gas (LNG) projects such as the North West Shelf, Pluto and Scarborough off Western Australia, and it became a global producer after merging with BHP's petroleum business in 2022.
wec: WEC Energy Group is an American utility holding company based in Milwaukee, Wisconsin. Through companies such as We Energies, Wisconsin Public Service and Peoples Gas in Chicago it supplies regulated electricity and natural gas to millions of customers in Wisconsin, Illinois, Michigan and Minnesota, and it owns a large stake in American Transmission Co.
wecan: Wecan is a blockchain project that tokenizes data so it can be audited, time-stamped and shared securely. Records stored this way cannot be quietly altered, and contributors can be rewarded with the WECAN token.
wege3: WEG is a Brazilian maker of electrical equipment based in Jaraguá do Sul, founded in 1961. It is one of the world's largest producers of electric motors and also makes generators, transformers, drives and equipment for renewable energy.
well: Welltower is a US real estate investment trust (REIT) based in Ohio. It owns senior housing, medical office buildings and care facilities in the United States, Canada and the United Kingdom and earns money from rent and property management.
well-token: Moonwell (WELL) is the token of Moonwell, an open lending and borrowing protocol running mainly on Base and Optimism. Users supply crypto to earn interest or borrow against it; WELL is used for governance and staking.
wemix: WEMIX is the blockchain and token of South Korean game publisher Wemade, known for the Legend of Mir series. The platform brings together blockchain games, NFTs and DeFi services; WEMIX serves as in-game currency and pays network fees.
wen: Wen (WEN) is a Solana memecoin launched in January 2024 as a fair launch through Jupiter, inspired by the poem 'A Love Letter to Wen Bros'. It was widely airdropped to Solana users and has no utility beyond trading and community.
wes: Wesfarmers is an Australian conglomerate based in Perth, founded in 1914 as a farmers' cooperative. It owns the Bunnings home-improvement chain, Kmart and Officeworks, as well as chemicals and pharmaceutical businesses.
wet: HumidiFi is a decentralized exchange on Solana that runs its own proprietary market-making engine (a 'prop AMM') instead of public liquidity pools, quoting tight prices mostly through DEX aggregators. WET is the project's token.
wfc: Wells Fargo is one of the largest US banks, headquartered in San Francisco and founded in 1852. It serves millions of people and businesses with accounts, cards, mortgages, business loans and wealth management; its symbol is a stagecoach.
wfi: WFI is the token of WeFi, an on-chain banking platform built around stablecoins. Users deposit regular money, receive stablecoins 1:1 and see one account with a single balance, while payments can run over bank rails or the blockchain.
wheat: Wheat is one of the world's staple grains and the raw material for bread and flour. Its price is driven by harvests in the US, Russia, the EU and Ukraine, and by the weather.
whuf: Ethos is an on-chain reputation protocol on Base, an Ethereum layer 2. Users build verifiable trust through vouches (staking tokens on another person) and reviews, and the resulting reputation score is visible to any app.
wif: dogwifhat (WIF) is a memecoin on Solana whose mascot is a Shiba Inu dog wearing a pink knitted hat. Launched at the end of 2023, it became one of the best-known Solana memecoins; the token has no practical use, and its value rests on the community.
wild: Wilder World is a metaverse built with Unreal Engine on Ethereum, centered on a virtual city called Wiami where land, cars and avatars are NFTs. The WILD token is used for purchases, staking and governance in this world.
win: WINkLink (WIN) is an oracle in the TRON ecosystem that feeds real-world data, such as asset prices and random numbers, into smart contracts. The project grew out of the WINk gaming platform; WIN is used to pay for data and for staking.
wings: Wingbits (WINGS) is a decentralized physical infrastructure (DePIN) network for flight tracking. Community members run ADS-B receivers that pick up aircraft signals, the data feeds a global flight-tracking service, and contributors earn WINGS rewards.
win界: WIN界 is a Chinese-language meme coin on BNB Chain, launched through the Flap launchpad. It has no product of its own: its value rests on community interest and trading.
wipro: Wipro is an Indian IT services company based in Bengaluru, founded in 1945 as a vegetable-oil maker. Today it provides software development, consulting, cloud and cybersecurity services to clients worldwide; Azim Premji led it for decades.
wkc: Wiki Cat (WKC) is a BNB Chain meme token with a cat mascot, conceived as an educational project to introduce people to cryptocurrencies. It relies on community activity and has no product of its own.
wkl: Wolters Kluwer is a Dutch information services and software company based in Alphen aan den Rijn. It supplies professionals with expert tools: the UpToDate clinical reference for doctors, tax and accounting software such as CCH, legal research databases and compliance solutions.
wld: Worldcoin (World) is a project by Tools for Humanity, co-founded by OpenAI chief Sam Altman. Its Orb device scans the iris to confirm that a user is a unique human rather than a bot; WLD is the ecosystem's token.
wlfi: World Liberty Financial is a decentralized finance crypto project linked to Donald Trump's family. It issues the USD1 stablecoin, and the WLFI token gives holders the right to vote on how the platform develops.
wm: Waste Management is the largest waste collection and recycling company in North America, based in Houston. It picks up trash from homes and businesses, runs landfills and recycling plants, and generates energy from landfill gas.
wmb: The Williams Companies is a US energy infrastructure company based in Tulsa, Oklahoma, founded in 1908. It owns natural gas pipelines, including Transco, the largest interstate gas pipeline in the US, plus gas gathering and processing facilities.
wmt: Walmart is the world's largest retailer by revenue, founded in 1962 by Sam Walton in Arkansas. It runs Walmart supercenters, Sam's Club warehouse stores and an online store, and also operates in Mexico, Canada, India (Flipkart) and other countries.
wmtx: World Mobile is a decentralized mobile and internet network project that started in Africa, on Zanzibar. Local node operators build out the network and earn rewards, while WMTX is used for staking and payments on the network.
wod: World of Dypians (WOD) is a multiplayer online role-playing game and metaverse built by the Dypius team, with Web3 features on BNB Chain and other networks. Players explore an open world, complete quests and events and own in-game items as NFTs; WOD is the game's token.
wojak: Wojak (WOJAK) is an Ethereum meme token inspired by the Wojak internet meme, also known as Feels Guy, the simple drawn face used to express emotions online. It has no utility beyond its community and trades as a memecoin.
wolf: LandWolf (WOLF) is a memecoin based on Landwolf, a character from Matt Furie's comic «Boy's Club», the same comic that gave the world Pepe the Frog. It has no product behind it: its value comes from meme culture and the community.
woo: WOO is the token of the WOO ecosystem, which includes the centralized exchange WOO X and the decentralized exchange WOOFi. It gives trading-fee discounts, a share of revenue through staking, and voting rights.
wow: Woolworths Group is Australia's largest supermarket chain, based in Sydney and founded in 1924. It runs Woolworths supermarkets in Australia and Woolworths (formerly Countdown) in New Zealand, as well as the Big W discount stores.
wpay: WPAY is the token of Wirex Pay, a payments network built on Polygon zk technology by Wirex, the company known for its crypto debit cards. The network aims to link blockchain payments with traditional card settlement.
wpm: Wheaton Precious Metals is a Vancouver-based streaming company. It finances mining companies in exchange for the right to buy part of their silver, gold or palladium output at a fixed low price, without running any mines itself.
wrb: W. R. Berkley is a US insurance holding company from Connecticut, founded in 1967 by William Berkley. Through dozens of specialised units it insures businesses for property, liability and workers' compensation, and also writes reinsurance.
wrx: WRX is the token of WazirX, a cryptocurrency exchange in India founded in Mumbai in 2018 that became one of the country's best-known crypto platforms. WRX was used for trading-fee discounts on the exchange, which suffered a major hack in 2024.
wsm: Williams-Sonoma is an American home furnishings retailer from San Francisco, founded in 1956 by Chuck Williams. It owns the Williams Sonoma (cookware and kitchen), Pottery Barn and West Elm (furniture and decor) brands and makes most of its sales online.
wst: West Pharmaceutical Services is a US company from Pennsylvania, founded in 1923. It makes rubber stoppers, seals, syringe components and delivery systems that drug makers use to package and give injectable medicines and vaccines.
wstar: Wanted Star (WSTAR) is an Ethereum meme token built around a star-shaped internet character with a playful "wanted poster" look. It exists for entertainment and community memes and does not give any ownership or claim on revenue.
wti: WTI is the US benchmark grade of crude oil, priced in New York. Its price moves with OPEC+ decisions, US output, inventories and global demand.
wtw: Willis Towers Watson (WTW) is a British-American advisory and insurance brokerage company formed in 2016 by the merger of Willis Group and Towers Watson. It helps companies buy insurance and manage risks, pension plans and employee benefits.
wuliangye: Wuliangye Yibin is a Chinese maker of baijiu, the strong grain liquor, based in Yibin in Sichuan province and controlled by the local government. Its flagship Wuliangye spirit is distilled from five grains — sorghum, rice, glutinous rice, wheat and corn — and is one of China's best-known premium liquor brands after Kweichow Moutai.
wuxi-biologics: WuXi Biologics is a Chinese company from Wuxi that develops and manufactures biological medicines such as antibodies, vaccines and protein drugs for pharmaceutical clients. It was spun out of the WuXi AppTec group and has sites in China, Ireland, Germany and the US.
xai: SideShift (XAI) is a service for swapping cryptocurrencies quickly without signing up or leaving funds on the platform, supporting dozens of coins across many networks. Holders who stake the XAI token receive a share of the platform's profit.
xan: Anoma is a decentralized "operating system" for Web3 that lets developers write one app that works on any blockchain. Builders focus on product logic instead of the infrastructure of individual networks; XAN is the project's token.
xaum: Matrixdock Gold (XAUM) is a tokenised gold product from Matrixdock, the real-world-asset platform of crypto financial firm Matrixport. Each token represents one troy ounce of LBMA-standard gold bullion held in vaults and can be redeemed for physical gold.
xaut: Tether Gold (XAUT) is a token from Tether in which each coin represents ownership of one troy ounce of physical gold stored in a vault in Switzerland. It lets people hold and move gold on Ethereum and other networks, and holders can redeem it for the metal.
xava: Avalaunch is a launchpad on the Avalanche network that helps new projects prepare for launch and sell tokens with fair, broad distribution. XAVA is its token: users stake it to qualify for allocations in new token sales.
xcat: PUMPSTOP (XCAT) is a community memecoin on Solana with a tabby cat mascot, created as a protest against unfair token launches dominated by insiders and snipers. It was fair-launched on Xtrends with built-in staking, token locking and sniper protection.
xch: Chia (XCH) is a blockchain founded by Bram Cohen, the inventor of BitTorrent. Instead of energy-hungry mining it uses a proof of space and time consensus based on free disk space, and its smart transactions are written in the Chialisp language.
xcn: Onyxcoin (XCN) is the token of Onyx Protocol, a project that grew out of the Chain blockchain platform and develops its own Onyx network for financial applications. XCN is used for protocol governance, staking and paying network fees.
xdc: XDC Network is a hybrid blockchain from XinFin focused on international trade and trade finance, such as tokenizing invoices, letters of credit and other documents. It runs on delegated Proof of Stake; XDC pays fees and is staked by node operators.
xdp: Doppler Finance is a yield protocol for XRP on the XRP Ledger that lets XRP holders earn on their coins through institutional-grade strategies. XDP is the protocol token.
xec: eCash (XEC) is a cryptocurrency for everyday payments that emerged in November 2020 as a split from Bitcoin Cash. It is developed by the Bitcoin ABC team led by Amaury Séchet; the network combines mining with Avalanche-based fast finality.
xef: Xeffy is a crypto project building a hybrid real-world-asset (RWA) platform that combines institutional-style multi-strategy yield vaults with on-chain infrastructure for tokenised assets. XEF is the platform's token.
xel: Xcel Energy is a US utility from Minneapolis. It supplies electricity and natural gas to millions of customers in eight Midwestern and Western states and is one of the country's leaders in wind power.
xem: NEM (XEM) is a blockchain launched in 2015 that introduced the Proof-of-Importance consensus, which rewards accounts by activity as well as holdings. It offered built-in features for tokens and messaging; its successor network is Symbol (XYM).
xen: XEN Crypto is a token launched in 2022 by Jack Levin, an early Google employee, that anyone can mint for free by locking in a term and paying only the network fee — a model it calls proof of participation. It started on Ethereum and was later deployed on many other EVM networks.
xeris: XerisCoin is the token of the Xeris blockchain project, which is building its own network with a patent-pending "triple consensus" design and plans to tokenize real estate. For now the coin trades on Solana ahead of the main network launch.
xgz: GoldZip (XGZ) is a gold-backed token issued in Singapore by GoldZip Digital, part of the Hong Kong Gold Exchange group. Each token is backed by 1 gram of 99.99% pure gold held in approved vaults, and holders can redeem it for gold bars.
xiaomi: Xiaomi is a Chinese tech company from Beijing, founded in 2010 by Lei Jun. It makes Xiaomi, Redmi and POCO smartphones, TVs, home appliances and smart home devices, and since 2024 electric cars such as the SU7 sedan.
xion: XION, rebranded as Verona, is a layer-1 blockchain from Burnt Labs built on Cosmos technology, first known for making crypto apps work without wallets, seed phrases or gas fees. It now positions itself as a verification layer that lets AI act on proven real-world data; XION is its token.
xle: Energy Select Sector SPDR (XLE) is an ETF on the oil and gas companies of the S&P 500, such as ExxonMobil and Chevron.
xlf: Financial Select Sector SPDR (XLF) is an ETF on the financial sector of the S&P 500: banks, insurers and payment companies.
xlk: Technology Select Sector SPDR (XLK) is an ETF holding the technology companies that belong to the S&P 500 index.
xlm: Stellar is an open network for fast, cheap money transfers and for issuing digital assets such as stablecoins. It was founded in 2014 by Jed McCaleb and Joyce Kim and is developed by the non-profit Stellar Development Foundation.
xlv: Health Care Select Sector SPDR (XLV) is an ETF on the healthcare companies of the S&P 500: drugmakers, medical devices and health insurers.
xmr: Monero is a cryptocurrency launched in 2014 with privacy switched on by default. Ring signatures and stealth addresses hide the sender, receiver and amount, making it one of the most anonymous coins.
xno: Nano (XNO) is a cryptocurrency for fast, fee-free payments, launched in 2015 under the name RaiBlocks. It uses a block-lattice structure in which every account has its own chain of blocks, so transfers confirm within seconds.
xny: Codatta is a decentralized protocol for labelling and verifying the data used to train AI. Contributors add and validate data and earn a share of its later use; XNY is the protocol token.
xom: ExxonMobil is one of the world's largest oil and gas companies, headquartered in Texas and formed in 1999 by the merger of Exxon and Mobil. It produces oil and gas and refines them into fuels, lubricants (the Mobil 1 brand) and chemicals.
xp: Xphere is a blockchain with a dual architecture: a main PBFT chain for fast transaction processing and a supporting proof-of-work chain for security. This way the project tries to combine scalability, security and decentralization; XP is the network's native coin.
xpin: XPIN Network is a decentralized wireless network platform that uses blockchain to link users' connection points into a global network. Participants earn XPIN tokens for providing coverage and connectivity to others.
xpl: Plasma is a layer-1 blockchain built specifically for stablecoins, above all USDT, with fee-free transfers for users. The network is Ethereum-compatible and aimed at payments and financial services; XPL is used for staking and network security.
xpr: XPR Network (XPR), formerly Proton, is a layer-1 blockchain for payments and smart contracts launched in San Francisco on EOSIO technology. It offers fee-free transfers and readable account names instead of long addresses; the WebAuth wallet and the Metal X exchange run on it.
xrd: Radix (XRD) is a layer-1 blockchain built specifically for decentralized finance. It has its own smart contract language, Scrypto, where tokens are native resources, reducing the risk of bugs and hacks; XRD is used for fees and staking.
xrp: XRP is the native coin of the XRP Ledger, launched in 2012 for fast and cheap international payments. The company Ripple uses XRP in products for banks and payment providers.
xsgd: XSGD is a Singapore dollar stablecoin issued by StraitsX, a payments company in Singapore. Each token is backed one-to-one by Singapore dollar reserves and is used for payments, trading and transfers on several blockchains.
xt: XT is the token of the crypto exchange XT.com, founded in 2018. It is used for trading-fee discounts and on XT Smart Chain, an energy-efficient public blockchain with smart-contract support.
xter: Xterio (XTER) is the token of Xterio, a Web3 game publisher and platform that develops and distributes games, including AI-powered titles. XTER is used across its games and platform for purchases, rewards and governance.
xtm: Minotari (XTM) is the coin of Tari, an open-source, privacy-focused blockchain for digital assets led by former Monero lead maintainer Riccardo Spagni. It is mined with proof-of-work, partly merge-mined with Monero, and aims to make creating and owning digital assets simple.
xtz: Tezos is a blockchain for smart contracts and tokens, founded by Arthur and Kathleen Breitman, with its mainnet live since 2018. Its key feature is self-amendment: XTZ holders vote on protocol changes, and the network upgrades itself without hard forks.
xu3o8: xU3O8 is a token from the Uranium.io platform that gives on-chain exposure to physical uranium: each token represents a set amount of U3O8 uranium oxide held in a licensed storage facility. It lets people trade uranium without buying it through traditional commodity channels.
xvg: Verge (XVG) is a privacy-focused cryptocurrency launched in 2014 under the name DogecoinDark. It can hide users' IP addresses through Tor and I2P and uses several mining algorithms.
xvs: Venus (XVS) is the largest lending protocol on BNB Chain, launched in 2020. Users deposit crypto to earn interest or borrow against collateral, and can also mint the VAI stablecoin; XVS is the protocol's governance token.
xyl: Xylem is an American water technology company headquartered in Washington, D.C., spun off from ITT in 2011. It makes pumps, water meters and equipment for treating, testing and moving water for utilities, industry and buildings, under brands such as Flygt and Sensus.
xyo: XYO Network (XYO) is a project founded in San Diego in 2018 that collects and verifies real-world data, such as geolocation, and passes it to blockchains, AI and business systems. Nodes in the network are rewarded in XYO tokens.
xyz: Block (formerly Square) is a US fintech company founded in 2009 by Twitter co-founder Jack Dorsey. It runs Square payment terminals and software for businesses, the Cash App money app, the Afterpay buy-now-pay-later service and bitcoin products.
yb: Yield Basis is a DeFi protocol from Curve founder Michael Egorov that lets users earn from providing bitcoin liquidity without so-called impermanent loss. YB is the token for governance and revenue sharing.
yee: Yee Token (YEE) is a community meme coin built around Yee the dinosaur, an old internet meme. Its story plays on a joking rivalry with Pepe the Frog, claiming Pepe stole Yee's launch plan.
yfi: yearn.finance (YFI) is a DeFi protocol on Ethereum created in 2020 by Andre Cronje that automatically moves users' funds between lending protocols for better yield. The YFI token launched with no sale to the team or investors and is used for governance.
yfsx: YFSX is a community-governed DeFi token on BNB Chain with a very small fixed supply of 19,900 tokens. Holders take part in governance, and liquidity providers share in the ecosystem it links with the VIN token.
ygg: Yield Guild Games is a decentralized guild of Web3 gamers founded in 2020 in the Philippines. It helps players access in-game NFTs and earn in blockchain games, and it also publishes its own games; YGG is used for governance.
yld5on: YLD5on is a token from Ondo Finance that tracks the Ondo 5 Targeted Income portfolio: preferred shares, covered-call ETFs, corporate, government and securitized bonds and REITs, aiming for about 5% yield with dividends reinvested.
yum: Yum! Brands is an American restaurant company based in Louisville, Kentucky, that owns KFC, Pizza Hut, Taco Bell and The Habit Burger Grill. Spun off from PepsiCo in 1997, it is one of the world's largest restaurant groups, with almost all of its outlets run by franchisees.
zama: Zama is a Paris-based cryptography company that develops open-source solutions based on fully homomorphic encryption (FHE), a technology that lets data be processed without decrypting it. Its protocol brings confidential smart contracts to public blockchains; ZAMA is the protocol's token.
zano: Zano (ZANO) is a privacy-focused layer-1 cryptocurrency launched in 2019. Transactions hide the sender, receiver and amount by default; the network also lets users issue their own confidential tokens and trade on a built-in exchange.
zarp: ZARP is a stablecoin pegged 1:1 to the South African rand and backed by rand reserves. It lets people and businesses hold and send rand on blockchains, for example to move money in and out of crypto in South Africa.
zaru: ZAR Universal (ZARU) is a stablecoin pegged 1:1 to the South African rand, issued by BlockTower South Africa, a provider licensed by the FSCA. Each token is backed by rand reserves held in segregated accounts at Standard Bank, and it runs on Solana, Ethereum, Base and other chains.
zbcn: Zebec Network is a blockchain payments platform best known for real-time payroll, where salary streams to employees second by second. It also offers on-chain payout infrastructure and crypto cards; the project started on Solana, and ZBCN is its ecosystem token for governance and staking.
zbh: Zimmer Biomet is a US medical device maker based in Warsaw, Indiana, founded in 1927. It is best known for artificial knee and hip joints, and also makes sports-medicine, trauma and face/skull implants plus the ROSA surgical robot.
zbt: ZEROBASE is a decentralized cryptographic network for verifiable off-chain computation using zero-knowledge proofs (ZK) and trusted execution environments (TEE). It powers zkStaking, zkLogin and ProofYield for institutional DeFi.
zcat: Anonymous Cat (ZCAT) is a Solana meme token launched through StonkFun. A 3% tax on every transfer is used to buy Zcash (ZEC), which is automatically distributed to ZCAT holders in proportion to their tokens, with no staking or wallet connection needed.
zchf: Frankencoin (ZCHF) is a decentralised stablecoin on Ethereum that tracks the Swiss franc. It is minted by users who lock crypto collateral, with no company behind it as issuer; the separate FPS token is used to govern and backstop the system.
zec: Zcash is a privacy cryptocurrency launched in 2016. It uses zero-knowledge proofs (zk-SNARKs) that can fully encrypt the sender, receiver and amount; users choose between transparent and shielded transfers.
zen: Horizen (ZEN) is a privacy-focused project that began in 2017 as a fork of Zcash. It builds a modular platform that makes privacy technology such as zero-knowledge proofs easy for applications to use; ZEN is its native token.
zent: Zentry (formerly GuildFi) is a project building a platform that combines AI and crypto: it turns everyday user activity into structured data to train AI agents, and users share in the value. ZENT is the ecosystem token.
zeph: Zephyr Protocol (ZEPH) is the reserve coin of Zephyr, a privacy-focused stablecoin protocol on its own blockchain. ZEPH backs the ZSD private stable dollar in an over-collateralized reserve, and transactions are private by default.
zerebro: Zerebro is an autonomous AI agent that creates, distributes and analyses content on social media and decentralized platforms by itself. It works without human control, writing posts, music and art; ZEREBRO is the project's token on Solana.
zest: Zest Protocol is a bitcoin lending protocol on the Stacks network. BTC holders can lend their bitcoin for interest or borrow against it as collateral; ZEST is the protocol's token.
zeta: ZetaChain (ZETA) is a layer-1 blockchain launched in 2024 to connect Ethereum, Bitcoin, Solana and other networks. The team also develops ZetaLabs, a private AI app, and ZETA gives access to the service, payment discounts and voting rights.
zeus: Zeus Network is a protocol that connects Bitcoin to Solana, letting BTC be used in Solana DeFi apps without a centralised middleman, notably through the zBTC token. ZEUS is used for node staking and paying for network services.
zfi: Zyfai (ZFI) is a decentralized finance project that uses AI agents to manage users' stablecoins, automatically moving them between DeFi protocols in search of better yield. ZFI is the project's token.
zig: ZIG Finance (ZIG) is an on-chain finance ecosystem that aims to make institutional-grade investment products available to everyone. ZIG Chain provides the infrastructure, ZIG Markets handles distribution, and ZIG is the ecosystem's native asset.
zijin-mining: Zijin Mining is a Chinese mining group from Fujian province and one of the world's largest gold and copper producers. It runs mines in China, Serbia, DR Congo, South America and other countries, and also mines zinc and lithium.
zil: Zilliqa is a layer-1 blockchain founded in Singapore in 2017 and one of the first to use sharding for scaling. It supports smart contracts in the Scilla language, and ZIL is used for fees and staking.
zk: ZKsync (ZK) is an Ethereum layer-2 network built by Matter Labs that uses zero-knowledge proofs to make transactions faster and cheaper. Other projects use its ZK Stack technology to build their own chains; ZK is the governance token.
zkc: Boundless is a protocol from the RISC Zero team that brings verifiable zero-knowledge (ZK) computing to any blockchain. Developers request proofs and independent provers compete to generate them, earning ZKC, which is also staked to secure the network.
zkj: Polyhedra Network builds zero-knowledge proof infrastructure, including zkBridge for moving assets and messages between blockchains and the Expander proof system for verifiable computing and AI. The ZKJ token is used for fees, staking and governance in its ecosystem.
zkp: zkPass is a decentralised oracle that turns private data from any HTTPS website into verifiable zero-knowledge proofs. This lets someone prove, for example, their age or bank balance without revealing the data itself; ZKP is the network token.
zora: Zora is an on-chain social network and creator platform on the Base network where every post can become its own token ("creator coins"). The project started as an NFT marketplace and protocol for artists; ZORA is the ecosystem token.
zrc: Zircuit is a layer-2 rollup for Ethereum that adds sequencer-level security: the network checks transactions for malicious activity before including them. It is built by a team with a background in smart-contract auditing; ZRC is its governance token.
zro: LayerZero is an interoperability protocol that lets smart contracts on different blockchains exchange messages and tokens without classic bridges. Hundreds of apps and stablecoins use it; ZRO is the governance token. Its co-founder is Bryan Pellegrino.
zrx: 0x Protocol (ZRX) is an open protocol for swapping tokens on Ethereum and other chains, launched in 2017. Its API and liquidity aggregator are built into many wallets and apps, including Matcha; ZRX is the protocol's governance token.
zs: Zscaler is an American cybersecurity company from San Jose, founded in 2007 by Jay Chaudhry. Its cloud platform secures employees' access to the internet and corporate apps using a zero-trust approach.
ztc: ZenChain is a layer-1 blockchain that is Bitcoin-native and EVM-compatible, designed to connect the Bitcoin and Ethereum ecosystems. It lets bitcoin and Ethereum-based assets work together in smart contracts; ZTC is the network token.
zts: Zoetis is the world's largest animal health company, spun off from Pfizer in 2013 and headquartered in New Jersey. It makes vaccines, medicines and diagnostics for pets and farm animals; well-known products include Apoquel and Simparica.
zurn: Zurich Insurance Group is a Swiss insurer based in Zurich, founded in 1872. It covers property, cars, businesses and lives of customers in more than 200 countries, and in the US also works through Farmers.
zylo: Zylo is an economic layer that combines games, tournaments, services and financial tools into one progression system. A user's actions across different apps build up in a shared economy, and the ZYLO token is its currency.
zzz: ZZZ is a meme coin on Robinhood Chain whose name comes from a viral story about AI agents that started adding "ZZZ" to their wiki edits to push them to the bottom of the review queue. It has no product of its own.
哈基米: 哈基米 (Hajimi) is a meme coin on BNB Chain. Like most meme coins, it is not backed by a business or assets, and its price is driven mainly by community attention and trading.
我踏马来了: 我踏马来了 is a meme coin on BNB Chain. Like most meme coins, it is not backed by a business or assets, and its price is driven mainly by community attention and trading.
犇犇牛: 犇犇牛 (BenBen Bull) is a Chinese-language meme coin on BNB Chain with a bull theme, launched through the Flap launchpad. It has no product of its own: its value rests on community interest and trading.
蝴蝶人生: 蝴蝶人生 ("Butterfly Life") is a Chinese-language meme coin on BNB Chain, launched through the Flap launchpad. It has no product of its own: its value rests on community interest and trading.
金蝶圣甲: 金蝶圣甲 (Golden Butterfly Sacred Armor) is a Chinese-community memecoin on BNB Chain, built around a 'dung beetle' community theme. It charges a 3% tax on every buy and sell, and its value rests on community promotion.
龙虾: 龙虾 (Lobster) is a meme coin. Like most meme coins, it is not backed by a business or assets, and its price is driven mainly by community attention and trading.
